Creating a Color Matte works, but the layer is always created as a grey matte. There is no dialog to choose a color during creation, and double-clicking the Color Matte in the Project panel does not open any color picker or edit dialog. The matte appears to be stuck as grey and cannot be changed.

title: Hardware acceleration: GPU/media-engine decode, GPU effects and GPU export
author: echelon
body:
## Problem

A user on Linux with an AMD GPU reports that preview and rendering barely touch the GPU while CPU usage spikes. The same is true on macOS and Windows. FilmCraft does use the GPU today, but only for the last step of preview:

| Stage | Where it runs today |
|---|---|
| Video decode (H.264, HEVC, VP9, AV1, ProRes, DNx) | **CPU**, pure-Rust software decoders |
| Preview compositing (scale, position, opacity, YUV→RGB, dissolves) | GPU (`filmcraft-gpu`, wgpu/WGSL) |
| Effects, non-Normal blend modes, adjustment layers, nested sequences, most transitions | **CPU**: rendered per layer, then handed to the GPU as an image |
| Export rendering | **CPU** (`render::render_sequence`); the GPU compositor isn't used |
| Export encoding (H.264, ProRes, …) | **CPU**, pure-Rust encoders |

Measured (docs/performance.md): playing 4K HEVC costs about **90 CPU-ms per displayed frame, and the decoder alone accounts for 82–87 ms**. That's 2–3 cores fully busy at 24 fps while the GPU only draws the final quad. Effects and export add more CPU on top.

## Goal

On machines that support it, preview and export should use the GPU and the OS's hardware media engines (VA-API / Vulkan Video, VideoToolbox, Media Foundation / D3D11). The pure-Rust paths stay as the reference and the fallback, so FilmCraft keeps working, with identical output, everywhere else.

Principles:
- **Auto by default, always fallible.** Hardware is tried first where supported. Any error (unsupported profile, driver failure, lost device) falls back to the software path for that clip without failing the edit or the export.
- **Same picture.** Hardware output is tested against the pure-Rust decoder and the CPU compositor within a tolerance, in the same way as the existing CPU/GPU compositor parity tests.
- **Visible.** Settings ▸ Playback / Export ▸ *Hardware acceleration: Auto / Off*, plus `perf.stats` counters for frames decoded or encoded in hardware vs software and GPU vs CPU layers, so you can see what's happen…

title: Engine: explicit flag for commands that accept named targets instead of a selection
author: echelon
body:
#52 lets a command run without a selection when its parameters name the targets. Which commands qualify is decided by substring-matching the parameter doc (`"clips":[id]`, `"item":id`), which is brittle. A command that documents `clips` but reads only the selection would pass the enabled check and then act on nothing; that's a no-op or an error, not a crash.

Proposal: an explicit `named_targets` flag (or the set of keys) on `CommandSpec`, plus a test that every flagged command really reads those keys.

title: Hardening: two overflow/recursion paths on hostile input (MP4 edit list, subclip chains)
author: echelon
body:
Found while reviewing #42 and #50. Neither PR introduced them.

- `crates/codecs/src/mp4.rs` (~line 362): `self.audio_offset * src_rate as i64` can overflow on a hostile edit list. Use `saturating_mul` or i128.
- `crates/engine/src/lib.rs` (~line 865): `media_duration` recurses through the subclip parent chain with no bound, so a cyclic or very deep chain in a hostile project file can overflow the stack. Bound it at 16 like `source_size` / `final_source_size` (#43).

Each fix needs a regression test that fails before it (AGENTS.md §0).

title: Media: one open file descriptor per source (fd limit on large projects)
author: echelon
body:
#41 (MEM1) keeps a file open per media source and reads it with positional reads, which is a good memory win. But a project with hundreds of media items can hit the soft descriptor limit (256 by default on macOS, 1024 on Linux). Opening then fails with `MediaError::Io`, and the media show as failed or offline.

Options:
- an LRU of open readers that reopens on demand;
- raising the soft limit at startup (`setrlimit`, via `crates/platform` since it's FFI).

Either needs a test with more sources than the limit.

title: WebM: every third frame dropped at 30 fps (video lookup floors the time against 1 ms-rounded timestamps)
author: Biromedic
body:
## Summary

With a 30 fps WebM (VP9) source, every third frame is skipped and the previous frame is shown twice in its place. A 30 fps export from such a clip only has 20 unique frames per second, and motion judders. The VP9 decoder itself is fine; the wrong source frame is being picked.

## Environment

- FilmCraft web build **v0.2.1** (`filmcraft-web-0.2.1.zip`, build `feee775cbf5d6f17`) in a Chromium-based browser on Windows 11, WebGPU backend
- Loaded with `?nowebcodecs`. Per `docs/web.md`, WebM isn't decoded with WebCodecs anyway.
- `crates/codecs/src/mkv.rs` hasn't changed since 6aa3c3734 (2026-10-04), so v0.2.1 and current `main` have the same code. I only tested the web build, but the code involved isn't web-specific.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Get a 30 fps WebM with 1 ms timestamps, e.g. Big Buck Bunny 1080p 10 s VP9 from test-videos.co.uk: `https://test-videos.co.uk/vids/bigbuckbunny/webm/vp9/1080/Big_Buck_Bunny_1080_10s_5MB.webm`
2. Import it, create a sequence from the clip, and export 5.0–5.3 s as a PNG sequence. With the browser API:

```js
const { items } = await filmcraft.importUrl("/Big_Buck_Bunny_1080_10s_5MB.webm");
const { sequence } = await filmcraft.execute("file.newSequence", { fromItem: items[0] });
await filmcraft.execute("file.exportMedia", { format: "png", path: "/exports/f.png", sequence,
  range: "custom", startSeconds: 5.0, endSeconds: 5.3, wait: true });
```

3. Compare the PNGs with the source frames (I decoded them with ffmpeg 7.1 / PyAV).

## Result

Each exported PNG matches exactly one source frame (PSNR 58.7 dB, i.e. a bit-exact decode plus RGB rounding), but not always the right one:

| Exported frame | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Expected source frame | 150 | 151 | 152 | 153 | 154 | 155 | 156 | 157 | 158 |
| Actual source frame | 150 | 151 | **151** | 153 | 154 | **154** | 156 | 157 | **157** |

title: H.264 export: ffmpeg -ec 0 flags 119/120 frames "corrupt decoded frame" (h264enc tests hide it with -v error)
author: Biromedic
body:
## Summary

A 1080p60 H.264 export plays fine and decodes to the right pictures. But with error concealment off (`ffmpeg -ec 0`), ffmpeg 7.1 reports `corrupt decoded frame` for 119 of the 120 frames. The README says exports decode cleanly in ffmpeg with error concealment off. The `h264enc` tests don't see this because they run ffmpeg at `-v error`, and that message is a warning.

## Environment

- FilmCraft web build **v0.2.1** (`filmcraft-web-0.2.1.zip`, build `feee775cbf5d6f17`) in a Chromium-based browser on Windows 11, WebGPU backend. Loaded with `?nowebcodecs`, which only affects how the source is decoded.
- ffmpeg 7.1 (gyan.dev essentials build) and PyAV 15.1.
- I only tested the web build's exporter. I expect the desktop / CLI export to behave the same, but I didn't check.

1. Source: Big Buck Bunny 1080p60 H.264 10 s from test-videos.co.uk: `https://test-videos.co.uk/vids/bigbuckbunny/mp4/h264/1080/Big_Buck_Bunny_1080_10s_5MB.mp4`

```js

The "Everywhere" section of `README.md` says "every crate up to the engine compiles to `wasm32`; the browser front end is next." The repository already contains the browser app (`apps/filmcraft-web`, documented in `docs/web.md`), and every release from v0.1.0 through v0.2.1 attaches a `filmcraft-web-<version>.zip`. The README also contradicts itself: its tagline says FilmCraft runs "in the browser via WebAssembly". Readers of the "Everywhere" section are told the browser front end is still to come and get no pointer to the web app or `docs/web.md`. The line is still present on `main`, and the same README ships inside the v0.2.1 release zips.

- Source: `main` at `771b614ad4c3fbefda5d668ce4384504b8c13f6d` (2026-10-06).

title: fix(web): window.filmcraft readFile, importUrl and openProject reject with plain strings instead of Error objects
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

In the browser build, some `window.filmcraft` promise members reject with a plain string instead of an `Error`, while `execute`, `request` and the other control-channel members reject with an `Error`. `readFile` on a missing path, `importUrl` and `openProject` on a URL that returns an HTTP error, and `openProject` given neither a `File` nor a URL all reject with a string, so `e.message` is `undefined` and `e instanceof Error` is `false`. `openProject` is inconsistent with itself: a damaged project file rejects with an `Error`, a missing project URL rejects with a string. Agent and test code that does `catch (e) { report(e.message) }`, the usual pattern for the other members, loses the failure reason on these paths.

## Runtime or environment

- FilmCraft web build v0.2.1, release asset `filmcraft-web-0.2.1.zip` (SHA-256 `f496c41f65e3f38b32b05b92c27940c5f464b442573b617e69923df0f085005c`, matching the release's `SHA256SUMS.txt`), served from `127.0.0.1` with `python3 -m http.server`.
- Driven by Playwright 1.63.0 with its Chromium 153.0.8010.12 (headless), on macOS 27.0 arm64, page opened with `?webgl`.
- Source: `main` at commit 771b614ad4c3fbefda5d668ce4384504b8c13f6d. `git diff v0.2.1 main -- apps/filmcraft-web docs/web.md` is empty, so the web crate and its docs are unchanged since the release; only the release build was run.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Unzip the v0.2.1 web release asset and serve its folder on localhost, for example `python3 -m http.server 8731 --bind 127.0.0.1`.
2. Open `http://127.0.0.1:8731/?webgl` and wait until `await filmcraft.commands()` resolves.

title: fix(control): bridge `file.exportMedia` with `wait: true` reports `timeout` after 60 s while the export succeeds
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

When the desktop app is driven over the control channel (`filmcraft --control <port>`), a `file.exportMedia` call with `wait: true` whose encode takes longer than 60 seconds returns the error `timeout`, but the app keeps encoding and later writes a complete, valid file. `filmcraft-cli --bridge … exec` exits with status 1, and MCP `command_run` in bridge mode returns `isError` with `app: timeout`. When the error arrives, the output file exists but is incomplete. A caller sees a failed export, gets no job id to follow, and may retry and start a second full export. Exports that finish within 60 seconds are not affected.

## Runtime or environment

- Release: v0.2.1, assets `filmcraft-0.2.1-macos-universal.dmg` (SHA-256 `4deff5924e8e4040e60c73db2e668812a5967c973790be7565f8e8d9c69344fd`) and `filmcraft-cli-0.2.1-macos-universal.zip` (SHA-256 `18535c3c82e4de9156251d73cf4d8f3626638ee3979063dcf4c966e811b666f6`), both matching the release's `SHA256SUMS.txt`; `filmcraft-cli --version` prints `filmcraft-cli 0.2.1`.
- Source: `main` at `771b614ad4c3fbefda5d668ce4384504b8c13f6d`. The code files cited below are byte-identical at the v0.2.1 tag, and the cited doc lines are unchanged there.
- Host: macOS 27 on Apple silicon (arm64). The app ran from the DMG's `FilmCraft.app` with a separate `--data-dir`.

## Steps to reproduce

The export must take longer than 60 seconds on the test machine. On the host above, an 8K ProRes HQ export of the demo sequence (642 frames) took 123 to 132 seconds, and a 4K ProRes HQ export took 26 to 32 seconds, so use the 8K settings or longer.

1. Start the app with the control channel and the demo project:

```sh

title: fix(packaging): Linux .rpm installs on glibc 2.34 (RHEL 9 family) where both binaries then fail with GLIBC_2.35 not found
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

The v0.2.1 Linux `.rpm` packages declare no glibc requirement, so `dnf` installs them without complaint on Rocky Linux 9 (glibc 2.34), and then both `/usr/bin/filmcraft-cli` and `/usr/bin/filmcraft` refuse to start with "version `GLIBC_2.35' not found". The release workflow states that the binaries need glibc 2.35 or newer and lists RHEL 10 as the oldest supported RHEL, and the matching `.deb` encodes that floor, so apt refuses the install on an older system. On the RHEL 9 family (RHEL, Rocky, Alma, CentOS Stream 9) the rpm instead reports a successful install of programs that cannot run. Observed for both `x86_64` and `aarch64` rpms.

## Runtime or environment

- Release: v0.2.1 (tag commit `61ab6f5c7dfc37097b8a28aac235a3e31a84a6ae`), assets `filmcraft-0.2.1-linux-x86_64.rpm` (SHA-256 `e808951b37476e7916b81e250d8f023e0c383b01c2cca938125caa284b3a80b8`) and `filmcraft-0.2.1-linux-aarch64.rpm` (SHA-256 `cb139bf6a6944d46dd35d0028a60a12d19737b924a1679a88c70f3fc6ffdfe86`), both matching the release's `SHA256SUMS.txt`. The deb control used `filmcraft-0.2.1-linux-x86_64.deb`.
- Failing system: `rockylinux/rockylinux:9` container (Rocky Linux 9.8, `ldd (GNU libc) 2.34`), on `linux/amd64` and on `linux/arm64`.
- Passing systems: `fedora:latest` (Fedora 44, glibc 2.43), where the same rpm installs and `filmcraft-cli --version` prints `filmcraft-cli 0.2.1`; `ubuntu:20.04` (glibc 2.31) for the deb control.
- `nfpm.yaml` on `main` (`771b614ad4c3fbefda5d668ce4384504b8c13f6d`) has the same rpm `depends` list as the release tag.

| Source (ffmpeg-generated) | ffprobe | FilmCraft `pixel_format`, `has_alpha` |

| `-c:v libx265 -pix_fmt yuv420p` | Main, yuv420p | `""`, false |

| `-c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv422p` | High 4:2:2, yuv422p | `"YUV 4:2:2"` (no bit depth), false |
| `-c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv422p10le -profile:v high422` | High 4:2:2, yuv422p10le | `"YUV 4:2:2"` (no bit depth), false |
| `-c:v prores_ks -profile:v 4 -pix_fmt yuv444p10le` (no alpha) | 4444, yuv444p12le | `"YUVA 4:4:4 12-bit"`, **true** |

Decoding is fine in every case; only the reported format (Project panel / probe JSON) is wrong.

## Expected

- HEVC: chroma format and bit depth from `hvcC` (`chromaFormat`, `bitDepthLumaMinus8`).
- H.264 High 4:2:2 / 4:4:4 / High 10: from the `avcC` High-profile extension (`chroma_format`,
  `bit_depth_luma_minus8`), not from `profile_idc` alone (High 4:2:2 can be 8 or 10-bit).
- ProRes 4444 / 4444 XQ: alpha only when the frame header's `alpha_channel_type` is non-zero; the

title: fix(packaging): Flatpak manifest's `xdg-pictures`-only grant leaves project media in ~/Videos and ~/Music missing
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

The Flatpak manifest `packaging/linux/flatpak/ai.storyteller.filmcraft.yml` grants one filesystem location, `--filesystem=xdg-pictures`. Its comment says the portals make broad filesystem access unnecessary: Open/Save dialogs go through the file-chooser portal and drag-and-drop through the document portal. That premise does not hold for a project's media. A `.fcproj` refers to media by absolute path, and the document portal exposes only the project file, not the media beside it. Under the manifest's permission set, the v0.2.1 engine reports a project's media in ~/Videos or ~/Music as `missing`. This held when the project in ~/Videos was handed in through the document portal, and its media sat in the same folder. Inside the sandbox ~/Videos and ~/Music are not mounted at all, so no stored path there can resolve. The same cases work under ~/Pictures. Every reproduced project was saved outside the sandbox, so it stored host paths. That covers a project made by a .deb, .rpm, AppImage, tarball or CLI install, or on another machine. Projects whose media was picked inside the Flatpak through the file chooser were not tested. The manifest's header says it is "ready for a Flathub submission". No Flatpak is published today: the v0.2.1 release assets have none, and Flathub has no `ai.storyteller.filmcraft` app. So this affects people who build the Flatpak from the repo, and anyone who would install a Flathub build made from this manifest.

- FilmCraft v0.2.1 release (tag commit 61ab6f5c7dfc37097b8a28aac235a3e31a84a6ae): the official `filmcraft-0.2.1-linux-aarch64.tar.gz`, checksum matched against `SHA256SUMS.txt`. title: fix(mcp): `render_frame` and `render_preview` advertise `readOnlyHint: true` but move the playhead when called with `seconds`
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

The MCP tools `render_frame` and `render_preview` advertise `readOnlyHint: true`, but a call with `seconds` moves the active sequence's playhead to that time. In bridge mode, this moves the playhead in the desktop app the user has open. The move persists after the call: `sequence_inspect` reports the new playhead, and later commands that default to the playhead act at the new position. With Sequence ▸ Selection Follows Playhead on, the call also changes the clip selection. `docs/agents.md` tells clients they can let renders run without asking because of this hint, so a client that follows it lets these calls change editor state without asking the user. It happens in headless mode (`--demo`/`--project`) and bridge mode (`--bridge`), and on every call that passes `seconds`. Calls without `seconds` leave the playhead where it is.

title: security(control): control port executes JSON smuggled in an HTTP request body (web pages can drive the app while --control is open)
author: pk-claude
body:
## Summary

The desktop control server (`filmcraft --control <port>` or `FILMCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT`) has no authentication. It also keeps reading after a line fails to parse as JSON. So an ordinary HTTP request, which any web page can send to `127.0.0.1` with `fetch(..., {mode: "no-cors", body})`, gets its header lines rejected but its JSON body executed. While the control port is open, a malicious page in the user's browser can drive the app: `engine.execute` (any of the 666 commands, including import and export to arbitrary paths), `ui.type`/`ui.key`/`ui.click`, `ui.screenshot` to an arbitrary path, and `app.quit`.

Binding to loopback doesn't prevent this, because the browser runs on the same machine. Chrome's Local Network Access prompt helps in recent Chrome versions, but not in other browsers, or once a user clicks Allow.

## Reproduction (v0.2.1, Windows x64 portable; the code is the same on `main`)

1. `filmcraft.exe --control 9876`
2. Send what a browser would send for a cross-origin `text/plain` POST:

```python
import socket, time
body = '{"id":7,"method":"engine.execute","params":{"command":"file.openDemoProject","params":{}}}\n'
req = ('POST / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: 127.0.0.1:9876\r\nOrigin: https://attacker.example\r\n'
       'Content-Type: text/plain\r\nContent-Length: %d\r\n\r\n%s') % (len(body), body)
s = socket.create_connection(('127.0.0.1', 9876)); s.sendall(req.encode()); time.sleep(4)
print(s.recv(65536).decode())
```

Each request line and header line gets `{"ok":false,"error":"bad JSON: ..."}`. The final reply is `{"id":7,"ok":true,"result":{"sequence":21}}`, and the demo project is now open in the app.

## Cause

`apps/filmcraft/src/control_server.rs`, `serve()`: a line that fails to parse produces an error reply and the loop continues, so the body after the HTTP headers is dispatched like a normal request.

## Suggested fix

1. **Close the connection if a line isn't valid JSON** (at least the first line), and/or if a line looks like an HTTP reques…

title: The `--control` server runs commands with no authentication. A friendly note and a few ideas
author: PyThonicsML
body:
Hi, and thank you for putting this out in the open.

I run a small operation where AI agents handle real work, and I have been looking for an editor that those agents can drive. This is exactly the one I was after. I read code for security before I install anything, so I went through v0.2.1, commit 61ab6f5c. I can see the project is about a week old and flagged as early alpha, so please take this as a heads-up from someone rooting for it, not a complaint.

**What I noticed**

The control server in `apps/filmcraft/src/control_server.rs` binds to `127.0.0.1`. That part is good. The problem is that it runs any line that parses as JSON, with no token and no handshake, and when a line will not parse, it answers with an error and carries on reading.

Loopback keeps other machines away. It does not keep out everything else on the same machine, and that covers a web page open in a browser, since browsers can fire plain requests at local ports. Because lines that are not JSON get skipped instead of closing the connection, I think a page could slip a command line through.

That counts for more because of what the commands are able to do. The engine writes and deletes at whatever path it receives. Two cases I read: `captions.export` writes to any path, and `media.makeOffline` with `deleteFiles` deletes the files behind imported media. I did not find any path checks in the engine.

To be clear about what I did and did not do: this comes from reading the code. I did not build a proof of concept and did not test it against a running app, so I could be wrong about how a particular browser behaves. I am deliberately keeping the details general here, and I am glad to share more privately.

**Ideas, in case they help**

- A random token generated when `--control` starts, and required on the first line. The MCP bridge could read it from a file or an env var.
- Drop the connection on the first line that is not valid JSON, and turn away anything that resembles an HTTP request.

title: Optional persistent managed-media catalog and identity-based relinking
author: whatever-industries
body:
For large projects and media spread across drives or shared storage, I would like an **optional persistent managed-media catalog** that resolves media by identity rather than relying only on its last path. Ordinary loose-file importing should remain available and unchanged by default.

The proposal is distinct from project storage. Avid AVB bins hold binary clip/sequence metadata, while PMR/MDB files index managed media. Separating project modules and indexing media are different features and should have independent acceptance criteria. Performance benefits need to be measured rather than assumed from that separation.

The motivation for the separate modular-project proposal in #1049 is **stability and recoverability at Hollywood feature-film/television scale**: independently loadable and recoverable bins/sequences should limit how much of a production is affected by a damaged module or interrupted save. The media catalog proposed here addresses the other side of that workflow—finding and maintaining media references across large collections and multiple volumes. Both need explicit reliability tests; neither should be presented as an automatic consequence of adopting Avid-like storage.

title: [Bug] Failed recovery snapshot write is not retried without another edit
author: Jagalite
body:
A transient OPFS recovery-snapshot write failure leaves the previous snapshot in place. Restoring write access does not retry the unchanged dirty revision; reloading then recovers the older project and omits the newest sequence.

- Current main release browser build `86f3375775258cd7140c36e5b8e3d21ced9ee711`, verified again on 2026-10-07. Rust 1.95.0, wasm-bindgen 0.2.129.
- macOS 26.5.2 arm64, Apple M1; isolated standalone Chrome 154.0.8037.93 and Firefox 155.0, headless, local COOP/COEP host, actual OPFS storage.

1. Start a disposable profile with `?fresh&norecover`. Create `Recovery test` with `file.newProject`, then create `Sequence A` with `file.newSequence` (`video:1`, `audio:1`).

title: [Bug] Browser proxy creation and mask tracking crash on unsupported std::time::Instant
author: Jagalite
body:
**Environment**

Tested latest main `61238bf8fc129077fe2b7982550303be49f55a93`, verified against upstream immediately before filing. Local release browser/Wasm build on macOS Apple Silicon, Chrome 154.0.8037.93, Firefox 155.0 and Playwright WebKit 26.6 (not Safari).

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Create a fresh project, import a valid small H.264 clip (128×128, 96 frames), and create a sequence from that media. Saving the project succeeds before the test.
2. Request proxies through the production browser API:
```js
await filmcraft.execute('media.createProxies', {
  items: [importedItemId],
  preset: 'h264_quarter',
  destination: '/exports/proxies',
  attach: false,
  wait: false
});
```

**Expected**

Proxy creation completes, exposes a job, or returns an actionable browser capability error while the app remains usable.

**Actual**

FilmCraft displays **FilmCraft stopped working**, with:
```
time not implemented on this platform
```
The panic stacks include `std::time::Instant::now`; the longer WebKit stack identifies `filmcraft_engine::proxies::start_job`. The request does not resolve within an external 30-second deadline; subsequent `jobs.list` and project Save requests also time out. Independent JavaScript timers continue running, so this is an app/Wasm panic rather than a stopped browser process.

**Impact**

Requesting proxies terminates the editor and prevents subsequent job queries or saving until reload.

**Scope and supporting evidence**

Reproduces in all three engines with both default decoding and the app-supported `nowebcodecs` software control: six fresh runs. No decoder or clock fault injection was used. Healthy pre-operation native project saves, available console stacks and crash screenshots were retained. This confirms the crash; it does not qualify proxy codec output or native threading.

title: Proposal: optional native Groq transcription using media-linked word timestamps
author: Gustitolito
body:
## Problem and workflow

I would like to use FilmCraft's existing media-linked, word-level transcripts with a hosted transcription provider such as Groq. My current workflow requires an external transcription API, agent-generated Premiere XML, manual timeline edits, another audio export and transcription pass, and externally rendered styled captions. Keeping transcription and editable captions inside FilmCraft would remove several of these steps while preserving manual editing freedom.

FilmCraft already stores transcript words in source-media time and derives a sequence transcript from timeline edits. Native Groq support could feed that existing model directly instead of requiring an external audio/transcription script or local Whisper weights.

## Proposed implementation

- Add an optional `groq` feature implementing the existing `Transcriber` trait; keep it disabled by default, expose it in desktop/CLI/MCP through the existing native host command path, and leave the web path unchanged.
- Initially select the provider through `FILMCRAFT_TRANSCRIPTION_PROVIDER=groq` and a process-only `GROQ_API_KEY`. A settings UI could follow the maintainers' preferred credential-storage design.
- Encode mono 16 kHz PCM16 WAV directly in Rust and send bounded chunks to Groq's fixed HTTPS transcription endpoint, requesting word timestamps. No FFmpeg dependency or external transcription subprocess is needed.
- Default to `whisper-large-v3-turbo`, allow model/language configuration, and use automatic language detection when language is unset.
- Convert word times and sample-based chunk offsets to FilmCraft ticks, validate timestamps/responses, bound response sizes, sanitize errors, retry transient failures and check cancellation between chunks.
- Optionally cache validated responses by audio/model/language in the host-selected data directory. Do not persist keys in projects or caches. Cache files contain transcript text and should be documented accordingly.

body:
## Summary

`project.delete` ignores its explicit `items` parameter when nothing is selected in the Project panel. It fails with `command 'project.delete' is not available right now: select an item in the Project panel`, even though the body handles `items` correctly. Agents driving the app through the control channel or MCP can't delete by id without first faking a UI selection.

## Repro

With the demo project open and nothing selected in the Project panel:

```json
{"id": "project.delete", "params": {"items": [1, 2, 3, 4]}}
```

This fails with "not available right now". The workaround is to select first:

```json
[{"id": "project.select", "params": {"items": [1, 2, 3, 4]}},
 {"id": "project.delete", "params": {"items": [1, 2, 3, 4]}}]
```

That returns `{"bins": 4, "items": 0}` as expected.

## Cause

`crates/engine/src/commands.rs:2361` registers `project.delete` with the `has_project_selection` enabled-check (`commands.rs:105`), which only looks at `s.state.project_selection`. The enabled-check runs before the body, so the explicit `items` never get used, even though the body already falls back to the selection only when `items` is absent.

Other commands gated on `has_project_selection` that also take explicit ids likely have the same problem; I haven't audited them.

## Suggested fix

Have the enabled-check accept an explicit, non-empty `items` param (or move the "nothing to delete" check into the body when `items` is given), so `{"items":[…]}` works regardless of UI selection. A regression test could call `project.delete` with `items` and an empty selection and assert the items are gone.

Related, minor: with Cmd+A in the Project panel, only items get selected, not bins, so empty bins can't be cleared via select-all + Delete.

Found while driving the app through the MCP bridge (`filmcraft-cli mcp --bridge`), Windows 11, commit 61238bf.

title: control: ui.key Ctrl+ chords do not trigger shortcuts on Windows/Linux (only Cmd+ works)
author: aitorsansal
body:
## Summary

On Windows (and presumably Linux), `ui.key` with a `Ctrl+…` chord, e.g. `{"key":"Ctrl+Z"}` through the control channel or the MCP `ui_key` tool, does nothing. `Cmd+Z` works. A physical Ctrl+Z should be unaffected (egui-winit sets `command` for Ctrl off macOS), so this looks specific to injected keys.

## Repro

1. `cargo run -p filmcraft -- --control 9876` on Windows, then make any undoable edit.
2. Send `{"cmd":"ui.key","params":{"key":"Ctrl+Z"}}`. Nothing is undone.
3. Send `{"cmd":"ui.key","params":{"key":"Cmd+Z"}}`. The edit is undone.

## Cause

- `ui.key` (`crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs:335`) parses the chord with `menus::parse_shortcut`, which maps `"Ctrl"` to `egui::Modifiers { ctrl: true, command: false }` (`crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs:515`).
- Bindings are stored as `Cmd+…` and become `command: true`. A real Ctrl press on Windows/Linux sets both `ctrl` and `command`, but the synthetic event only has `ctrl`, so no binding matches.
- The engine's `Chord::parse` already handles this per platform (`crates/engine/src/shortcuts.rs:277`: `ctrl` becomes `cmd` off macOS); `parse_shortcut` doesn't.
- `ui.click`'s `modifiers: {"ctrl": true}` (`control.rs:68`) has the same gap: it sets `ctrl` without `command` off macOS.

## Suggested fix

In `parse_shortcut` (and the `modifiers()` helper in `control.rs`), set `command = true` alongside `ctrl` when not on macOS, mirroring what egui-winit does for a physical Ctrl key. Alternatively, build the event from `filmcraft_engine::shortcuts::Chord::parse`. A regression test could drive `ui.key` with `Ctrl+Z` after an edit and assert the undo happened.

Agents tend to send `Ctrl+…` on Windows, since that's what the menus show there, so this silently breaks every Ctrl-based shortcut for them.

Found while driving the app through the MCP bridge (`filmcraft-cli mcp --bridge`), Windows 11, commit 61238bf.

title: [Bug/Improvement] Window shows "not responding" on Linux while a file dialog is open
author: floriank
body:
## System
Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS

### What happens
On Ubuntu (GNOME), GNOME's "Waiting for response / Force Quit / Wait" prompt appears often when importing media. It appears while a file picker is open or an import is running.

## Why
GNOME shows this prompt when the app doesn't answer the compositor's ping for about 5 seconds. The native file pickers in `apps/filmcraft/src/main.rs` use the blocking `rfd::FileDialog`  (`pick_files`, `pick_file`, `save_file`, `pick_folder`)

<details>
  <summary>Quick Sweep via Claude</summary>
 

  With the xdg-portal backend, the call waits for the portal dialog on the UI thread, so the event loop can't respond until the user has chosen a file. HostHooks::pick_* is synchronous, and about 25 call sites in ui-egui use the returned path immediately.
</details>

## Affects
Every picker, export and preset import/export.

Maybe Make the pickers non-blocking?. A caller may requests a pick with a continuation (a command id plus params). A worker thread runs `rfd::AsyncFileDialog`. The frame loop applies the continuation when the result arrives.

Happy to help and donate a couple tokens/time if need be.

title: Import reads long WAV files whole on the UI thread: ~1 GB per 90-minute mono WAV, window frozen while it loads
author: BlaineMoore
body:
## Summary

On current `main`, importing a WAV still reads and holds the whole file, and does it on the UI thread. A 90-minute mono 16-bit WAV (518 MB) adds about **1.0 GB** to the app's physical footprint, and the window and the control port stop responding until it has loaded: **13.9 s** for one file from a USB SSD, and about **55 s** for a session's four mic and system tracks.

#41 (MEM1) fixed this for MP4. A 7.1 GB HEVC webcam recording now imports in 0.12 s and costs about 25 MB, and frames from anywhere in it render in about 0.06 s, which is great. WAV is still a format "decoded in one go" (`crates/media/src/reader.rs`), and `import_streamed` → `MediaPool::open_file` → `open_reader` falls back to reading the whole file when no reader opener takes it. #165 bounded that fallback for the Media Browser's probe and mentioned a streaming WAV reader as a possible follow-up; this is the import side of the same thing.

Related: #157, #165 (the Media Browser probe), #41 (MEM1, the desktop reader), #55 (overall memory budget).

- `main` at `5231852443363f001c3f6b396dd9b1e6461ae2be`, `cargo build --release -p filmcraft`, Rust 1.99.0 (Homebrew)

title: Windows: export paths don't expand ~, mishandle a trailing \ and verbatim (\\?\) paths
author: Tom1tk
body:
## Summary
Export output paths are mishandled on Windows in three ways:

1. **`~/` is not expanded.** `expand_home` (engine `export_tools.rs`, and a copy in the Export panel's `export_mode.rs`) reads only `HOME`, which Windows does not set. A location like `~/Exports/` stays literal.
2. **A folder named by a trailing `\` gets numbered names when queuing several sequences.** `output_path` treats a path ending in `/` or `\` as a folder, but the suffix check in `export.queue.add` only looks for `/`. Queuing two sequences to `C:\Exports\` (not yet created) gives `Main Edit.wav` and `Second Cut_2.wav` instead of `Second Cut.wav`.
3. **`/` after a `\\?\` prefix is not a separator.** For a verbatim path (what `std::fs::canonicalize` returns on Windows), `"\\?\C:\out/"` joined with a sequence name becomes `...\out/\Main Edit.wav`, and writing it fails with os error 123. This is why `export_tests::queue_exports_several_sequences_and_ranges` fails on Windows.

Also, `std_home_dir` prefers `HOME` over `USERPROFILE`, so under Git Bash/MSYS (where `HOME=/c/Users/...`) the home directory is a Unix-style path that native file APIs cannot open.

## Steps to reproduce (Windows 11)
`cargo test -p filmcraft-engine queue_exports_several_sequences_and_ranges`:

```
os error 123 ... engine-queue-many-<pid>/\Main Edit.wav
```

Or from the control channel: `export.queue.add` with `"path": "~/Exports/"` and check the queued item's path in `export.queue.list`.


## Fix
PR #282

# H.264 frame cropping (SPS crop offsets) is ignored — iPhone videos render with the wrong field of view

## Summary

FilmCraft reports and renders clips larger than they should be when the source carries a non-zero
H.264 frame-crop rectangle. For iPhone video the extra border is **real picture content**
(sensor / electronic-stabilisation margin), so the viewer sees a wider field of view than
QuickTime, Photos, or ffmpeg — i.e. anything that follows the spec.

Nothing errors out. `probe`, the generated sequence preset, and `render` all agree on the same
wrong size, so the mismatch is silent.

## Environment

- FilmCraft **0.2.1**, Windows x64 (portable build unpacked from `filmcraft-0.2.1-windows-x64.msi`)
- Windows 10/11 x64, NVIDIA GTX 1660

title: Loudness analysis ignores channel count - mono measured ~3 LU too loud
author: jkstrom
body:
# Loudness analysis ignores the source channel count — mono clips are measured ~3 LU too loud

## Summary

`essentialSound.autoMatch` (and the `measured_lufs` it reports) computes loudness **as if every
source were stereo**, ignoring the actual channel count of the media. For a mono source this
overstates the integrated loudness by **≈3 LU**, so the gain it applies is **≈3 dB too small**
and the result still misses the requested target.

The R128 implementation itself appears correct — the error is entirely in the channel handling.

## Environment

- FilmCraft **0.2.1**, Windows x64 (headless MCP: `filmcraft-cli --demo mcp`)
- ffmpeg 7.x `ebur128` filter used as the independent reference
- Sequence: 44100 Hz, clips placed on A1

## Steps to reproduce

### 1. Make two files with identical content and different channel counts

```bash
# source: any mono clip; using an iPhone movie here
ffmpeg -i IMG_2061.MOV -af "pan=stereo|c0=c0|c1=c0" -c:a pcm_s16le img2061_stereo.wav
ffmpeg -i IMG_2061.MOV -ac 1                       -c:a pcm_s16le img2061_mono.wav
```

Reference values from `ffmpeg -i <file> -filter_complex ebur128 -f null -`:

| file | channels | ffmpeg `I` |
|---|---|---|
| `img2061_stereo.wav` | 2 | **−40.9 LUFS** |
| `img2061_mono.wav` | 1 | **−43.9 LUFS** |

### 2. Import both, place them on one sequence, and ask FilmCraft to match loudness

```
exec file.import            '{"paths":["……/img2061_stereo.wav","……/img2061_mono.wav"]}'
exec file.newSequence       '{"name":"LoudnessTest","fps":30}'
exec timeline.place         '{"item":114,"audioTrack":"A1","time":0}'
exec timeline.place         '{"item":115,"audioTrack":"A1","time":762048000000}'

# [Bug] MKV files with multiple stereo audio streams only import the first audio stream

## Description

When importing MKV video files containing multiple independent stereo audio streams, FilmCraft only recognizes and imports the first audio stream.

For example, my gameplay recordings contain **3 separate stereo audio streams (6 channels total)**. Adobe Premiere Pro recognizes all three streams, allowing them to be edited independently.

FilmCraft currently only exposes the first stereo stream. The other two are inaccessible.

**This also happens when importing the original MKV directly into FilmCraft, without using Premiere Pro or XML interchange.**

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Obtain an MKV file containing 1 video stream and 3 independent stereo audio streams.
2. Import the MKV directly into FilmCraft.
3. Add the imported video to a sequence.
4. Inspect the available audio tracks and source audio options.

## Expected Behavior

FilmCraft should recognize all three stereo audio streams and allow them to be placed onto separate timeline tracks.

For example:
- A1: Stereo stream 1 (channels L/R)
- A2: Stereo stream 2 (channels L/R)
- A3: Stereo stream 3 (channels L/R)

Each stream should be independently accessible for playback, mixing, muting and editing.

## Actual Behavior

Only the first stereo audio stream is available. Streams 2 and 3 cannot be selected or added to the timeline.

## Potential Cause

After looking through the source code, I noticed that `crates/codecs/src/mkv.rs` selects the audio track using:

```rust
let atrack = file.tracks.iter()
    .position(|t| t.kind == TrackKind::Audio && !t.samples.is_empty());
```

Using `.position()` appears to select only the first audio stream.

Additionally, `MediaInfo` currently exposes a single optional `AudioStreamInfo`, which may limit support for multiple independent audio streams.

This suggests the issue may extend beyond the MKV decoder to the media model and timeline audio handling.

title: Shared audio engine and absolute timeline for SoundCraft sync and ST 2110 playout
author: marcnnn
body:
## Summary

A proposal to give FilmCraft and SoundCraft **one shared audio engine** with an absolute, PTP-capable timeline. On top of that, an optional **FPGA audio-over-IP card** backend would enable:

- **Sample-accurate sync** between FilmCraft and SoundCraft on one machine, and between machines via PTP (IEEE 1588)
- **SMPTE ST 2110 playout and ingest:** ST 2110-30 / AES67 audio first, ST 2110-20 video later
- **Low-latency monitoring** for recording and production, processed on the card

The engine and monitoring side is described in detail in storytold/soundcraft#27. This issue covers what it means for FilmCraft.

This issue is for discussion. It doesn't ask for anything to be built right away.

## Motivation

FilmCraft's playback (M4) uses the standard model: the audio device is the master clock and picture follows sound. Each cpal callback moves the timeline forward by one buffer. That is the right choice for a standalone NLE, but it leaves three gaps:

1. **No shared time with SoundCraft.** Two apps counting callbacks from their own devices can only be kept aligned by exchanging positions (IPC, MTC), and they drift between updates.
2. **No shared time between machines.** A cutting room and a mix stage, or an edit system and a broadcast facility, can't agree on what "now" means.
3. **No path to IP playout.** ST 2110 and AES67 identify each sample and frame by absolute PTP time (mapped by SMPTE ST 2059-1). A relative timeline can't produce or consume those timestamps directly.

## Proposal

### Transport as a function of time

Transport state becomes one **anchor**:

```
position(t) = P0 + (t - T0) * rate
```

`T0` is a time on a shared clock, `P0` the media position at that time, `rate` the speed (J/K/L map onto it naturally). The audio render asks "which samples belong to the span my output will actually play?" Video presentation is scheduled against the same anchor. Transport commands become anchors scheduled slightly ahead, so FilmCraft and SoundCraft star…

Tested **Film Craft 0.4.0 for Windows**.

Film Craft is still rough around the edges compared with EffectCraft, but it shows real promise. These issues currently make common editing tasks harder than they need to be:

title: Improving Color Grading Tools and Introducing Node-Based Workflows
author: jjajek
body:
In my opinion, color grading is one of Premiere Pro's biggest weaknesses. I've been working with Premiere Pro since 2018, and I work professionally in media production. I've always found it baffling that Adobe has tools like Lightroom Classic and Photoshop, yet Premiere Pro's color grading workflow still feels incredibly clunky and unintuitive. The UI, in particular, leaves a lot to be desired.

One thing I absolutely love about Premiere Pro is the ability to apply color corrections using adjustment layers and stack them as needed. It's a simple but incredibly powerful workflow.

It would be great to see FilmCraft offer a choice between the traditional color grading workflow and a new, node-based approach, implemented as a separate effect or tool. Node-based grading would open up a lot of possibilities for more advanced workflows. Alternatively, even a substantial overhaul of the existing color grading UI would be a huge improvement.

I'll try to put some time into exploring possible solutions myself and come up with a more concrete proposal, but I wanted to raise this issue now. Since FilmCraft is open source, I believe that investing in better color grading tools could significantly increase the project's overall value and make it a much more compelling alternative to established video editing software.

title: feat(packaging): include the CLI and MCP server in source-built Flatpaks

title: feat(control): add optional strict validation for command params and export settings
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Provide an opt-in way for automation callers to reject unrecognized engine parameter and export-setting keys before an edit or export runs. This requests a new diagnostic capability; it does not assume that the current free-form parameter contract promises rejection.

## Problem to solve

A caller can misspell an optional key, receive success, and get the default behavior. In the tested release, `timeline.razor {"second":3}` cuts at the playhead, and `file.exportMedia` with `start` and `end` exports the whole sequence. CLI `export --settings '{"hardware_encoding":"auto"}'` uses the default encoder because the JSON field is `hardwareEncoding`. The caller must inspect the resulting timeline or resolved settings to discover that the intended option was ignored.

The MCP layer rejects unrecognized outer tool arguments, but this protection does not extend to engine parameters inside `command_run.params`. The documented distinction is deliberate: engine parameters reach the command unchanged.

## Proposed behavior

Allow automation callers to opt into strict parameter validation for engine commands, including nested `ExportSettings` passed by the CLI export command. In that mode, report each unrecognized key with its command or settings context and the supported keys before changing the project or creating an export job. Make the recognized keys discoverable so callers can correct their input. Keep existing calls available under the current lenient behavior.

Validation must recognize the command's actual supported inputs, including shared time aliases and command-specific dynamic objects. The published JSON-ish description strings are not complete closed schemas and cannot alone define the accepted-key set.

## Acceptance criteria

- Strict calls reject `timeline.razor {"second":3}` before adding cuts. The error identifies `second` and provides the accepted time inputs. Valid `seconds`, `frame`, `time`, and `timecode` calls keep working where the command supp…

title: [Feature Request] Suite-Wide Real-Time Collaborative Editing with a Shared Open-Source, Self-Hosted Collaboration Server
author: wjywbs
body:
(Prompt: Write a feature request for Collaborative Editing. Request not only for this app but also for the whole suite of apps. Request a common open source Collaborative Editing server that can be hosted in a local network, remote or cloud that supports all apps.)

## Summary

I would like to request **real-time collaborative editing for FilmCraft and the entire ArtCraft suite**, powered by a **common, open-source collaboration server** that can be self-hosted on a local network, a private remote server, or public/private cloud infrastructure.

Instead of developing an independent collaboration solution for each application, I propose creating a **shared collaboration framework, protocol, and server** that all ArtCraft applications can use.

The goal is to enable multiple users to work simultaneously on the same project, with synchronized changes, user presence, permissions, conflict management, and version history, while retaining full control over their files, infrastructure, and data.

**Most importantly, collaboration should not require an ArtCraft-operated cloud service or a proprietary subscription.**

## Scope: The Entire ArtCraft Ecosystem

Although I am opening this request in the FilmCraft repository, I would like this to be considered an **ecosystem-wide feature and architectural initiative**.

title: Only the first audio track of multi-track video files is imported
author: rangamitch
body:
﻿## Problem

When a video file with several audio tracks is imported, FilmCraft only imports the first audio track and ignores the rest.

Example: a Medal.tv clip (MP4) with 7 AAC stereo tracks (14 channels). Only the first stereo pair was available in the timeline.

## Fix

PR #396 (https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/pull/396) imports every audio track of MP4/MOV files:

- Each playable audio track (up to 8) becomes its own stream.
- On import, each stream gets its own audio clip through the existing Modify ▸ Audio Channels mapping.
- Placing the clip adds audio tracks when the sequence lacks them.

## Remaining limits

- MKV, WebM and MXF still import only their first audio track.
- Each clip decodes every stream of the file, which could be optimised later.

title: Feature Request: Object Mask (AI-Powered Masking) for FilmCraft
author: SirCartaux
body: Hi everyone, As you can see here, FilmCraft currently offers three masking tools: the Pen Tool, the Rectangle Tool, and the Ellipse Tool. While these cover the basics of manual masking quite well, they quickly reach their limits when it comes to more complex or organic shapes — especially when dealing with moving objects or irregular contours. In Adobe Premiere Pro, there's a newer addition to the toolkit: the so-called Object Mask. This is an AI-assisted masking feature that automatically detects objects and tracks them over time, without the need to manually place hundreds of keyframes. It not only saves an enormous amount of time, but also enables workflows that would be practically unrealistic with classic path-based masks. My suggestion: Would it be possible to bring a similar feature to FilmCraft? I imagine this would be a fairly complex undertaking — it would likely require some form of object detection (e.g., via a machine learning model), a tracking component, and a clean integration into the existing mask UI. But features like this are exactly what could set FilmCraft apart from the competition in the long run. Some possible implementation ideas: Automatic object detection via AI (e.g., an ONNX model or similar) Motion tracking across multiple frames Manual fine-tuning of the generated mask (feather, expansion, etc.) Integration as a fourth tool alongside Pen, Rectangle, and Ellipse — perhaps as an "Object Mask Tool" I'd love to hear your thoughts on this, and I'd be happy if this feature could at least be considered as an idea for future versions. If there are already discussions going in this direction, please let me know! Best regards, Henri

body:
## Environment

- Fedora 44, GNOME Shell 50.5, Wayland session, 167% display scaling
- Built from source at `7b6c134`

## Title bar doesn't follow the GNOME theme (Wayland)

On GNOME Wayland, the app draws its own title bar. This app shows winit's plain fallback bar, which
ignores the GNOME theme, dark mode and button layout.

The workspace sets `eframe = { version = "0.36", default-features = false }` (`Cargo.toml:69`),
which also drops winit's default `wayland-csd-adwaita` feature, so `sctk-adwaita` isn't in
`Cargo.lock`.

Possible fixes:

- Enable `winit/wayland-csd-adwaita`, so the title bar follows GNOME's look and light/dark mode, or
- Draw an in-app title bar, as PhotoCraft does on Linux.

Workaround: start the app through Xwayland (`env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY filmcraft`), so GNOME draws a real
title bar.

Same issue in GridCraft, with more detail: https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/issues/54

title: HybridDecoder fallback loses pictures when the software decoder rejects a replayed sample
author: MrCloudy2
body:
## Summary

When a hardware decoder fails mid-stream, `HybridDecoder` replays the samples since the last restart point through the software decoder ([`fall_back`](https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/blob/7b6c134472287db4367fca80bcb498240ba36567/crates/platform/src/hybrid.rs#L133-L158)). If the software decoder rejects **one** of the replayed samples, the replay stops at that sample:

https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/blob/7b6c134472287db4367fca80bcb498240ba36567/crates/platform/src/hybrid.rs#L152-L155

The `?` returns at once, so:

1. **Pictures are lost.** The pictures the software decoder already output during the replay are neither returned nor kept, and the software decoder has consumed those samples, so they never come out again.
2. **The rest of the replay is skipped.** The software decoder never sees the remaining samples of the run.
3. **The error lands on the wrong sample.** The caller gets an error for the sample that triggered the fallback, which the software decoder may have accepted, while the rejected sample's call had already succeeded in hardware.
4. The replay log is not put back (`self.log` stays `None`).

Decoding in software from the start would instead report that one sample and carry on.

The code is shared by every hardware backend (VideoToolbox, Media Foundation, VA-API), so this isn't specific to one OS. It happens with damaged input that the GPU tolerates but our decoder rejects, followed by a hardware failure in the same run. That is the usual case when a driver gives up on corrupt data a few frames later.

## How to reproduce

**On real hardware** (Linux, Intel UHD 750, iHD 26.3.5): an open-GOP HEVC file with 5 flipped bits in the sample data. Pure software decoding outputs **100** pictures (3 samples rejected). Through VA-API the driver fails at a later sample and the hybrid falls back: **99** pictures, every run. NVIDIA (nvidia-vaapi-driver) tolerates the damage and never falls back, so it outputs 100.

**Without a GPU:** a stan…

title: Ultra Key: "Setting" (Relaxed/Aggressive) only scales two factors, the parameter values stay at Default
author: wustrauthomas-png
body:
Version: 0.4.0 (macOS, Apple M4 Pro), engine driven via `filmcraft-cli mcp` (headless).

What happens
Setting `setting` = 2 (Aggressive) on `ultra_key` only changes two internal multipliers (gain and pedestal, `crates/render/src/vfx/color.rs` around line 267 at 7b6c134). Matte Generation, Matte Cleanup and Spill Suppression values (transparency, tolerance, pedestal, choke, soften, contrast, spill, ...) stay at their Default values.

What the user sees
On green-screen footage (Sony FX3, 4K 4:2:2 10-bit), light and dark clothing turns partly transparent: the background shows through a white shirt and a dark jacket.

What we expected
In Premiere Pro, switching Setting from Default to Aggressive visibly changes the parameter values themselves (we observed 8 parameters change: transparency, shadow, tolerance, pedestal, choke, soften, contrast, desaturate). When we set those values by hand in FilmCraft (transparency 40, highlight 10, shadow 55, tolerance 90, pedestal 50, choke 10, soften 10, contrast 10, mid point 50, desaturate 50, range 50, spill 50, luma 50), the key is clean.

Why it matters
Editors coming from Premiere switch to Aggressive and expect a solid matte. Here they get a matte with holes and no hint why.

Suggestion
When `setting` changes, write the corresponding value set into the parameters (like an effect preset), or at least document in the effect notes that only two factors are affected.

Steps to reproduce
1. Import a green-screen clip, place it on V2 over any background on V1.
2. `effects.apply {"effect":"ultra_key"}`, `effects.setParam key_color=<green>`, `effects.setParam setting=2`.
3. `render_frame` and look at bright/dark clothing; switch `output` to 1 (alpha) to see the matte.

title: MCP render_frame: max_side 0 fails with "render scale 0 must be finite and positive"
author: wustrauthomas-png
body:
Version: 0.4.0, `filmcraft-cli mcp` (headless).

What happens
`render_frame {"seconds": 30, "max_side": 0}` returns the error "render scale 0 must be finite and positive".

What we expected
The doc comment of the PNG helper in `crates/automation/src/lib.rs` says 0 means no limit, so we expected a full-size frame.

Cause (from reading the code at 7b6c134)
`crates/automation/src/server.rs` around line 405 computes `max / longest side` without a special case for 0.

Suggestion
Treat `max_side == 0` as scale 1.0 (or document that 0 is not allowed). Workaround: pass the sequence's longest side.

Steps to reproduce
Any project with an active sequence, MCP `render_frame` with `max_side: 0`.

title: Sony FX3 MP4: start timecode in the rtmd metadata track is not read
author: wustrauthomas-png
body:
Version: 0.4.0, macOS.

What happens
`filmcraft-cli probe <FX3 file>.MP4` reports `"start_timecode": null`. The file carries its timecode in Sony's real-time metadata track: ffprobe lists a data stream with codec tag `rtmd` and `tag:timecode=21:22:40:02`.

Why it matters
Synchronising by timecode (Clip > Synchronize, multicam) does not work with this footage. Low priority for us (we sync by audio).

Suggestion
When the file has no `tmcd` track, read the start timecode from the `rtmd` track.

Steps to reproduce
Probe a Sony FX3 XAVC S-I MP4 with FilmCraft and with ffprobe and compare. We only tested the FX3; other Sony XAVC S cameras may behave the same.

title: Importing a Premiere FCP7 XML / OTIO sequence takes 97 s / 66 s for 3 media files
author: wustrauthomas-png
body:
Version: 0.4.0, macOS, Apple M4 Pro, media on an external SSD, `filmcraft-cli mcp` (headless). Measured once, system load 2 to 7.

What happens
A Premiere Pro 26 sequence (6:14 min, 70 clips, 3 media files: two 4K MP4, one WAV) imported with `file.import`:
- FCP7 XML: 97 s
- OTIO: 66 s
The cut itself arrives exactly (70/70 clips frame-exact, 20/20 markers). Saved as `.fcproj`, the same project opens in 0.03 s, and importing the two video files directly takes under 1 s.

Question
What does the interchange import do with each file that takes this long (full read, waveform, checksum)? A progress report or deferring that work would help. Happy to rerun with a debug or log option if you tell us which.

title: FCP7 XML export writes every audio clip as source channel 1 (right channel of a split stereo file is lost)
author: wustrauthomas-png
body:
Version: 0.4.0, macOS.

What happens
A Premiere Pro sequence with a stereo camera file split onto two mono tracks (A1 = channel 1, A2 = channel 2) is imported into FilmCraft as FCP7 XML and exported again with `file.exportFcp7Xml`. In the exported XML both tracks reference source channel 1, and re-imported into Premiere both show "L"; the right channel is gone. The cut itself round-trips exactly: all 70 clips, 20 markers, Basic Motion scale and position.

Cause (from reading the code at 7b6c134)
`crates/interchange/src/fcp7.rs` around lines 963-966 always writes `<sourcetrack><mediatype>audio</mediatype><trackindex>1</trackindex></sourcetrack>`. The importer does not read `sourcetrack` (the only occurrences in `crates/interchange` are in the writer), so the information is already lost on the way in.

Suggestion
Keep `sourcetrack/trackindex` on the audio clip when importing, and write it back on export.

Steps to reproduce
1. In Premiere, put a stereo clip in a sequence so that it shows as two mono tracks (L and R), export Final Cut Pro XML.
2. FilmCraft: `file.import` the XML, then `file.exportFcp7Xml`.
3. Compare `sourcetrack/trackindex` in both files (2 becomes 1), or import into Premiere.

title: Add a System theme option that follows the macOS light/dark appearance
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Add a System choice to FilmCraft's interface theme setting that follows the macOS light/dark appearance live, so the app changes with the rest of the desktop when macOS switches appearance automatically.

## Problem to solve

macOS can switch between Light and Dark appearance automatically (System Settings → Appearance → Auto changes it at sunset and sunrise), and many Mac apps offer a "System" theme choice that tracks it.

FilmCraft offers only manual interface themes. View → Appearance lists "Darkest" (the default), "Medium" and "Light", and Settings → Appearance → Color Theme lists the same themes as "Darkest", "Dark" and "Light". The choice is stored as `appearance.colorTheme` in `preferences.json`, and the palette is chosen only from it; no code path reads the OS appearance.

Because FilmCraft only has manual choices, a user whose macOS appearance switches automatically has to change the app theme by hand at least twice a day, or leave it mismatched with every other app.

## Proposed behavior

Add System to the existing theme choice. With System selected, the app applies a light theme while macOS is in Light mode and a dark theme while it is in Dark mode, both at launch and immediately when the OS appearance changes while the app is open. The saved choice stays System; only the displayed theme changes. The existing manual choices keep working as they do today.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The theme control offers a System choice (for example "System" or "Use system setting") alongside the existing manual choices, and every place that exposes the theme (View → Appearance and Settings → Appearance → Color Theme) shows it.
2. With System selected, the app starts in its light theme when macOS is set to Light and in its dark theme when macOS is set to Dark.

title: Suggestion: optional Nvidia CUDA / NVENC fast lane
author: Jaimetud
body:
Love that FilmCraft uses a wgpu GPU compositor — the vendor-neutral route (Metal/Vulkan/DirectX 12/WebGPU) is the right long-term call, and the same goes for the homegrown Rust codecs.

The gap vs. Premiere Pro for Nvidia users is the Nvidia-specific fast lane: Premiere's Mercury engine leans on CUDA cores for GPU-accelerated effects/rendering, and exports can use NVENC hardware encoding, which is a big real-world time saver on long renders.

Would you consider an optional Nvidia backend that kicks in when an Nvidia GPU is present — CUDA-accelerated effects/compositing where it fits, NVENC hardware encode, and possibly NVDEC decode — while keeping wgpu compositing and the current Rust encoders as the universal fallback? That would keep the cross-platform story intact (AMD/Mac/Intel users lose nothing) while giving Nvidia folks Adobe-class export times.

Happy to test on an Nvidia Windows rig if it ever lands. Thanks for building this in the open.

title: VA-API on NVIDIA: every decoder opens and terminates its own display, freezing the UI and dropping frames at clip changes
author: MrCloudy2
body:
## Summary

Each VA-API `Session` opens its own display and terminates it when it's dropped ([`Session::new`](https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/blob/7b6c134472287db4367fca80bcb498240ba36567/crates/platform/src/vaapi/va.rs#L235) calls `Display::open()`; [`Drop for Display`](https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/blob/7b6c134472287db4367fca80bcb498240ba36567/crates/platform/src/vaapi/va.rs#L198-L204) calls `vaTerminate`). The startup probe also opens one and terminates it straight away ([`probe`](https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/blob/7b6c134472287db4367fca80bcb498240ba36567/crates/platform/src/vaapi/va.rs#L524)).

With Intel's and Mesa's drivers that costs a few milliseconds. NVIDIA's driver (nvidia-vaapi-driver, direct backend) makes a CUDA context per display, and both setting it up and tearing it down are slow. The cost lands on whichever thread creates or drops the decoder: a frame worker at every clip on the timeline, and the UI thread when media is removed (`project.delete` → `MediaPool::remove` → source drop → decoder drop).

## Measurements

Each VA-API call FilmCraft makes when a decoder is created and dropped (a small C program against libva 2.24, 1080p H.264 High, 18 surfaces):

| Call | NVIDIA RTX 3060 (driver 615.71.09, nvidia-vaapi-driver 0.0.18) | Intel UHD 750 (iHD 26.3.5) |
|---|---:|---:|
| `vaInitialize` | **190–310 ms** | 2.3 ms |
| `vaCreateContext` | 11–13 ms | 0.7 ms |
| `vaDestroyContext` | 7–9 ms | 0.05 ms |
| `vaTerminate` | **59–72 ms** | 0.4 ms |

Each NVIDIA display also holds about **104 MB** of video memory (measured with `nvidia-smi`: 104, 416, 832, 1248 MiB for 1, 4, 8, 12 displays).

In the desktop app (`--control`), five 4-second H.264 / HEVC Main 10 clips one after another on V1, 20 s of playback, then `project.delete` of the five clips:

| | NVIDIA | Intel | Hardware decoding off |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `project.delete` round trip (a no-op request: 42 ms) | **650–690 ms** | 43–48 ms | 46–58 ms |
| Frames dropped in 20 s…

title: Timeline transition drag does not preview the destination edge or span
author: DWAA1660
body:
When dragging a transition effect onto a timeline clip, Filmcraft outlines the whole clip without showing whether it will land at the In or Out edge. This is especially ambiguous on short clips.

title: MCP `media_import` input schema is a single `text` string instead of a list of paths
author: sawizzle
body:
## Summary
`filmcraft-cli mcp` advertises `media_import` with the description "Import media files by absolute path" but its inputSchema is `{"properties":{"text":{"type":"string"}},"required":["text"]}`. The engine command it wraps, `file.import`, takes `{"paths":[str],"bin":binId?,"imageSequence":bool?}`.

## Impact
An agent reading the schema has no way to know `text` is a file path, cannot pass several files in one call, and cannot set `bin` or `imageSequence`. Passing one absolute path in `text` does work.

## Repro (Windows 11, filmcraft-cli 0.4.0 MSI)
1. `filmcraft-cli mcp`, then `tools/list` and look at `media_import`
2. `tools/call media_import {"text":"C:/clips/a.mp4"}` -> `{"errors":[],"items":[1]}` (works)

## Suggested fix
Mirror `file.import`: `{"paths":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"minItems":1},"bin":...,"imageSequence":{"type":"boolean"}}`.

title: Stereo 3D: FilmCraft ignores the 3D mark of a clip (we measured it, and we have a patch)
author: danielcamposramos
body:
Hi, I am Daniel Ramos. I work on a stereo 3D edition of SparkyLinux, and I use FilmCraft because it is pure Rust and openly licensed.
I tested FilmCraft 61238bf on Debian testing with synthetic clips we made ourselves: 57 files, each with a blue left eye and an orange right eye, so a swapped or mixed eye shows.
They carry every 3D mark the specifications define: the H.264 frame packing SEI (types 0 to 6), the H.265 one (types 3 to 5), Matroska `StereoMode` 0 to 12, and the MP4 `st3d` box.

**What we measured**
- All 57 import, and no mark changes anything. `StereoMode` is parsed (`stereo_mode=Some(N)`) and used nowhere.

title: Link (clip.link) on several video/audio pairs makes one big link instead of one link per pair (Premiere parity)
author: vibecodingog
body:
**Version:** FilmCraft 0.4.0, macOS (Apple Silicon)

**Command:** Clip > Link (`clip.link`, default Cmd+L, same default as Premiere Pro)

### What happens
Select several cut video clips together with their audio (for example 3 clips on V1 plus the 3 matching clips on A1) after unlinking them, then run Clip > Link. FilmCraft puts **all six clips into one link**. Clicking any one of them now selects the whole run, and moving or trimming one moves all of them.

The cause is in `crates/engine/src/commands.rs`: `clip.link` allocates a single link id and assigns it to every selected clip.

### Expected (Premiere-compatible)
In Premiere Pro a link holds one video clip plus audio clips on separate tracks ([Adobe docs](https://helpx.adobe.com/premiere/desktop/add-audio-effects/basic-audio-editing/link-audio-and-video-clips.html)), so a multi-clip link like this can't happen there. Editors who unlink a batch of cuts and relink them expect each video clip to go back with its own audio.

Suggested behavior when the selection contains more than one video clip: create **one link per video clip**, containing that video clip plus the selected audio clips that overlap it in time (ideally from the same source media). Selections with a single video clip would keep today's behavior.

### Repro via the CLI
```
filmcraft-cli --project p.fcproj exec clip.link '{"clips":[v1,a1,v2,a2,v3,a3]}'   # all already linked: unlinks all
filmcraft-cli --project p.fcproj exec clip.link '{"clips":[v1,a1,v2,a2,v3,a3]}'   # links all six into ONE link
```
`inspect sequence` then shows the same `link` id on all six items.

### Workaround we use
After Link, unlink the selection and call `clip.link` once per video/audio pair over the control port. A native per-pair Link would make this unnecessary.

title: FilmCraft crashes on startup with Intel UHD Graphics (igvk64.dll)
author: SavioN38
body:
**NOTE**: I had experienced this issue and used AI to assist me in fixing it. Once I got it working I thought I should mention the issue here. The below content is written by AI that assisted me.
### Description

FilmCraft crashes immediately on startup on my Windows 11 ThinkPad T14 Gen 1. The loading cursor appears briefly, then disappears without opening the editor.

The issue occurs repeatedly with the installed version and the portable build.

### System information

* **OS:** Windows 11, build 26200
* **Laptop:** Lenovo ThinkPad T14 Gen 1
* **GPU:** Intel UHD Graphics
* **Intel graphics driver:** 31.0.101.2137
* **Installed FilmCraft version:** 0.4.0
* **Portable version tested:** 0.4.0 (Windows x64)

### Crash details

Windows Reliability Monitor reports:

* **Event:** APPCRASH
* **Faulting application:** `filmcraft.exe`
* **Faulting module:** `igvk64.dll`
* **Module version:** 31.0.101.2137
* **Exception code:** `0xc0000005`
* **Exception offset:** `0000000000630e61`

### Steps to reproduce

1. Launch FilmCraft normally on Windows 11 with Intel UHD Graphics.
2. The loading cursor appears briefly.
3. The application exits without displaying its window.
4. Windows Reliability Monitor records an APPCRASH involving `igvk64.dll`.

### Workaround discovered

Launching the portable 0.4.0 build from PowerShell with the following commands allows the editor to open:

```powershell
$env:WGPU_BACKEND = "dx12"
.\filmcraft.exe
```

Without this environment variable, the portable build did not open.

### Expected behaviour

FilmCraft should launch normally on a supported Windows system, or report a useful error if the graphics backend cannot initialize.

### Actual behaviour

The application exits during startup, and Windows reports an access violation in Intel's Vulkan driver module.

Could this be a graphics-backend compatibility issue? Please let me know if additional logs or diagnostics would help.

Thank you!

title: Dropping files from the OS onto the Timeline should place them there, with a drop preview
author: rangamitch
body:
Dragging video files from the file manager onto the Timeline only imported them into the Project bin; you then had to drag them onto the timeline a second time. Premiere places them where you drop.

Related: #171 (\"import media by drag and drop does not work\", empty report), #483 (creating new tracks by dropping media where none exists; not covered here).

**Wanted**
- Files dropped on the Timeline are imported and placed (overwrite) at the snapped drop point on the track under the cursor, chained end to end when several are dropped.
- While dragging, the Timeline previews where they would land.
- A setting to turn it off (default on), so a drop can stay a plain bin import.

**Cause of the Windows part**
winit sends no cursor events while files are dragged in from the OS (it only reports hovered and dropped files), so the UI had no drop position. The desktop app now reads the cursor from the OS (`GetCursorPos`) through a host hook. Other platforms still use the last pointer position egui saw; whether macOS and Linux report the cursor during a file drag is not verified.

**Implemented in** #517:
- setting `timeline.dropImportToTimeline` (default on)
- drop placement and the hover preview
- engine, UI and headless drop tests

Not covered: dropping onto a spot with no track (#483), and preview width using the real clip length (durations are unknown until import, so the placeholder is a fixed width).

title: Anamorphic clips (non-square pixels) display squeezed
author: LloydNicholson
body:
A clip with non-square pixels (for example 1440x1080 with 4:3 pixels: HDV, or 2x/1.33x anamorphic footage) shows squeezed. The demuxers read the clip's pixel aspect ratio, but nothing after import uses it.

**Repro:**
```sh
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc2=s=1440x1080:r=30:d=5 -vf setsar=4/3 -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p anamorphic.mp4
```
Import it. Then use New Sequence From Clip, or overwrite it into a 1920x1080 sequence, or open it in the Source monitor.

**Expected:** a 16:9 picture. New Sequence From Clip gives a 1440x1080 sequence with 4:3 pixels. In a 1920x1080 square-pixel sequence the clip fills the frame, and both monitors display it at 16:9.

**Actual:**
- New Sequence From Clip makes a 1440x1080 sequence with `par: [1, 1]`.
- In a 1920x1080 sequence the clip is pillarboxed at 1440 wide.
- The Source and Program monitors show a 4:3 picture.

**Cause:** the ratio is parsed (`crates/codecs/src/mp4.rs` gives `par (4,3)`), but `default_seq_settings_for` (`crates/engine/src/commands.rs`) doesn't copy it, and `motion_matrix` (`crates/render/src/lib.rs`) sizes clips from storage pixels.

**Environment:** macOS 26.6.2 arm64, filmcraft `main` @ ef6391d (0.4.0).

Fix in #445.

title: HDR and colour info wrong for MP4/MKV files without a container colour tag
author: LloydNicholson
body:
MP4 files without a `colr` box report BT.709 limited range whatever their stream says. ffmpeg doesn't write `colr` by default, so this covers most ffmpeg-made files. Matroska files without a `Colour` element have the same problem. The picture itself decodes correctly; the colour info (`media.colorInfo`), HDR detection and the Interpret Footage defaults are wrong.

**Repro:**
```sh
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc2=s=1920x1080:r=30:d=2 -c:v libx265 -tag:v hvc1 -pix_fmt yuv420p10le \
  -color_primaries bt2020 -color_trc smpte2084 -colorspace bt2020nc \
  -x265-params colorprim=bt2020:transfer=smpte2084:colormatrix=bt2020nc hevc_pq.mp4
```
Import it and run `media.colorInfo`.

**Expected:** `rec2100-pq`, `hdr: true`. That is what the same stream gives when remuxed with `-movflags +write_colr`.

**Actual:** `rec709`, `hdr: false`. Also:
- A full-range H.264 file (`-pix_fmt yuvj420p`) reports limited range.
- A BT.601 SD file (720x480, smpte170m) reports BT.709 primaries.

**Cause:** `color_from` in `crates/codecs/src/mp4.rs` only reads `colr` (or `vpcC` / `apvC`). Without one it falls back to the size-based defaults, instead of reading the colour from the stream (SPS VUI in `avcC` / `hvcC`, or the AV1 sequence header).

**Environment:** macOS 26.6.2 arm64, filmcraft `main` @ ef6391d (0.4.0), ffmpeg 8.0.1.

Fix in #446.

title: Timeline and monitor timecodes: drag to scrub, click to type a time
author: ReReddo
body:
The big blue timecode at the top left of the Timeline, and the current-time timecodes of the Program and Source monitors, are display-only. In Premiere you can drag them to move the playhead, or click them to type a time. Here nothing happens on drag or click.

**Proposed behaviour** (the same for all three):

- Hovering over the timecode shows a horizontal-resize cursor.
- Dragging left or right moves that panel's playhead live, 1 frame per pixel (Shift for 10 frames per pixel). It stops at the start (`00:00:00:00`).
- A click without dragging turns the timecode into a text field with the whole value selected. Enter goes to the typed time. Escape cancels. Clicking elsewhere commits.
- Typed input goes through the existing `parse_timecode`, so `01:02:03:04`, `1000` (= 10 s) and relative `+15` / `-1.00` all work. Invalid input shows an error in the status bar and leaves the playhead where it was.
- The Timeline and Program monitor use `playhead.set`; the Source monitor uses `source.setPlayhead`. Every new widget gets an automation id.

**Coordination:** #265 adds a right-click menu on the monitor timecode. This change only uses left click and drag, so the two should fit together.

I'm working on this and will open a PR.

title: Project panel: drag in empty space to marquee-select, in List, Icon and Freeform views
author: ReReddo
body:
In the Project panel you can only select clips by clicking (with Shift/Ctrl to extend). Dragging from empty space does nothing, in any view. In Premiere, dragging from empty space draws a selection rectangle, which matters when picking many clips at once.

**Proposed behaviour** (the same in List, Icon and Freeform views):

- Dragging from empty space draws a selection rectangle. Every clip whose row or card it touches is selected when you let go, and the selection updates live while dragging.
- A plain drag replaces the selection. Shift or Ctrl adds to it.
- Escape while dragging cancels and keeps the previous selection.
- The selection goes through the existing `project.select` command. The rectangle gets an automation id.

**Limit:** the Project panel tracks one selected bin (`selected_bin`), so the rectangle selects clips but not several bins. Multi-selecting bins would be a separate, larger change.

title: Headless round-trip fidelity: file.import merges into pre-existing project content; no empty-project start
author: NkAntony777
body:
**Version**: filmcraft-cli 0.4.0 (windows-x64 portable)

**What happened**: In headless mode (with `--demo`), `file.import` merges the imported timeline into the pre-existing demo project content, so `file.exportMedia` output is not a faithful reproduction of the imported timeline (export reflects demo content + import, not import alone). `file.newProject` does replace the demo content (open_sequences goes from `[21,…]` to `[]` — verified), but import semantics remain "merge into current project", and there is no documented "import into a fresh/empty project" or "import replacing current" form.

**Expected**: Either an `import` mode/flag for faithful from-scratch reproduction, or documented guidance for the empty-project-start workflow headlessly.

**Why it matters**: Round-trip parity checks (import → export → compare) are the natural acceptance test for agent-driven editing; merge-by-default makes them ambiguous.

**Repro**: headless session: `file.newProject` → `file.import <timeline>` → `file.exportMedia` → compare export duration/content against source timeline span.

title: [Feature Request]: Add support for importing AVI (Audio Video Interleave) container format
author: Aedan-S
body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

I am unable to import legacy video footage saved in the AVI (.avi) container format into FilmCraft. Since FilmCraft uses custom native decoders instead of FFmpeg, these files currently fail to load, forcing a tedious external transcoding workaround (e.g., via HandBrake) into MP4/MOV before editing can begin.

### Describe the solution you'd like

I would like FilmCraft to support parsing the AVI container format for video imports.
• Scope: This request is strictly for the container parser to read the file structure and extract the underlying audio/video streams.
• Codec Alignment: Once parsed, the video stream should map to FilmCraft's existing native decoders (such as H.264/AVC or MPEG-4 if supported by the engine).

### Describe alternatives you've considered

• External Transcoding: Manually converting .avi files to .mp4 (H.264) or .mov (ProRes) prior to import. This wastes time and disk space.
• FFmpeg wrapper: While bundling FFmpeg would solve this, I understand it contradicts FilmCraft’s clean-room, bit-exact Rust decoder philosophy. Adding a native AVI demuxer keeps the binary clean.

### Additional context

Many archival pipelines, retro gameplay captures, and legacy cameras still rely heavily on the AVI wrapper. Adding native demuxing for it would significantly lower the friction for editors migrating older projects into FilmCraft via AAF or XML timelines.
