title: Paste images and copied files from the system clipboard into the Timeline and Project panel
author: ReReddo
body:
Ctrl+V only pastes clips copied inside FilmCraft. A screenshot, an image copied from a browser, or files copied in Explorer / Finder can't be pasted; they have to be saved or found on disk and then imported or dragged in.

**Proposed behaviour**

- **Timeline:** Ctrl+V with an image on the system clipboard imports it and places it at the playhead for the default still duration (Settings ▸ Timeline), **without touching any clip already there**. It goes on the first video track, from the targeted one upward, that is empty for that span; if none is, a new video track is added on top. So an image pasted over footage sits above it as an overlay. Ctrl+Shift+V (Paste Insert) inserts it on the targeted track instead, pushing later clips right, as with clips. Undo takes it off the Timeline (and removes a track added for it).
- **Copied files** (videos, audio, images copied in Explorer / Finder) paste the same way, end to end in the order they were copied, on free tracks. Audio goes on the first audio track that's free for its span, else a new one.
- **Project panel:** Ctrl+V imports into the current bin without placing anything.
- **Whichever was copied last wins.** Copying clips in FilmCraft already writes their names to the system clipboard, so an image or files on the clipboard mean they were copied after any clips, and Ctrl+V pastes those. Otherwise it pastes clips as today.
- **Where a pasted image is saved:** projects reference media by path, so the image is written as `Pasted Image <n>.png`. It uses the same place voice-over recordings use: Project Settings ▸ Scratch Disks ▸ Captured Audio and Video, else next to the project file, else the data directory for an unsaved project.

Not covered: the web build, where the browser's clipboard API works differently.

I'm working on this and will open a PR.

title: Feature request: Continuous video thumbnails (filmstrip) across the full clip width in the Timeline
author: tradmangh
body:
## Summary

Add an option that shows **continuous video thumbnails**: a filmstrip of frames across the full width of each video clip in the Timeline. Today only the clip's first frame is shown.

## Current behaviour

The **Show Video Thumbnails** checkbox in the Timeline wrench (settings) menu is a plain on/off switch. When it is on, each enabled video clip draws **one** thumbnail at its head: the frame at `source_in`, left-aligned below the name band. The clip's width doesn't change this. Even when a clip is hundreds of points wide at high zoom, the rest of the clip body stays a flat colour.

Code references (at `5a56844`):

- `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/timeline.rs` ~L635–663: `// head thumbnail (video)` makes a single `app.thumbnail(ctx, thumb_item, rate.snap(it.source_in), 160)` call per clip.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/timeline.rs` ~L1182: `ui.checkbox(&mut app.ui.timeline.show_thumbnails, tl!("Show Video Thumbnails"))`.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/state.rs` ~L192: `show_thumbnails: bool`.

## Motivation

- **Visual navigation:** in long clips (interviews, B-roll, screen recordings, long takes), editors find shot changes, actions and cut points by scanning the picture in the Timeline. They shouldn't have to scrub the Program monitor to do it.
- **Expected NLE behaviour:** professional editors usually offer *Head*, *Head and Tail* and *Continuous* thumbnail display modes. Editors coming from those tools expect a filmstrip view, and FilmCraft's goal is a familiar timeline.
- **Better use of space:** at high zoom and with tall video tracks, most of the clip body is empty today.

| Mode | Behaviour |

title: Dev builds fill the disk: 62 GB target/ (full DWARF x ~50 test binaries + never-GC'd incremental)
author: ahmedhosnypro
body:
## What happened

On 2026-10-10 a single day of building filled the disk (370 GB, 100% full). `target/` measured **62 GB**, all of it from one fresh build day — not stale accumulation:

| Component | Size | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 43 `ui-egui` `*_ui.rs` integration-test binaries | **41.6 GB** | each ~970 MB, statically linking the whole app stack (egui/wgpu/naga/vello + the codec crates); measured on one binary: 858 MB of 970 MB is `.debug_*` DWARF (`.debug_info` 332 MB, `.debug_loc` 254 MB, `.debug_str` 205 MB — `.debug_line` only 44 MB) |
| other debug executables + 4 bench examples | ~6.6 GB | same full-DWARF amplification |
| `target/debug/incremental` | 7.0 GB | 209 session dirs from one day; cargo never GCs them |
| `target/release` (a `cargo test --workspace --release` gate run) | 5.3 GB | |
| dep rlib/rmeta debuginfo | ~3.6 GB | |

**Root cause:** the workspace `[profile.dev]` sets only `opt-level`, so cargo's default `debug = 2` (full DWARF) applies to all 47 workspace crates, all 695 lockfile packages, and every one of ~50 test/example binaries that each statically link the whole UI stack.

## Proposed fix

- `[profile.dev]` / `[profile.test]` `debug = "line-tables-only"` — backtraces keep file:line at roughly one fifth of the size; `[profile.dev.package."*"] debug = false` drops third-party debuginfo (the Cargo book: `"*"` never matches workspace members)
- `[build] incremental = false` in `.cargo/config.toml` — covers agents, worktrees, scripts and gates (env exports missed those); `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=1` for a one-off session
- `cargo xtask target-size [--check]` (30 GB cap, `TARGET_CAP_GB`) and `cargo xtask clean-target [--incremental|--debug|--release|--dbg]` hygiene commands
- `[profile.dbg]` (inherits dev, full DWARF) as the opt-in for a debugging session that needs variable inspection
- docs: `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/contributing.md` §2 "Target-dir hygiene"

The same recipe is proven in the sibling projects (harhaial-desktop 66 → 15 GB, IronRouter 9.5 GB → 7…

title: Support decoding H.264 High 10 and High 4:2:2 (e.g. Panasonic Lumix 4K 10-bit 4:2:2 MOV) - currently black frames with no error
author: 4papuce
body:
## Summary

Camera material in H.264 **High 4:2:2 10-bit** (Panasonic Lumix S5/S1 MOV mode, `H264_422_LongGOP`,
4K25/30/60) and **High 10** imports but every video frame fails to decode: the monitors and timeline
show black while the PCM audio track plays. No error is shown — `filmcraft_h264::Sps::check_supported`
rejects the stream ("chroma_format_idc 2 (only 4:2:0 is implemented)" / "only 8-bit is implemented")
and the render pipeline silently drops failed frames.

## Reproduce

1. `filmcraft-cli import XYZ.MOV` (Lumix S5 4K25 4:2:2 10-bit LongGOP) — import succeeds.
2. Create a sequence from the clip and render/preview: the picture is entirely black; audio plays.
3. `filmcraft-cli bench-decode XYZ.MOV --frames 3` →
   `decode error: unsupported: chroma_format_idc 2 (only 4:2:0 is implemented)`.

## Expected

Decode H.264 High 10 (10-bit 4:2:0) and High 4:2:2 (8- and 10-bit) natively, bit-exactly, with
CAVLC and CABAC, and report unsupported formats as a visible "media unreadable" slate instead of
black frames.

## Notes

- The decoder's README already sketches the extension ("Extending to High 10 and 4:2:2").
- The silent-black failure mode deserves its own fix: a failed frame decode should surface the
  existing offline/unreadable slate or a status message.
- Hardware decode does not cover these formats on consumer GPUs (VA-API/DXVA/VideoToolbox H.264 is
  4:2:0 8-bit), so the software decoder must handle them.

LLM used: Xiaomi MiMo v2.6 pro on deepseek-harness

## Status
- **Native High 10 / High 4:2:2 decoding** - PR #629 (in review).
- **No more silent black frames** - being fixed separately in #762  (thanks!): frames a
  decoder reports as unsupported will render the existing MEDIA UNREADABLE slate, and the item
  shows as Unreadable, instead of a black picture with playing audio clearly informing the user what is wrong

title: Preview renders entirely on the CPU (GPU at 0 %, CPU at 100 %) when wgpu falls back to a software rasterizer and nothing says so
author: 4papuce
body:
## Summary

On machines where wgpu cannot reach a GPU, the whole preview pipeline runs on the CPU and the
app gives no visible explanation: GPU usage reads 0 %, CPU usage spikes to 100 %, and playback is
laggy. It looks like a renderer bug; it is actually a silent fallback.

## What happens

wgpu's instance cannot open the GPU device (`/dev/dri` missing in a container/sandbox, missing
`video`/`render` group, broken or missing Mesa/Vulkan drivers) and falls back to a **software
rasterizer** (llvmpipe / SwiftShader). The log says only:

```
wgpu_hal::vulkan::instance: Failed to detect any valid GPUs in the current config
egui_wgpu: Software rasterizer detected - loss of performance expected. backend: Gl, device_type: Cpu, name: "llvmpipe (LLVM >
```

FilmCraft then happily treats that CPU rasterizer as its "GPU compositor" (`set_wgpu` accepts it:
llvmpipe satisfies the `Rgba16Float` capability checks), so:

- every monitor frame is composited through WGSL running on the CPU rasterizer — slower than the
  native CPU compositor;
- `perf.stats` and the UI give no hint that there is no GPU;
- hardware decoding is also unavailable in the same situations (`no DRM render node`), so 4K
  software decode on top of CPU compositing makes preview unusable.

## Reproduce

1. Run FilmCraft in an environment without GPU device access (e.g. a container without `/dev/dri`,
   or a VM without GPU passthrough).
2. Import any 4K clip, open it in the Program monitor and play.
3. GPU utilisation stays at 0 %, one CPU core per worker is saturated, playback is laggy. Only the
   log excerpt above explains it.

## Expected

- The app should not present a software rasterizer as GPU acceleration: composite with the native
  CPU compositor instead (it is faster than wgpu-on-llvmpipe).
- The user should be told plainly and a status-bar message such as "GPU acceleration is unavailable;
  preview renders on the CPU (software rasterizer (llvmpipe, Cpu))" — so the symptom is
  self-explanatory.

title: Program monitor: on-screen transform handles for Motion and Transform
author: ReReddo
body:
Position, Scale, Rotation and Anchor Point can only be changed by dragging or typing their values in Effect Controls or Properties. In Premiere you can also change them directly on the picture in the Program monitor, which is often faster, especially for placing and sizing an overlay.

**Proposed behaviour**

- **Showing the handles:** selecting the Motion effect in Effect Controls (clicking its header or one of its properties: Position, Scale, Rotation, Anchor Point) shows a bounding box around the clip's picture in the Program monitor, with eight handles and the anchor point. Double-clicking the picture in the Program monitor selects Motion too, as in Premiere.
- **Clicking a header** selects the effect instead of twirling it open or shut; only the arrow on the left twirls, as in Premiere.
- **Move:** dragging inside the box changes Position.
- **Scale:** dragging a handle changes Scale. With Uniform Scale off, the side handles change only Scale Width and the top and bottom handles only the height.
- **Rotate:** dragging just outside a corner (the pointer turns into a rotate cursor) changes Rotation.
- **Anchor point:** dragging the anchor point moves it without moving the picture: Position changes by the same amount.
- **Keyframes:** a drag sets the value at the playhead, so a property with its stopwatch on gets a keyframe added or updated there; with the stopwatch off the value just changes.
- **Undo and Escape:** one drag is one undo step, and Escape during a drag puts everything back, as for other drags (#580).
- **The Transform effect** (Video Effects ▸ Transform ▸ Transform) gets the same handles for its own Position, Scale Height / Scale Width, Rotation and Anchor Point when it is selected.

Masks already edit on the Program monitor the same way (select the mask, drag on the picture), so the handles would follow that.

I'm working on this and will open a PR.

title: Effect Controls: draggable divider between the effects and the keyframe area; scroll the whole panel

body:
In Effect Controls the split between the effect list and the keyframe area is fixed, so long property names get cut off or the keyframe area stays too narrow, depending on the panel size. Scrolling is also tied to the effect list: the scrollbar sits in the middle of the panel, and the mouse wheel does nothing over the keyframe area, although the keyframe rows scroll with the list.

title: Effect Controls: zoom bar under the keyframe area, as in the Timeline
author: ReReddo
body:
The keyframe area in Effect Controls always shows the whole clip, so on a long clip keyframes a few frames apart sit on top of each other and are hard to place or drag precisely. Premiere puts the same zoom bar under the keyframe area as under the Timeline.

**Proposed behaviour**

- **Zoom bar:** a bar under the keyframe area, behaving exactly like the Timeline's: drag either end to zoom in or out (the view stays centred on the playhead while an end is dragged, as for the Timeline and monitor zoom bars), drag the middle to scroll, click beside it to jump there.
- **Everything follows the zoom:** the time ruler, the keyframe diamonds, the playhead, and dragging keyframes and the playhead in the lane. Zoomed in, the ruler shows finer ticks, down to single frames.
- **Fully zoomed out** shows the whole clip, as today, and is where a newly selected clip starts.

**Implementation note:** the Timeline's `zoom_scrollbar` (`panels/timeline.rs`) works on the Timeline's own view state. I'd turn it into a shared widget that takes the view it zooms and scrolls, so both panels use the same code and look. Two open items touch that function: #436 (anchor zoom on the playhead) and #317 (scaling the timeline view by dragging the bar's ends). The shared widget should keep their behaviour, and whichever lands second rebases onto the other.

I'm working on this and will open a PR.

title: **Title: [macOS] Voice-over recording blocked by missing microphone privacy declaration and audio-input entitlement**
author: Lushere
body:
### Description
FilmCraft v0.5.0 cannot access any microphone on my Apple Silicon Mac M4.

Neither the built-in Mac microphone nor an external HyperX microphone works for voice-over recording.

FilmCraft never requests microphone permission and does not appear under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone.

### Diagnostics

The following command:

`/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Print :NSMicrophoneUsageDescription" "/Applications/FilmCraft.app/Contents/Info.plist"`

Returns:

`Print: Entry, ":NSMicrophoneUsageDescription", Does Not Exist`

Inspecting the application entitlements with `codesign` returns an empty dictionary:

`<plist version="1.0"><dict></dict></plist>`

The previous v0.4.0 installation was also confirmed to use Hardened Runtime (`flags=0x10000(runtime)`).

### Expected behavior
FilmCraft should request microphone access through macOS and allow the user to select an available input device for voice-over recording.

### Suggested fix
- Add `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` to the macOS app's Info.plist.
- Include `com.apple.security.device.audio-input = true` in the signing entitlements.
- Re-sign, notarize and test the distributed macOS application.

The issue was reproducible on both v0.4.0 and v0.5.0.

I'm Hanzo main.

title: fix(cli): space-separated GPU rendering option loses its value
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

The documented `export --gpu-rendering auto|off` spelling does not pass its value to the export command. With the option after the output filename, the CLI silently omits the requested setting. With `--gpu-rendering off` before the filename, it treats `off` as the output path and refuses an otherwise valid WAV export. The equals spelling works.

## Steps to reproduce

Use the tested CLI identified below, available as `filmcraft-cli` on `PATH`. Run these commands in a new writable directory. The built-in demo provides an active sequence, and `data` isolates the export-preset library. The WAV format and 0.1-second range keep the exports small and require no external media or GPU adapter.

```sh
mkdir data
filmcraft-cli --demo --data-dir data export --gpu-rendering off requested.wav --start 0 --end 0.1
echo "exit=$?"

title: fix(gpu): Extract exceeds the CPU parity tolerance on Apple silicon
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

The existing GPU effect-stage parity test fails for Extract with Black Input Level 90, White Input Level 160, Invert enabled and the default Softness 0. The GPU working-image readback exceeds the test's normalized CPU-reference tolerance on the tested Apple-silicon environment. This leaves the repository's effect parity check failing for contributors in that environment. The observation does not establish a perceptible difference in a preview or exported video.

## Steps to reproduce

Use the source baseline and build environment under Runtime or environment, with a working GPU adapter. Run this single existing library test from the repository root; it generates its own 67×41 half-float-representable premultiplied RGBA fixture and needs no media file, project, GUI or preference changes.

```sh
CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 cargo test --locked -p filmcraft-gpu --lib \
  fx_tests::gpu_effects_match_cpu_exactly -- --exact --nocapture
```

The test requests the default wgpu adapter and device. A run that prints `no GPU adapter; skipping` does not reproduce the case. The verified run reached GPU effect-image readback and the parity assertion.

## Expected behavior

The effect stage must satisfy its existing CPU-reference parity criterion for this supported Extract configuration. The test compares each CPU/GPU component using `d = abs(cpu - gpu) / (1 + abs(cpu))`. It counts components with `d > 0.02` as threshold flips; for Extract, at most 1% of components may be flips. The maximum `d` among the remaining components must be at most `1e-4`. With zero flips in this case, a reported maximum of `1.33e-4` must fail that criterion.

The effect definition supports both input levels within 0–255, Invert as a boolean and Softness 0 within its 0–100 range. The GPU-capability guard accepts the evaluated finite parameters. The larger 8-bit composited-image tolerance is a separate contract and does not replace this working-image criterion.

title: macOS: double-clicking a .fcproj in Finder fails with "FilmCraft cannot open files of this type"
author: impostazioni
body:
## Summary

On macOS, double-clicking a `.fcproj` project in Finder (or using Open With ▸ FilmCraft) doesn't open it. macOS shows:

> The document "projectname.fcproj" could not be opened. FilmCraft cannot open files of this type.

Projects only open from inside the app or when passed on the command line (`filmcraft path/to/project.fcproj`).

## Cause

There are two gaps, and both need fixing.

1. **The bundle doesn't claim the document type.** `packaging/macos/Info.plist.in` exports the UTI `ai.storyteller.filmcraft.project` for the `fcproj` extension (`UTExportedTypeDeclarations`), but has no `CFBundleDocumentTypes` entry naming it in `LSItemContentTypes` with a role. Launch Services therefore knows the type but no app that can open it, and it refuses the double-click with the dialog above. The key has never existed in the template (`git log -p -- packaging/macos/Info.plist.in`). #100 renamed the exported extension from `.pcraft` to `.fcproj` but didn't add document types.

2. **The app doesn't handle macOS open-document events.** Files are only read from `std::env::args()` (`apps/filmcraft/src/main.rs`). When Finder opens a document, Launch Services doesn't put the path in argv. It sends the app an open-documents Apple Event (`application:openURLs:` on the app delegate), both on a cold launch and when the app is already running. Nothing in FilmCraft handles that event, and winit 0.30 doesn't surface it to the app. So with (1) fixed alone, the app would launch with no project, or do nothing if it's already open.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install the macOS build (the bundle produced by `packaging/macos/package.sh` / the release `.dmg`) in `/Applications`.
2. Save a project, e.g. `test.fcproj`.
3. Double-click it in Finder.

Expected: FilmCraft opens the project, starting the app first if needed.
Actual: the "cannot open files of this type" dialog.

## Environment

- macOS on Apple silicon (arm64), `main` at `7bd7621` (0.5.0).

title: macOS: ~3.2 GB held from launch: the CJK system-font fallback reads every system font face's whole file and keeps it
author: BlaineMoore
body:
## Summary

Since #363, FilmCraft on macOS holds about **3.2 GB** of heap from its first frame, with no project open, and keeps it for the life of the process. A build of `main` from before #363 started at about 33 MB on the same machine.

`cjk::system_font()` runs on every launch (from `theme::install` → `cjk::install`), whatever the interface language. Its preferred-family shortcut can't match on macOS, so it falls back to checking every non-italic system face for the sample characters. Each check goes through `Face::has_char` → `Face::glyph` → `Face::bytes`, which `std::fs::read`s the face's whole file into a `OnceLock` that is never released. Faces from the same `.ttc` don't share the read, so a collection is read once per face.

It shipped in v0.5.0 (the tag contains `34cf600`) and is still on `main`.

Related: #363 (where it came from), #547 and #40 (the CJK fallback work), #41 and #55 (desktop memory budget). #655 is a different start-up problem (a crash on 0.4.0, before #363).

## Environment

- `main` at `73723151ce9c004638346013cc1cc3b21e9ce484`, `cargo build --release -p filmcraft`, Rust 1.99.0
- macOS 27.0 (26A428), Apple M2, 24 GB, English interface
- 429 font files in `/System/Library/Fonts` and `/Library/Fonts` (0.95 GB on disk)

## Steps to reproduce

```bash
filmcraft --empty &
sleep 10
vmmap --summary $(pgrep -x filmcraft) | grep "Physical footprint"
```

To rule out user-installed fonts, run it with an empty home folder. `DirectorySource::system()` takes `~/Library/Fonts` from `HOME`:

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/emptyhome && HOME=/tmp/emptyhome filmcraft --empty &
```

## Expected

Start-up costs tens of MB, as it did before #363. At most, the one face actually chosen for the fallback stays in memory.

## Actual

| launch | physical footprint after 10 s |
| --- | --- |
| `main` before #363 (`5231852`), same machine | 33 MB |
| `7372315`, normal `HOME` (699 more fonts in `~/Library/Fonts`) | 3.3 GB (peak 3.4 GB) |
| `7372315`, empty `HOME` (system fonts…

title: Optical Flow time interpolation renders as Frame Blending
author: vangel76
body:
Premiere Pro parity, docs/gaps.md G18: a speed-changed clip set to Time Interpolation > Optical Flow currently renders exactly like Frame Blending (crossfade of the two neighbouring source frames, so moving objects show double images; see the TODO on `filmcraft_render::interpolation_blend`). Expected (Premiere): Optical Flow synthesises the in-between frame by estimating per-pixel motion between the two source frames and warping both towards the in-between time, so a moving object appears once, at its interpolated position.

Plan: dense coarse-to-fine Lucas–Kanade flow (forward and backward) on a reduced-resolution luma pyramid, intermediate flow from the two (linear motion approximation), bilinear warp of both frames and an occlusion-aware blend that falls back to Frame Blending where the flows disagree. CPU path in crates/render, deterministic, tested on synthetic moving shapes.

title: Matroska AAC / AC-3 audio starts up to 16 samples off: CodecDelay rounded to 1 ms
author: vangel76
body:
Premiere Pro parity, docs/gaps.md G10: audio imported from Matroska must line up sample-exactly with the source, as it does from MP4.

ffmpeg writes the encoder priming as `CodecDelay` (e.g. 1024 samples = 21.333 ms for AAC at 48 kHz, 256 samples = 5.805 ms for AC-3 at 44.1 kHz). Our demuxer subtracts it from the block timestamps rounded to the 1 ms `TimestampScale`, and for AAC, MPEG audio and AC-3 the packet starts are then anchored on that rounded timestamp, so the whole track plays 16 samples (AAC 48 kHz), 10 samples (AAC 44.1 kHz) or 8 samples (AC-3 44.1 kHz) late against ffmpeg's decode. Opus already undoes the rounding and trims the exact delay; the other codecs should too.

Expected: the decoded track matches ffmpeg's decode with zero sample offset.

I'm working on this and will open a PR.

title: feat(packaging): provide reliable CLI access with desktop releases
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Provide a supported CLI invocation with FilmCraft desktop distributions on Windows, Linux, and macOS, so people, scripts, and agents can edit a timeline or export a sequence through a documented invocation.

## Problem to solve

Desktop acquisition does not imply a command is available in a shell. Windows packages include `filmcraft-cli.exe` without adding it to PATH. Linux native packages install the CLI in `/usr/bin`, while AppImage and Flatpak contain it internally. The macOS desktop DMG and CLI ZIP are separate downloads. Users need reliable CLI invocation without an agent client.

## Proposed behavior

Each supported desktop distribution should supply a usable CLI or an integrated route to install its matching CLI, with a documented invocation. Use the actual executable path, a supported launcher, or a sandbox command override. Optional shell exposure is allowed; invocation must work without global PATH changes.

Preserve native Linux commands and document Windows install paths and portable executables. Make the CLI accessible to AppImage and Flatpak users through supported invocations. For macOS, include the CLI with desktop acquisition or provide an integrated matching install route.

## Acceptance criteria

- The same advertised invocation can initialize MCP and discover tools without an agent client or document edit; the temporary server stops after the check.

title: Number fields: type a calculation (100*2, 200/3) and get its result
author: ReReddo
body:
When you type into a number field (the blue values you can drag in Effect Controls and Properties, or a field in a dialog such as Speed/Duration or Sequence Settings), only a plain number is accepted. To halve a scale, double a duration or split a width into thirds, you work it out elsewhere and type the result; anything else is thrown away and the old value stays.

**Proposed behaviour**

- Every number field accepts a calculation and applies its result when you press Enter or click away: `100*2` gives 200, `1920/3` gives 640, `(50+10)*1.5` gives 90.
- `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, brackets, decimals and negative numbers.
- The field opens with its current value, so adding `/3` after it divides that value by three.
- With the value selected, typing a calculation that starts with `*` or `/` applies it to the current value: `*2` doubles it, `/3` divides it by three. (`+` and `-` at the start stay signs, so `-10` is minus ten.)
- A field's unit can be typed or left out: `50%*2` reads as `50*2` in a percentage field.
- A result outside the field's range is clamped to it, as a typed number is today. Something that isn't a calculation, or a division by zero, leaves the value as it was.

I'm working on this and will open a PR.

title: Audio playback recovers when the output stream drops (ALSA xrun / POLLERR, unplugged device) instead of going silent
author: vangel76
body:
Premiere Pro parity, docs/gaps.md G17: when the audio driver hiccups or the output device goes away, Premiere keeps playing with sound (it re-opens the device, or switches to the system default). FilmCraft goes silent for the rest of the playback.

What happens now (apps/filmcraft/src/audio.rs): the cpal error callback sets `failed` on the first stream error of any kind, `played_frames()` then returns `None`, and the UI stops the stream and continues without sound ("Audio output failed: playing without sound"). Many of those errors are transient: cpal's ALSA backend reports `alsa::poll() returned POLLERR` (an xrun the backend does not recover from, so the stream stops consuming samples), spurious poll returns and short writes through the error callback and keeps the stream alive. This matches the reports in #23 (a second or two of audio, then POLLERR and silence while the meters keep moving), #602 and possibly #605 / #106.

Expected: a stream error triggers a bounded restart of the output stream on the same device (or the default device if the chosen one is gone) with the same sample rate and channel count, keeping the playback clock and the play-ahead mixer position, so sound resumes within a few milliseconds. Only when the restart fails, or errors keep recurring, does playback fall back to the wall clock without sound, as today. Transient errors that do not stop the stream no longer silence it. The audio callback must never panic (a panicking fill outputs silence).

I'm working on this and will open a PR.

title: AV1 software decode: run deblocking, CDEF and loop restoration in parallel row bands
author: vangel76
body:
Premiere Pro parity, docs/gaps.md G16 (performance): AV1 software decode is slow. The in-loop post-filters (deblocking 7.14, CDEF 7.15, loop restoration 7.17) run on one thread per frame (`postfilter::apply` has an unused `_pool` parameter). On a single-tile 1080p SVT-AV1 GOP they are about a third of a frame's time (CDEF 6.6 ms + restoration 5.1 ms + deblock 0.9 ms of ~35 ms), and because a frame's references are waited for as whole frames, that serial tail sits on the critical path of every frame that references it.

Expected: the three filters run in row bands on the decoder's existing rayon pool (no new dependency), with output bit-identical to the single-threaded path and to libdav1d; before/after timings measured with `crates/av1/tests/perf.rs` on ffmpeg-made fixtures.

I'm working on this and will open a PR.

title: h264: High 4:2:2 10-bit playback — ~2x slower per core than ffmpeg and no thread scaling
author: 4papuce
body:
## What

H.264 High 10 / High 4:2:2 decoding was added in #629 (bit-exact, 46/46 ffmpeg conformance fixtures). Playback of that material is not yet smooth at 4K in FilmCraft, while kdenlive previews the same camera files smoothly on the same laptop. This issue tracks closing that gap.

Two distinct problems, and only the first is decode:

### 1. Decode is ~3x slower per core than ffmpeg

Raw decoder, 4K High 4:2:2 10-bit, 30 frames, `tests/perf.rs` fixtures:

| | ours | ffmpeg | gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 thread | 9.5–12.6 fps | 30.9 fps | ~3x |
| 12 threads | 41.6–43.3 fps | 62.5 fps | 1.4x |

Scaling caps at ~**4x regardless of core count**: 1/2/4/8/12 threads = 10.5/19.8/31.7/39.6/41.6 fps. It is not lock contention — concurrency is bounded by pictures in flight (3/4/6/14 in flight → 24/31/39/45 fps) because references must be decoded before their dependents. Oversubscribing is worse (24 threads 41.1 fps, 48 threads 36.5 fps). So **more cores is not the fix**; faster cores are.

`crates/h264` has zero `std::arch` / `target_feature`: IDCT, deblocking, interpolation, weighted prediction and residual reconstruction are all scalar. ffmpeg's advantage here is hand-written SIMD.

### 2. Tail latency, which is what actually drops frames on real footage

`bench_playback --file ~/Videos/P1004888.MOV --res full --gpu` (16-core laptop), and the `h264-2160-422-10b` fixture for comparison:

| source | on time | `svc50` | `svc95` | `lat99` | `src/j` decode |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| synthetic 4K fixture (noisy) | 80–90% | 8.6–9.8 ms | 63–96 ms | 348–477 ms | 7.9–12.6 ms |
| same, CPU path | 14% | 282–341 ms | 629–723 ms | 1.6–2.6 s | 120.0 ms |

Real camera material decodes in **7.9–12.6 ms against a 40 ms budget** (25 fps), so decode is *not* the constraint for that file — the median is fine and the drops come from **350–480 ms occasional stalls**. End-to-end the pipeline spends `cpu ms/f` 331–366 (~8 cores' worth) while decode itself needs ~0.2 cores.

Note the earlier s…

title: Opening files at launch on Windows and Linux: a .FCPROJ is imported as media, relative paths go offline
author: vangel76
body:
Premiere Pro parity, docs/gaps.md G9: `filmcraft [project.fcproj | media files...]` (terminal, Open With, a Windows or Linux file association) should open the project and import the media the same way whatever the case of the extension or the working directory.

What is missing today:

- `apps/filmcraft/src/main.rs` picks the project with `f.ends_with(".fcproj")`. Windows file associations and the shared-mime-info glob match extensions case-insensitively, so double-clicking `CUT.FCPROJ` (or `Cut.FcProj`) starts FilmCraft, which then tries to import the project as a media file and fails instead of opening it.
- Relative paths are passed on as given: `filmcraft clip.mp4` stores `clip.mp4` in the project and `filmcraft cut.fcproj` adds `cut.fcproj` to Recent Projects, so both go missing once the app runs from another folder (desktop launcher, Open Most Recent).
- `filmcraft-cli import` makes paths absolute with `std::fs::canonicalize`, which on Windows returns verbatim `\\?\C:\...` paths; those are stored in the project and shown in the Project panel.

Expected: the project is found by a case-insensitive `.fcproj` extension, and every launch path is made absolute (`std::path::absolute`: no verbatim prefix, symlinks kept) before it is opened or imported.

I'm working on this and will open a PR.

title: iPadOS: the engine and the UI already build for the device, and a 264 line host runs them
author: smithplus
body:
Found by compiling `v0.5.0` against `aarch64-apple-ios` to see what would break. Almost nothing
did. This is what the port actually costs, measured on an iPad Pro 11-inch (M2, iPadOS 26.7.1)
with rustc 1.95 and Xcode 27, not estimated.

## What already compiles, unmodified

| | |
|---|---|
| `cargo check -p filmcraft-engine --target aarch64-apple-ios` | clean |
| `cargo check -p filmcraft-ui-egui --target aarch64-apple-ios` | clean |
| `cargo check -p filmcraft --target aarch64-apple-ios` | fails on `rfd` only |
| `cpal`, `muda`, `arboard` for iOS | compile |

The `ui-egui` check pulls in eframe, egui-winit, egui-wgpu and objc2-ui-kit. The UI crate needs no
change to build for a device.

`cargo xtask wasm` is why. Gating L0 to L4 and the egui UI against `wasm32-unknown-unknown`
forced out `std::fs`, `Instant::now`, `std::thread` and `temp_dir`, which is the same discipline
an iOS port needs. The WASM gate paid for this before anyone asked for it.

iOS is in places easier than the web. `std::fs` works inside the app container and there are real
threads, so none of it runs into the single-threaded limit the web build documents for render
previews, proxies, the Project Manager and mask tracking. I have not exercised those paths yet.

## What runs on the device

All of this is verified on hardware, not in the simulator:

- Engine and the full egui UI, on Metal through wgpu.
- Hardware H.264 and HEVC decode. `filmcraft_platform::register()` reports
  `Available("VideoToolbox")` on the device.
- Audio out through `cpal`, unchanged.
- Auto-save and the crash recovery journal. Verified by killing the app and reopening it.

title: fix(engine): saving a new demo replaces the previously opened project file
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Opening Demo Project after a saved project leaves the demo associated with the previous file. Save without an explicit destination then replaces that file with the demo. A synthetic bin that was present before this sequence was absent when the same file was reopened. This reproduced through the local CLI in both tested builds. The desktop menu reaches the same commands without an intervening guard in the inspected source; a desktop interaction was not executed.

## Steps to reproduce

Use either tested CLI build on PATH. This executed sequence uses only a disposable synthetic project and an isolated data directory. The original project is fully saved before Demo Project opens, so it has no unsaved changes that require confirmation.

```sh
probe_dir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$probe_dir"' EXIT
export FILMCRAFT_DATA_DIR="$probe_dir/data"
cd "$probe_dir"

filmcraft-cli run - <<'JSONL'
{"id":"file.newProject","params":{"name":"Synthetic"}}
{"id":"file.newBin","params":{"name":"ORIGINAL"}}
{"id":"file.saveAs","params":{"path":"original.fcproj"}}
JSONL

filmcraft-cli --project original.fcproj --compact inspect project
shasum -a 256 original.fcproj

filmcraft-cli --project original.fcproj run - <<'JSONL'
{"id":"file.openDemoProject"}
{"id":"file.save"}

author: fernandodilland
body:

FilmCraft already has atomic saves, rolling auto-save versions and a crash-recovery journal. Please extend them to remote targets the user owns, add Premiere Productions-style project locking, and make projects portable between machines without uploading footage by default. Opt-in, no vendor server, no telemetry.

## How Premiere does it
- Auto-Save has a configurable interval and number of versions, and can store its copies in a different location than the project (for example local disk while the project sits on shared storage). An option also performs a normal save of the open projects.

title: VP9 software decode: run the loop filter of a frame in parallel (superblock-row wavefront)
author: vangel76
body:
Premiere Pro parity, docs/gaps.md G16: smooth playback of VP9 (WebM) footage without hardware decoding.

The VP9 decoder loop-filters each frame on one thread (one post job per frame, superblock rows in raster order). Later frames wait per band for their references, so this serial filter sits on the critical path of every inter frame: with 16 threads a 1080p30 stream decodes at ~107 fps against ~60 fps with one thread (1.8x), and the loop filter is ~30% of the CPU profile.

Expected: the loop filter of a frame runs as a wavefront over superblock rows (row r trails row r-1 by two superblocks, which is what the raster order of the specification allows), with bit-identical output, bands still published in order as soon as they are final, and one thread / wasm unchanged.

I'm working on this and will open a PR.

title: perf.stats reports zero hardware-encode counters for VideoToolbox exports
author: wowshy
body:
On macOS, FilmCraft commit 4e2d0bc2, a successful 30-frame H.264 export with `hardwareEncoding: "auto"` leaves `export.hardware.frames` and `sessions` at `0`.

**Reproduction**: 
In the same CLI process, run `file.exportMedia` with `wait: true` and `hardwareEncoding: "auto"`, then `perf.stats`. CPU sampling confirms calls through `HardwareEncoder::encode` → `VtEncoder::encode`.

**Expected**: 
The counters reflect the VideoToolbox export session and encoded frames.

**Root cause**: 
`crates/platform/src/hardware_encode.rs` never calls `note_hw_encode_session()`, `note_hw_encode_frame()`, or `note_hw_encode_declined()`. These counters were introduced in 6db932a9 and wired into NVENC, but not VideoToolbox.

This makes performance diagnostics misleading even though export succeeds.

title: Lumetri Color panel: control rows overflow the panel when the header shows a long clip name
author: vark-debug
body:
## Description

The Lumetri 颜色 (Lumetri Color) panel does not handle long clip names gracefully: when the header displays a long filename, the control rows below — each consisting of a label, a slider track, and a numeric value — get pushed beyond the panel's visible content area. As a result, the value column (`26.9`, `0.0`, `100.0`, …) is clipped at or past the right edge of the panel.

**The bug is filename-length dependent.** Short filenames (e.g. `diagram.png`) render the layout correctly and all values stay visible. The bug only reproduces when the filename exceeds a certain length — for example, an auto-generated name like `inference_output_rollout_2026-10-04_3ce159cb-52e3-4b72-9e90-0c4a…`.

The same panel layout is shared with 基本图形 / 基本声音 / 文字转语音 / 属性, so the bug is likely reproducible across all of them when their header content is long enough.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open FilmCraft and create a new project.
2. Import **two** clips:
   - one with a short filename, e.g. `diagram.png`
   - one with a long filename, e.g. `inference_output_rollout_2026-10-04_3ce159cb-52e3-4b72-9e90-0c4a…`

title: HEVC software decode is 2.7–4× slower per core than ffmpeg (1080p Main): motion compensation is half the profile
author: vangel76
body:
## What

The software HEVC decoder (`crates/hevc`) is 2.7–4× slower per core than ffmpeg on 1080p Main (8-bit) material. Scrubbing a long-GOP HEVC clip pays this on every seek (decode from the IRAP to the target): found while measuring storytold/effectcraft#329 (scrubbing long videos in EffectCraft, which uses FilmCraft's decoders), where a 15-min 1080p HEVC clip with GOP 250 costs ~435 ms per seek vs ~224 ms with ffmpeg.

This is decode speed only. #965 (HEVC preview dropping frames) turned out to be the HDR conversion path (#1017), and #848 is H.264.

## Measurements

`crates/hevc/examples/hevcdec` (release, thin LTO), Ryzen 7 7800X3D, ffmpeg 9.0.2 `-benchmark` rtime:

| stream | frames | ours 1 thread | ffmpeg 1 thread | ours 4 threads | ffmpeg 4 threads |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| testsrc2 1080p30, x265 ultrafast, GOP 250, 900 kb/s | 500 | 3.93 s (7.9 ms/frame) | 0.95 s | 1.73 s | 0.28 s |
| testsrc2 + noise 1080p30, x265 medium CRF 24 (the `bench_1080p` recipe) | 120 | 1.49 s (12.4 ms/frame) | 0.55 s | 0.63 s | 0.23 s |

## Profile (perf, 1 thread, first stream)

| share | where |
|---:|---|
| ~27% | `prediction_unit`, almost all of it inlined motion compensation: `put_uni` / `put_bi` (~14%, clipping loops over runtime widths), `copy_line` (~3%) |
| ~10% | libc `memmove` called from `copy_line` in `luma_window` / `chroma_window`: the u16 → i16 window copy compiles to one libc call per row of a tiny block |
| ~17% | `interpolate::<8>` / `interpolate::<4>` (8- and 4-tap filters, i32 lanes) |
| ~11% | deblocking (`boundary_strength`, `filter_luma`, `advance`) |
| ~4% | `residual` (17% on the noisier CRF 24 stream) |

So motion compensation (window fetch, interpolation, weighted-prediction store) is about half of the decode time.

## Plan

Bit-exact changes only, no `unsafe`, no new dependencies:
1. Width-specialised (const-generic) `put_uni` / `put_bi` loops so short rows vectorise.
2. A window fetch that does not call `memmove` per row.
3. Integer-vector f…

title: Optional modular project storage and conversion
author: whatever-industries
body:
FilmCraft should optionally support project storage in independently addressable modules, with a conversion path from its current single project file. This is separate from media indexing and relinking: modular project storage manages bins/sequences and their references, while a media catalog manages identities and locations of source files.

The primary motivation is **stability and recoverability on large Hollywood-scale feature-film and television productions**. This request comes from concern about the reliability problems encountered with Premiere-like, monolithic project workflows at that scale: a production can accumulate huge numbers of bins, clips, sequence versions and complex edits over months of work. FilmCraft should offer a way to keep that growing production organized without requiring all project data to be loaded, rewritten or recovered as one unit.

Independent bin/sequence modules should let editors load only the working set, save changed modules, and restore an affected bin or sequence from a backup without rolling back unrelated work. A damaged or unavailable module should be identified and isolated so unaffected modules remain usable wherever their dependencies allow. This is a reliability requirement first; faster opening/saving and lower memory use are additional goals to measure.

Modular storage alone does not guarantee stability. The design must demonstrate transactional saves, consistent cross-module references and useful recovery under interrupted writes, missing modules and corruption. It also does not replace application crash handling or backups.

**Implementation intent — @whatever-industries:** I plan to work on this after the initial Avid importer in #1056, as a separate follow-up. I intend to develop the optional modular-storage design and recovery requirements with maintainer feedback before implementing it. This is distinct from the managed-media catalog in #170.

- Add **File > Convert Project to Modu…

title: fix(cli): export with missing media writes the placeholder and exits 0 with no warning
author: Envaris-Avalon
body:
## Summary
When a project references a media file that is no longer on disk, the headless CLI export completes as if nothing were wrong: it writes the "media not found" placeholder frames into the output, prints its normal success JSON, prints nothing on stderr and exits 0. `media.status` on the same project correctly reports the item as `missing`, so the engine knows.

In an automated build the exit code and the result JSON are the only signals, so a moved or unmounted media folder produces a complete-looking file of placeholder frames.

## Version / platform
`filmcraft-cli 0.6.0` (also reproduced on 0.5.0), Linux x86_64, headless CLI, CPU only.

## Steps to reproduce
```bash
ffmpeg -v error -y -f lavfi -i testsrc=size=640x360:rate=24:duration=3 -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:v libx264 "$PWD/miss.mp4"

cat > setup.jsonl <<EOF
{"id":"file.newSequence","params":{"name":"s","width":640,"height":360,"fps":24}}
{"id":"file.import","params":{"paths":["$PWD/miss.mp4"]}}
EOF
echo '{"id":"timeline.place","params":{"item":8,"track":"V1","frame":0,"audio":false}}' > place.jsonl

filmcraft-cli --save-as p.fcproj run - < setup.jsonl
filmcraft-cli --project p.fcproj --save run - < place.jsonl

filmcraft-cli --project p.fcproj export on.mp4 --format h264 --no-audio; echo "exit=$?"     # fine

mv miss.mp4 miss.mp4.moved
filmcraft-cli --project p.fcproj exec media.status                                          # "status":"missing"
filmcraft-cli --project p.fcproj export off.mp4 --format h264 --no-audio; echo "exit=$?"
```

(In a fresh project the imported item is id 8; adjust `item` if yours differs.)

## Actual
- The second export prints the usual result (`"frames":72`, `exported off.mp4 in 0.4s`), nothing on stderr, `exit=0`.
- `off.mp4` has 72 frames of the placeholder (mean grey of the frame at 1 s: 40, against 125 with the media online).
- `render --seconds 1 --out f.png` on the same project also exits 0 with no warning.

## Expected
A non-zero exit, or at the least a warning on stderr …

title: fix(effects): setParam keyframe past the clip end is clamped silently and can overwrite the clip-end keyframe
author: Envaris-Avalon
body:
## Summary
`effects.setParam` with a `time` that falls after the clip's end does not fail and does not keep the keyframe at that time. The time is clamped to the clip end, with `"ok":true` and no warning. Two consequences:

1. If a keyframe already sits exactly at the clip end, the new call **overwrites its value** instead of adding a keyframe.
2. A ramp whose second keyframe is past the clip end is **compressed** to finish at the clip end, so its slope over the visible part is wrong.

This matters for ramps computed in sequence time that span a cut (a fade that starts inside one clip and ends after it).

## Version / platform
`filmcraft-cli 0.6.0` (identical on 0.5.0), Linux x86_64, headless CLI.

## Steps to reproduce
Base project: a 3 s, 24 fps, 640x360 clip (`ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc=size=640x360:rate=24:duration=3`) placed on V1 at frame 0 of a 640x360/24 sequence. The clip is 72 frames = 762048000000 ticks; in my project it is clip id 9.

**Case A - the clip-end keyframe is overwritten**
```json
{"id":"effects.toggleAnimation","params":{"clip":9,"effect":"opacity","param":"opacity"}}
{"id":"effects.setParam","params":{"clip":9,"effect":"opacity","param":"opacity","value":100,"time":0}}
{"id":"effects.setParam","params":{"clip":9,"effect":"opacity","param":"opacity","value":100,"time":762048000000}}
{"id":"effects.setParam","params":{"clip":9,"effect":"opacity","param":"opacity","value":20,"time":1270080000000}}
```
Results: `{"keyframes":1}`, `{"keyframes":2}`, `{"keyframes":2}`. The third call (5 s, past the end) adds no keyframe; `inspect sequence` shows 2 keyframes, and the clip now fades to 20 % at its end. Rendered mean grey: 58 at 2.9 s and 54 at 2.97 s, against 127 at full opacity.

**Case B - the ramp is compressed**
```json
{"id":"effects.toggleAnimation","params":{"clip":9,"effect":"opacity","param":"opacity"}}
{"id":"effects.setParam","params":{"clip":9,"effect":"opacity","param":"opacity","value":100,"time":0}}
{"id":"effects.setParam","params":{…

title: Audio VU meter levels stop updating when playback is paused and the mouse is idle
author: Max6mm
body:
**Environment**
Application version: filmcraft-0.6.0-linux-x86_64.AppImage
Operating system: Arch Linux
Desktop environment: KDE Plasma
Display server: Wayland

**Description**
The audio VU meter works correctly during playback, displaying both average and peak audio levels. However, I noticed some unexpected behavior when pausing playback.

When playback is paused, the displayed levels remain frozen at their current values as long as the mouse is not moving. As soon as I move the mouse, both the average and peak levels gradually decrease. If I stop moving the mouse, the levels freeze again at their current values.


**Steps to reproduce**
Start playback with some audio.
Pause playback while the VU meter is displaying audio levels.
Keep the mouse still and observe the meter.
Move the mouse and observe the levels gradually decrease.
Stop moving the mouse and observe that the levels freeze again.


**Expected behavior**
I'm not sure what the intended behavior is when playback is paused. The meter could either hold the last displayed values or gradually return to zero, but its behavior should ideally be consistent and independent of mouse movement.

**Actual behavior**
The displayed levels only decrease when the mouse is moving. When the mouse is idle, they remain frozen at their current values.

This makes the VU meter's behavior feel unexpected and suggests that its updates might somehow be tied to mouse movement.

author: vangel76
body:
Camera RAW support is at 0% (docs/codec-parity.md). CinemaDNG is the one widely used cinema RAW format with a **public specification**, so it can be implemented clean-room in pure Rust without any vendor SDK. Related: #383.

## Spec basis (public documents only)
- Adobe Digital Negative (DNG) Specification, versions 1.4 – 1.7 (public PDF)
- TIFF Revision 6.0 and TIFF/EP (ISO 12234-2)
- ITU-T T.81 / ISO/IEC 10918-1, lossless JPEG (process 14, "LJ92")
- CinemaDNG format description (DNG image sequences in folders, or MXF-wrapped)

No other decoder's source (dcraw, LibRaw, rawspeed, darktable, RawTherapee, ffmpeg, the Adobe DNG SDK…) is read.

## Scope of the first PR
- DNG/TIFF container: IFD parsing incl. SubIFDs, bounded and hostile-input safe (offset/size checks, IFD cycle/count limits, capped allocations).
- Raw CFA data: uncompressed (8–16-bit, packed and unpacked) and lossless JPEG (T.81 process 14, predictors 1–7, tiles and strips).
- Processing to RGB following the DNG pipeline: linearization table, black/white levels (incl. per-CFA black), DefaultCrop, AsShotNeutral white balance, demosaic, ColorMatrix/ForwardMatrix to a linear working space, and an output transform consistent with FilmCraft's colour pipeline.
- CinemaDNG sequences: a folder of numbered `.dng` frames imported as one clip (reusing image-sequence import), frame rate from the CinemaDNG FrameRate tag when present.
- Tests on synthetic DNGs written by a test-only spec-based writer (no camera files committed), plus hostile-input tests.

Out of scope for the first PR: lossy DNG (JPEG/JPEG XL), MXF-wrapped CinemaDNG, opcode lists, a Raw/Color settings UI.

I'm working on this and will open a PR.

title: Text panel: "Import captions file…" button label is invisible in light mode
author: vark-debug
body:
## Description

In the Text panel's **Captions** sub-tab, there are two stacked CTA buttons under the "Add captions" headline:

1. `Create new caption track` — primary, blue background, white label.
2. `Import captions file…` — secondary, appears to use the panel surface color as its background.

In **dark mode**, both buttons render their labels in white. Against the dark panel surface, the secondary button's label is legible (the panel itself is dark, so white-on-dark works).

In **light mode**, the panel surface becomes light. The `Create new caption track` button keeps its blue background, so its white label is still legible. But the secondary `Import captions file…` button's background also becomes light, while its label is still rendered in white — so the label is now white-on-light and effectively disappears.

The most likely root cause is that the button label color is **not bound to a theme-aware token** (it is hardcoded to white, or hardcoded to a color that resolves to white in both themes). The fix is to switch the label to a token that flips with the active theme.

> Triggers: Always present whenever the Text panel's Captions sub-tab is shown in light mode.
> Scope: a single button in the Text panel's Captions empty state. Other "secondary / ghost" buttons across the app may share the same hardcoded color and could exhibit the same bug — they should be audited, but are out of scope for this issue.
> Not affected: `Create new caption track` (primary button — its background is the brand blue, so white-on-blue works in both themes).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the workspace and switch the app to **light mode** (the global theme toggle, not the OS appearance).
2. Open the **Text** panel and click into the **Captions** sub-tab.
3. Make sure the Captions empty state is showing (no caption track yet, or the active context is one where this CTA appears). The headline reads "Add captions" with the sub-line "Create a caption track or import a caption file."
4…

title: Accessibility of filmcraft for visually impaired film makers
author: logicproxgaming
body: Film craft is partially accessible to text to speech screen readers such as jaws or NVDA but some improvements based on standard practices can be made. The elements, menus, buttons, sliders, and dialogues need to be properly labeled in order for text to speech to read them. Visually impaired users cannot use the mouse too much, so tab order is also important. Making sure that when you tab through the interface things show up in a logical order is very beneficial. When tapping through the interface currently, most of the elements say unknown which leads me to believe that they might not have proper aria labeling or whatever equivalent labeling system is used in rust. Audible feedback is important such as when splitting a clip, adding in effect, or making any sort of change to the timeline. Normal shortcut keys such as JKL are standard across video editors, cut copy and paste commands play pause and things of that nature. Those don’t really need to be changed but spoken feedback when things Sledge it as slicing clips or adding media is useful. Having some sort of way to apply effects, pull in media from the media manager, and things that normally involve dragging and dropping are essential for visually impaired users who get Lil to no use out of the mouse.

title: Panel focus ring is partially occluded by inner components
author: vark-debug
body: ## Description In the workspace, six panels are expected to show a complete, closed blue focus ring when focused — a single visual signal for the current focus. In practice, the ring is **not** inconsistent in thickness / color / radius. The real cause is that the ring is **occluded by each panel's own inner components** (tab bar, status bar, toolbar, child buttons, etc.). (`media browser` shares a parent container with several tabs, so its occluders are denser — top tab bar **+** toolbar — but the root cause is the same.) ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Open the workspace with all six target panels visible. Disable any auto-blur-on-hover-out so the ring stays visible. 2. Click each panel in turn and screenshot the focused state. 3. For each screenshot, use DevTools to identify which inner component occludes each missing arc of the ring. ## Expected Behavior All six panels must show a single, complete, closed blue focus ring on focus — same color / width / radius / inset, fully visible, no segment occluded by any inner component. title: Feature request: Align / Center for video and image clips
author: HaydenHarms
body:
**What I'm trying to do**
Center a photo or video clip in the frame (or snap it to an edge) without retyping Motion ▸ Position by hand. This comes up constantly in vertical talking-head reels where B-roll stills sit as "cards" on a background and each one needs re-centering after scaling.

**What happens now (0.5.0)**
- `Graphics ▸ Align` (`graphics.align`, `graphics.alignFrame.*`) only works on layers inside a graphic clip, not on regular video/image clips.
- `Clip ▸ Video Options ▸ Fit to frame / Fill frame` do center the clip, but they also change Scale and clear the Scale/Position keyframes, which wipes a push-in.
- The Motion reset button resets Scale, Rotation and Anchor too.
- So the only way to just center is typing half the sequence size (e.g. 540, 960 for 1080×1920) into Position.

**Proposal**
Let the existing align commands (Center Horizontally / Center Vertically / Left / Right / Top / Bottom, aligned to the frame) work on selected video and image clips by setting Motion ▸ Position only, based on the clip's scaled bounds. Scale, rotation and keyframes on other parameters stay untouched; if Position has keyframes, set the value at the playhead (like typing it would).

Nice to have: align several selected clips to each other, and buttons for this in the Effect Controls Motion section or the Program monitor.

**Why**
It's one of the most common fiddly moves when building card-style B-roll edits, and the align commands already exist; they just don't reach regular clips.

title: Add Russian interface language (ru.tsv, full catalog)
author: vsemke
body:
[filmcraft-russian.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33306560/filmcraft-russian.patch)
[ru.tsv](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33306561/ru.tsv)

FilmCraft has no Russian yet, while PhotoCraft already ships one. Here is a complete Russian catalog for FilmCraft, plus a patch that wires it in.

### Files
- `ru.tsv`: goes to `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/ru.tsv`. Covers all 3,496 source strings of `es.tsv`.
- `filmcraft-russian.patch`: the catalog plus the wiring, following the Ukrainian example. Made against `main` as of 2026-10-10; apply with `git am filmcraft-russian.patch`.

### What the patch changes
- `i18n/mod.rs`: `Language::Ru` (code `ru`, name «Русский»), catalog loading, `from_locales` (any `ru`, `ru-RU`, `ru_RU.UTF-8` → Russian), added to `catalogs_are_well_formed`, plus a `russian_renders_with_bundled_fonts` test covering the whole Cyrillic alphabet
- `menus.rs`: new `app.language.russian` item under Edit ▸ Language
- `apps/filmcraft/src/native_menu.rs`: Russian in the native menu
- `engine/src/settings.rs`: «Русский» in Settings ▸ General ▸ Interface Language
- `ru.tsv.attribution` and a row in `ATTRIBUTION.md` (MIT OR Apache-2.0)

### Checks
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-ui-egui --lib i18n`: 18 passed (placeholders, trailing "…", no duplicates, bundled fonts render every Russian letter)
- `cargo check -p filmcraft` builds; `cargo fmt` is clean

### Notes
- Clean-room: written from the meaning of the English strings, using common Russian video-editing terms (дорожка, клип, секвенция, курсор воспроизведения, точка входа/выхода, подрезка). No other product's localization was used.
- Strings with a count use the form "Клипов: {n}", which reads correctly for any number, since the catalog has no plural forms.
- Prepared with the help of an AI assistant (Claude). Corrections from other native speakers are welcome.

title: Timeline does not scroll to the playhead after Home / End (go to sequence start/end)
author: vangel76
body:
## What happens
Pressing Home moves the playhead to the sequence start, but the visible Timeline range stays where it was, so the playhead is off screen. Same for End and any other jump (Up/Down edit points, go to marker, ...). Reported on Discord for 0.6.0 (Windows 10).

The Timeline scrolls so the playhead is visible after the jump.

## Steps
1. Open a sequence longer than the visible range, zoom in, scroll right.

The Timeline only follows the playhead while playing (`app.playback.playing` in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/timeline.rs`); a seek while stopped never touches the scroll.

title: Project panel: Shift-click toggles one item instead of selecting the range from the anchor
author: vangel76
body:
## What happens
In the Project panel (List, Icon and Freeform views), Shift-click on a second item adds just that one item to the selection, exactly like Ctrl/Cmd-click. The items between the first-clicked item and the Shift-clicked one stay unselected. Reported on Discord against 0.6.0.

## Expected (Premiere Pro)
Click an item, Shift-click another: every item between them (in the order the panel shows) is selected. Ctrl/Cmd-click toggles single items and sets a new anchor.

title: fix(timeline): Continuous thumbnails flicker and backlog decoders for 20+ seconds during timeline zoom
author: tradmangh
body:
### Bug: Continuous thumbnails flicker and backlog decoders for 20+ seconds during timeline zoom

Follow-up to #614 / PR #698 (`c85d0ac9`).

#### Problem
When changing the Timeline zoom level (dragging the zoom scroll bar handles or using Option+wheel / pinch zoom) while **Show Video Thumbnails** is set to **Continuous**:
1. Thumbnails rapidly flicker, appear, and disappear while zooming.
2. When the zoom gesture finishes and the mouse button is released, many thumbnail tiles appear missing or blank.
3. The missing thumbnails eventually populate, but it can take **20+ seconds** (e.g. for a 12-minute clip) before the strip is completely rendered.

#### Cause
1. **Per-frame timestamp recalculation:**
   In `thumbnail_tiles` (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/timeline.rs`), each tile's source offset is computed from the clip's screen width:
   ```rust
   let offset_at = |x: f32| Tick(((x - x0) as f64 / width as f64 * dur.0 as f64).round() as i64)...
   ```
   During a zoom drag, the clip width changes continuously on every render frame (~60 times/sec). Every tile computes a brand new media timestamp `mt` on every tick.
2. **Cache misses & UI flickering:**
   Because each tick asks for a new timestamp, `app.thumbnail()` misses the cache on every frame and returns `None`, immediately turning previously rendered tiles blank while dragging.
3. **Queue backlog & FIFO starvation in `frames.rs`:**
   Unlike monitor scrubbing (`prio == 0` in `crates/ui-egui/src/frames.rs`), thumbnail jobs (`prio == 50`) have no job cancellation for superseded requests. A 1–2 second zoom drag queues hundreds or thousands of obsolete decode requests.
   Because the worker queue processes these jobs sequentially, the **final** frames (requested when the mouse is released) are placed at the back of the queue. The decoders spend 20+ seconds seeking and decoding frames from intermediate zoom levels before finally reaching the visible tiles.

#### Expected Behaviour
- **Freeze during drag:** During active z…

title: fix(commands): sequence.applyAudioTransition schema omits edge, params and reverse
author: Marssvoodoo
body:
**Version:** FilmCraft 0.6.0 (Windows x64 MSI). The schema below is unchanged on `main` at 4e2d0bc.

### Summary

`sequence.applyAudioTransition` advertises only `{"clip":id?,"effect":str?,"frames":i64?}` (`crates/engine/src/commands.rs`). It shares `apply_transition` with `sequence.applyVideoTransition`, and that handler also reads `edge`, `params` and `reverse` for audio. The video command documents all three. FilmCraft relies on `edge` for audio itself: `trim.applyDefaultTransition` (`sequence_extras.rs`) calls `sequence.applyAudioTransition` with `{"clip": …, "edge": …}`.

Because the schema is what `filmcraft-cli describe`, `commands --json` and the MCP server publish, scripted clients can't see that an audio fade can go on a clip's out edge. Given only `clip`, the transition goes on the in edge. For example, a fade-out requested on the last clip of a track lands at its head.

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
filmcraft-cli describe sequence.applyAudioTransition
# params: {"clip":id?,"effect":str?,"frames":i64?}

# With an audio clip (id 35) as the last item on A2:
filmcraft-cli --project p.fcproj --save exec sequence.applyAudioTransition '{"clip":35,"effect":"Constant Gain","frames":48}'
filmcraft-cli --project p.fcproj inspect sequence
# A2 transition: "from": null, "to": 35, "align": "start"  (in edge: fade-in)

filmcraft-cli --project p.fcproj --save exec sequence.applyAudioTransition '{"clip":35,"effect":"Constant Gain","frames":48,"edge":"out"}'
# A2 transition: "from": 35, "to": null, "align": "end"     (out edge: fade-out, works)
```

### Expected

The audio schema lists the parameters the handler accepts, matching the video command: `"edge":"in"|"out"?`, `"params":{param:value}?`, `"reverse":bool?`. Ideally it also lists the audio effect names in `effect` (`constant_power|constant_gain|exponential_fade`), as the video schema does for its effects.

### Suggested fix

Update the schema string for `sequence.applyAudioTransition` in `commands.rs`. The handler …

title: fix(timeline): timeline.place with a sub-frame time rounds duration up; export renders one frame more than inspect reports
author: Marssvoodoo
body:
**Version:** FilmCraft 0.6.0 (Windows x64 MSI), headless `filmcraft-cli`.

### Summary

1. `timeline.place` with a `time` that isn't on a frame boundary keeps that start time but rounds `duration` up to whole frames. The clip therefore ends after the requested end.
2. The sequence then ends between frames. `inspect sequence` reports `durationFrames: 120`, but export renders 121 frames.

### Steps to reproduce

Media (ffmpeg used only to make the inputs and to measure the output):

```sh
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i "testsrc2=s=640x360:r=24:d=5" -f lavfi -i "sine=f=1000:r=48000:d=5" -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:a aac -shortest clip.mp4
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i "sine=f=440:r=48000:d=5" -c:a pcm_s16le tone.wav
filmcraft-cli --save-as p.fcproj exec file.import '{"paths":["clip.mp4","tone.wav"]}'
```

`place.jsonl`, with ticks at 254016000000 per second, so 10584000000 per frame at 24 fps:

```jsonl
{"id":"file.newSequence","params":{"name":"f","width":640,"height":360,"fps":24,"sampleRate":48000,"video":1,"audio":2,"mix":"Stereo","trackType":"Standard"}}
{"id":"timeline.place","params":{"item":1,"track":"V1","audioTrack":"A1","frame":0,"insert":false,"sourceIn":0,"duration":1270080000000}}
{"id":"timeline.place","params":{"item":2,"track":"A2","time":638568000000,"insert":false,"sourceIn":0,"duration":631512000000}}
```

The second placement starts 1/3 frame after frame 60 and should end exactly at 5.000 s: 638568000000 + 631512000000 = 1270080000000, which is frame 120.

filmcraft-cli --project p.fcproj inspect sequence
filmcraft-cli --project p.fcproj export out.mp4 --format h264
ffprobe -v error -count_frames -select_streams v:0 -show_entries stream=nb_read_frames -of csv=p=0 out.mp4

title: MP3 imports play ~25 ms late: encoder delay not trimmed (symphonia enable_gapless is off)
author: sarvin-5124
body:
## Summary

FilmCraft 0.6.0 plays every MP3 about 25 ms late, even when the file's LAME/Xing tag records the encoder delay. The MP3 decoder's start padding (576 + 529 = 1105 samples) is never trimmed, so MP3 audio drifts out of sync with other media, with the source timecode, and with other editors (ffmpeg, Premiere, CapCut and SoundCraft all trim it).

## Reproduce

```sh
# 4 s of silence at 44.1 kHz with short clicks at exactly 1.000, 2.000 and 3.000 s, saved as click.wav
ffmpeg -i click.wav -c:a libmp3lame -b:a 128k tagged.mp3            # standard LAME tag with delay/padding
```

1. Import `tagged.mp3`, place it at 00:00 in a 48 kHz sequence and export WAV (preset "Waveform Audio 48 kHz 16-bit").
2. Find the clicks in the export.

**Expected:** clicks at 1.000 / 2.000 / 3.000 s, as `ffmpeg -i tagged.mp3` decodes them.
**Actual:** every click is 1196 samples @48 kHz late (24.9 ms; 1105 samples at the source's 44.1 kHz).

| Decoder | Click offset |
|---|---|
| ffmpeg | 0 |
| SoundCraft 0.5.0 (bounce) | 0–1 samples |
| **FilmCraft 0.6.0 (export)** | **+1196 samples (24.9 ms)** |

The offset is the same for ElevenLabs MP3s at 44.1 and 48 kHz (1105 native samples). Waveforms and playback in the app show the same delay.

## Cause

`crates/codecs/src/audio.rs` (`AudioFileSource::decode`) probes with `FormatOptions::default()`. In symphonia 0.5, `enable_gapless` defaults to `false`, so the MP3 reader ignores the LAME delay/padding and never sets `trim_start`/`trim_end` on packets.

## Suggested fix

```rust
let fmt_opts = FormatOptions { enable_gapless: true, ..FormatOptions::default() };
```

SoundCraft already does this in `crates/audio-io/src/symph.rs`, and its bounce lands sample-accurate on the same file. It is worth checking the same option on the other symphonia probe sites, for example the audio of video imports.

Projects saved with the current behaviour will shift by about 25 ms once this is fixed, which may be worth a release note.

title: A marker's colour cannot be set anywhere in the UI: the context menu's Label submenu runs the clip command `edit.label`
author: schubam
body:
## What happens

Right-click a marker in the timeline → the context menu opens with every entry disabled **except `Label`**. The `Label` submenu lists the full colour set (Violet … Yellow). Choosing one **has no effect** on the marker.

## Why

The `Label` submenu dispatches **`edit.label`**, which is a clip/item command and knows nothing about markers:

- `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/timeline.rs:1753` — the menu entry is `&[("Label", "edit.label")]`.
- `edit.label` (`crates/engine/src/commands.rs:1393-1412`) applies the label to `state.selection` (sequence clips) and `state.project_selection` (project items):

```rust
for i in &items { if let Some(it) = pr.item_mut(*i) { it.label = l; } }
for c in &clips { if let Some((_, it)) = q.find_item_mut(*c) { it.label = l; } }
```

A marker is neither a clip nor a project item, so the command runs over an empty set: no error, no effect, no feedback.

The command that *does* set a marker's colour is **`markers.edit`** (`crates/engine/src/sequence_tools.rs:199`), params `{"target":"program|source","marker":id,"name":str?,"comment":str?,"color":label?,"durationFrames":i64?}`.

`filmcraft-cli describe markers.edit` reports `"menu": []` and no shortcut, and a grep across `crates/ui-egui/src` finds only `markers.add`, `markers.addChapter` and `markers.addFlashCue` — **no UI code invokes `markers.edit`**, so there is no route to it from the app by any means (menu, shortcut, context menu, or dialog).

## Why it matters

Marker colour is a first-class surface in the UI: the Markers panel draws each marker's colour as a bar beside its row and its colour filter is the panel's only filterable axis (`MARKER_FILTER`, seven chips, `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/misc.rs:55`), and the timeline ruler draws a duration band per marker. So a user can **see** colours, **filter** by colour, and **cannot set** one.

Any workflow that keys on marker colour — for example undecided / keep / drop triage, which is what the colour field is for — cannot be per…

title: Feature (Beyond Premiere): Halation effect, a film-style red glow around highlights
author: Mateo-RR
body:
## What it is

Halation is a trait of photographic film. Very bright light passes through the emulsion, reflects off the back of the film base and re-exposes the emulsion from below, mostly the red-sensitive layer, which sits closest to the base. The result is a red-orange halo *around* strong highlights: street lights, windows, specular reflections, backlit edges. It is one of the most recognisable parts of the "film look", and digital sensors never produce it.

Premiere Pro has no such effect. Its users fake it by duplicating the clip, applying Channel Blur to the red channel only and changing the blend mode, or they buy presets. DaVinci Resolve includes it in its Film Look Creator.

## Proposal

A new video effect, **Halation**, CPU only. A small external contribution; I'll implement it.

**Algorithm** (linear light, `f32`, premultiplied alpha, like the other effects):

1. **Highlight mask:** luminance above *Threshold*, with a soft knee (the `highlights` helper, as in Wonder Glow).
2. **Gaussian blur of the mask** at two scales, a tight core and a wider falloff. Only a single plane (the mask) is blurred, not the full RGBA image. The radius is scaled by `cx.px_scale`, with the usual radius = 2σ convention.
3. **Core suppression:** the halo is multiplied by `1 − Core Suppression × mask`, so the light sits *around* the source rather than on top of it. This is what sets it apart from Wonder Glow.
4. **Tint** the halo with *Color* and add it to the image. The halo colour comes from the film, not from the source, so every highlight gets the same red-orange halo.

**Parameters:**

| Id | Name | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `threshold` | Threshold | 80 % | What counts as a strong highlight |
| `radius` | Radius | 20 px | Halo size |
| `intensity` | Intensity | 100 % | Strength |
| `color` | Color | red-orange | Halo tint |
| `core_suppression` | Core Suppression | 50 % | 0 % = the halo also covers the source; 100 % = only around it |

I'd love to see a Media Jobs system similar to Kdenlive's.

The idea is to let users run external tools on a clip directly from FilmCraft instead of having to leave the editor, process the file manually, and import the result again.

title: Export: let the user cap how many CPU cores an export uses
author: JordyUSA
body:
The only workaround is the RAYON_NUM_THREADS environment variable, set before launching. It's undocumented for this use. It also only affects the global rayon pool, not the decoders' and the encoder's own thread pools.

Where the core count comes from today (main @ ef12831b)

	•	Render batch and overlap: rayon::current_num_threads().clamp(2, 16) in crates/export/src/job.rs:272 and crates/export/src/lib.rs:1849. Overlap is on when current_num_threads() > 1 (job.rs:323).
	•	Renderer pool: crates/export/src/pipeline.rs:179.
	•	Decoders: each H.264 / HEVC / VP9 / AV1 decoder builds its own pool of available_parallelism().min(16) threads (h264/src/decoder.rs:114, hevc/src/decoder.rs:103, vp9/src/decoder.rs:89, av1/src/decoder.rs:218). The GOP caches decode on a global pool of available_parallelism() threads (codecs/src/gop.rs:450).
	•	H.264 encoder: EncoderConfig::threads is 0, so the encoder uses every core (h264enc/src/lib.rs:483).

So with several sources being decoded, an export can run well over N threads at once on an N-core machine.

Proposal

	1.	Setting: add ExportSettings::max_threads: u32 (camelCase maxThreads, serde default 0 = all cores, as now). Because ExportSettings is already serde with defaults, the CLI, the control channel and MCP pick it up with no further work. It should also appear:
	•	in the Export Settings dialog, as an "Advanced" option, "CPU threads: All / 1…N" (with an automation id);
	•	optionally as an app-wide default under Settings ▸ Performance.
	2.	Export pool: when set, export() runs inside a dedicated rayon::ThreadPool of max_threads threads (pool.install). Batch size, overlap, the renderer pool and every par_iter in rendering and in the ProRes / DNxHR / APV encoders then follow it automatically.
	3.	Encoder: make_venc passes the cap to filmcraft_h264enc::EncoderConfig::threads.
	4.	Decoders: carry the cap as a hint in filmcraft_media::cancel::Context, next to the background / draft / cancel hints.
	•	Set it on the export pool's workers…

title: Export: H.264 High 10, High 4:2:2 and High 4:4:4 Predictive (incl. lossless) in the built-in encoder
author: JordyUSA
body:
FilmCraft's H.264 encoder (crates/h264enc) only writes 8-bit 4:2:0: Constrained Baseline, Main and High. Its README lists "no 4:2:2/4:4:4 or high bit depth" as not yet implemented, and qpprime_y_zero_transform_bypass_flag is always written as 0 (crates/h264enc/src/nal.rs:59), so there's no lossless mode either. CRF 0 is near-lossless, not lossless.

The H.264 standard covers much more, and these profiles are widely used for masters, intermediates and camera-matching deliverables:

Profile	profile_idc	Chroma	Bit depth	Use
High 10 (+ Intra)	110	4:2:0	8–10	10-bit masters and deliverables without banding
High 4:2:2 (+ Intra)	122	4:2:0, 4:2:2	8–10	Broadcast / camera-native (XAVC Intra, XAVC S-I, AVC-Intra style)
High 4:4:4 Predictive (+ Intra)	244	4:2:0, 4:2:2, 4:4:4	8–14	Full-chroma masters; true lossless (transform bypass)

Today, a user who needs any of these has to export ProRes / DNxHR / APV and re-encode in another tool. Mathematically lossless H.264 isn't available at all.

Related (decode side, not this issue)

	•	#626 / PR #629: High 10 and High 4:2:2 decoding. Once merged it gives an in-tree, bit-exact decoder for round-trip tests of everything this issue proposes except 4:4:4 / lossless.
	•	#848: High 4:2:2 10-bit decode performance.
	•	#1136: unreadable Sony 10-bit 4:2:2 file.
	•	docs/gaps.md G3 covers decode only; G13 (delivery formats) doesn't list these encoder profiles yet.

Proposal

Ship in stages, each one useful on its own:

	1.	High 10 (4:2:0, 10-bit). Bit depth in the SPS (bit_depth_luma/chroma_minus8), QP range extended by 6 × (bitdepth − 8) (QpBdOffset), 16-bit sample paths in the transform, quantisation, intra prediction, deblocking and reconstruction.
	2.	High 4:2:2 (8/10-bit). chroma_format_idc = 2: 8×16 chroma blocks with the 2×4 chroma DC transform, chroma QP mapping for 4:2:2, and the CABAC context and residual changes it needs.
	3.	High 4:4:4 Predictive. chroma_format_idc = 3: chroma coded like luma (separate Cb/Cr residuals with luma-style…
