title: APV oracle tests fail instead of skipping when the system ffmpeg is older than 8.0
author: TramEFX
body:
The three tests in `crates/apv/tests/oracle.rs` fail on a machine whose `ffmpeg` predates APV support. Ubuntu 24.04's packaged ffmpeg (`7:6.1.1-3ubuntu5`) is one example:

```
thread 'all_profiles_bit_exact_with_ffmpeg' panicked at crates/apv/tests/oracle.rs:39:5:
ffmpeg failed on ".../target/fixtures/apv/oracle_422-10.apv": [in#0 @ ...] Unknown input format: 'apv'
```

`custom_q_matrix_and_fh_tile_sizes_bit_exact_with_ffmpeg` and `odd_dimensions_and_multi_tile_bit_exact_with_ffmpeg` fail the same way. `ffmpeg_or_skip` skips only when ffmpeg is *missing*. FFmpeg added the APV decoder and raw APV demuxer in 8.0 (its Changelog, "version 8.0"), so an older ffmpeg is found and the tests fail. Because `cargo test` stops at the first failing test binary, the rest of `cargo xtask ci` then never runs.

With a static ffmpeg 9.0.2, passed through `FILMCRAFT_FFMPEG` / `FILMCRAFT_FFPROBE`, all three pass.

**Suggestion:** when `ffmpeg -formats` does not list `apv`, skip with `SKIPPED (apv oracle): ffmpeg <version> cannot read APV (needs 8.0+)`. That becomes a failure under `FILMCRAFT_REQUIRE_ORACLES=1`. Also mention ffmpeg ≥ 8.0 in `docs/testing.md`.

Seen at `7b6c134`, running the gate on GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-24.04`. `crates/apv/tests/oracle.rs` and `crates/testkit/src/oracle.rs` are unchanged on `main` as of 2026-10-12.

title: Golden GPU parity tests panic when the adapter cannot render to Rgba32Float (GPU-less Linux)
author: TramEFX
body:
On a GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-24.04` runner (no GPU, Mesa's EGL/OpenGL installed, no Vulkan driver), the four GPU tests in `crates/golden/tests/golden.rs` panic. Those are `gpu_matches_cpu_on_golden_scenes`, `gpu_blend_modes_match_cpu_render`, `gpu_transition_of_blended_clips_matches_cpu_render` and `gpu_effect_chains_match_cpu_render`:

```
wgpu error: Validation Error

Caused by:
  In Device::create_render_pipeline, label = 'fx-source'
    Color state [0] is invalid
      Format Rgba32Float is not renderable
```

`device()` skips only when `request_adapter` fails. Here it succeeds with a software adapter that cannot use `Rgba32Float` as a render attachment. The 29 CPU tests in the same binary pass.

After installing Mesa's Vulkan driver (`mesa-vulkan-drivers`, lavapipe), wgpu picks the Vulkan adapter (`llvmpipe`, `PHYSICAL_DEVICE_TYPE_CPU`) and all four pass. On real hardware (an AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT, Vulkan) they pass too.

**Suggestion:** in `device()`, also skip when
`adapter.get_texture_format_features(wgpu::TextureFormat::Rgba32Float).allowed_usages` lacks `RENDER_ATTACHMENT`, and print the adapter's name in the `SKIPPED` line.

Seen at `7b6c134`. `crates/golden/tests/golden.rs` is unchanged on `main` as of 2026-10-12.

title: `language_commands_switch_and_persist_without_a_document` fails without a Japanese font
author: TramEFX
body:
On a machine with no Japanese font (no craft-fonts build input and no system CJK font, such as a stock `ubuntu-24.04` runner), this `ui-egui` test fails at its first Japanese switch:

```
thread 'i18n::tests::language_commands_switch_and_persist_without_a_document' panicked at crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/mod.rs:
called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: "no Japanese font is installed on this system (for example Noto Sans CJK JP); the interface stays in English"

title: # Decide the plugin / extension direction early — Adobe is in its CEP→UXP transition pain, and FilmCraft has a window
author: vark-debug
body:
## TL;DR

Adobe's plugin story is in the worst state it has been in years. CEP is being deprecated, UXP's public surface is still incomplete (timeline hooks, audio APIs, several render integrations), plugin authors are stuck in the middle — too expensive to rewrite, too painful to stay — and CEP itself is heavy: large bundles, separate runtime, slow load, fragile debugging. **If FilmCraft ships a lightweight, well-documented, AI-friendly extension system early, it can be the NLE where junior developers and editors-paired-with-AI first write plugins**, instead of the third option behind Adobe and a hex editor.

This issue is **a direction proposal, not a bug report**. The ask is small: pick at least one of the five decisions in §5 and put it in writing. The architecture details can wait for follow-up RFCs.

---

## 1. Context — Adobe's CEP→UXP transition pain

For over a decade, Adobe's plugin story was CEP (Common Extensibility Platform) — a Creative Suite-era ExtendScript-derived system with its own config format (`.csxs/manifest.xml`), its own signing toolchain, and its own debug quirks. Two things are true at once:

- **CEP is being deprecated.** Adobe has postponed the final cutoff more than once; the postponements themselves are a signal that the migration is bigger than predicted. The exact date is less important than the direction: CEP plugins will eventually stop loading.
- **UXP is incomplete.** UXP (Unified Extensibility Platform) is the future. It is also, today, missing pieces that CEP plugins depended on — most visibly in the timeline / audio / render integration area. The migration is not "write the same plugin, swap the runtime." It is "rewrite the plugin, work around the gaps."

The combination means that a large chunk of the existing plugin ecosystem — both the authors and the install base — is in an uncomfortable middle: too expensive to rewrite, too painful to stay, no good third path.

title: MP4 with a leading empty edit (start offset) renders one frame early
author: TramEFX
body:
A video track whose edit list starts with an empty edit, followed by the usual B-frame skip edit, is rendered one frame early.

**Reproduce:**

```
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc=size=640x360:rate=24:decimals=3 -t 10 -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -g 48 -bf 2 -output_ts_offset 0.0533 late.mp4
```

The video edit list is `[53 ms empty (media_time -1), 10000 ms from media_time 1024]` (track timescale 12288, so a 2-frame skip). `ffprobe` reports `start_time=0.052979`.

Import it, use **Sequence From Clip**, and render the program at **2.1042 s** (inside frame 50 of the 24 fps sequence). `testsrc` prints each frame's own time, and the rendered picture's timer reads **2.000**: source frame 48.

- On the file's presentation timeline (ffmpeg / ffprobe), frame **49** is on screen at 2.1042 s (presented from 2.0946 s).
- Counting from the clip's first frame, it would be frame **50** (2.083).

The same command **without** `-output_ts_offset` (a single edit, media_time 1024) renders 2.083 at that time, which is correct. A variable-frame-rate variant (frames dropped with `select`, `-fps_mode vfr`) is also exact. Real files with a start offset like this exist: one with a 53 ms offset showed the same lag.

Seen at v0.6.0 (`2ff3f5e`) on Windows 11, through `filmcraft-engine`'s headless `Session` (`file.import`, `file.newSequenceFromClip`, `try_render_program_at`). Not checked: whether the clip's audio shifts the same way, i.e. whether picture and sound stay in sync.

Related, both closed: #714 (MP4 with no edit list) and #715 (Matroska remux that keeps its timestamps). This is the MP4 case with an empty edit.

title: Video shows the previous frame when frame timestamps sit just after the sequence frame grid (phone footage)
author: TramEFX
body:
A source frame whose timestamp is even slightly later than the start of the sequence frame it belongs to is not shown in that frame. The previous source frame is shown instead.

**Reproduce:**

```
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc=size=640x360:rate=30:decimals=3 -t 10 -vf "settb=1/90000,setpts='if(eq(N,0),PTS,PTS+0.001/TB)'" -fps_mode passthrough -enc_time_base:v 1/90000 -video_track_timescale 90000 -c:v libx264 -bf 0 -pix_fmt yuv420p late.mp4
```

Every frame after the first is 1 ms after the 1/30 s grid (pts 0, 0.034333, 0.067667, …). There are no B-frames and no edit list, and FilmCraft reports 30.0 fps. Import it, use **Sequence From Clip**, and render the program at (k + 0.5)/30 s. `testsrc` prints each frame's own time:

| k | frame on screen (timer) | rendered (timer) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.033 | **0.000** |
| 75 | 2.500 | **2.466** |
| 150 | 5.000 | **4.966** |

The same command without the `setpts` shift renders 0.033 / 2.500 / 5.000.

The shown frame is the last source frame at or before the *start of the sequence frame* containing the time. On a real Android 15 clip (3840×2160 H.264, 30 fps; its first frame is 34.1 ms long, so later frames sit up to ~0.7 ms after the grid), that rule predicts all 10 measured times. The frame actually on screen matches only 2 of 10. The decoding itself is fine: the full-resolution render matches ffmpeg's decode of the frame it shows at 45.8 dB.

Effects: such a clip runs one frame behind and shows frame 0 twice. Where a clip's timestamp drift crosses the grid, a source frame would be skipped. Phone footage commonly has this kind of timestamp jitter.

It looks like the same class as #73 (WebM: "video lookup floors the time against 1 ms-rounded timestamps"), here on the MP4 path. Choosing the source frame nearest the sequence frame's start, or allowing a small tolerance, would avoid it.

Seen at v0.6.0 (`2ff3f5e`) on Windows 11, through `filmcraft-engine`'s headless `Session`. Not checked: whether the audio of such a clip stays i…

title: Export never finishes with a 1080p VP9 clip (0 % CPU, looks like a rayon deadlock in render_batch)
author: acroberts88
body:
**Version:** filmcraft-cli 0.6.0 (macOS universal, release v0.6.0, Apple Silicon).

Exporting a sequence that contains a 1080p VP9 clip never finishes. The process sits at 0 % CPU and leaves an `out.mp4` without a `moov` atom. `render` of a single frame from the same clip works, and a small 320×180 VP9 clip exports fine.

```sh
curl -LO https://test-videos.co.uk/vids/bigbuckbunny/webm/vp9/1080/Big_Buck_Bunny_1080_10s_5MB.webm
filmcraft-cli --data-dir ./fcdata --save-as p.fcproj import Big_Buck_Bunny_1080_10s_5MB.webm
printf '%s\n' '{"id":"file.newSequenceFromClip","params":{"items":[1]}}' '{"id":"timeline.place","params":{"item":1,"track":"V1","seconds":0}}' > s.jsonl
filmcraft-cli --data-dir ./fcdata --project p.fcproj --save run s.jsonl
filmcraft-cli --data-dir ./fcdata --project p.fcproj export out.mp4    # never returns
```

- It happened in all 4 tries, including `--start 0 --end 2`, `--gpu-rendering off` and `--format prores`.
- Same project with the clip transcoded to H.264 (`ffmpeg -i in.webm -c:v libx264 h.mp4`): the 10 s export finishes in about 12 s.
- `sample` of the hung process: the export thread waits in `rayon_core::latch::LockLatch::wait` under `filmcraft_export::job::render_batch`, while the `vp9-0` … `vp9-8` threads sit in `rayon_core::registry::WorkerThread::wait_until_cold`. That looks like a deadlock between the export pool and the VP9 decoder pool.

**Expected:** the export completes. If decoding stalls, the export should fail after a timeout with a clear error instead of hanging.

**Workaround we use today:** transcode VP9 sources to H.264 with ffmpeg before importing, and run CLI exports under a time limit.

Possibly related: #1195 (export freezes on Windows; codec not stated).

title: Windows: AVI oracle test doesn't compile (Unix-only `read_exact_at`)
author: Tom1tk
body:
`crates/avi/tests/ffmpeg_oracle.rs` (added in 2f4b5932) reads the file with `std::os::unix::fs::FileExt::read_exact_at`, which doesn't exist on Windows, so `cargo test --workspace` fails to compile there:

```
error[E0433]: cannot find `unix` in `os`
   --> crates\avi\tests\ffmpeg_oracle.rs:149:18
149 |         std::os::unix::fs::FileExt::read_exact_at(&self.0, buf, offset)
```

Since `--workspace` builds every test target, this stops the whole suite from running on Windows, not just the AVI tests.

## Fix
PR #1286

title: Can't import ADTS .aac files, including FilmCraft's own AAC export
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Raw ADTS `.aac` files are offered by File ▸ Import and the Media Browser (`aac` is in `AUDIO_EXTENSIONS`), but importing one always fails with `unrecognised format`. That includes the `.aac` FilmCraft writes itself with Export ▸ AAC Audio (#814), so an AAC export can't be brought back in. `.m4a` (AAC in MP4) imports fine.

**Repro:**
```sh
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i sine=frequency=440:sample_rate=48000:duration=3 -c:a aac -f adts tone.aac
filmcraft-cli import tone.aac
```
Or as a round trip: `filmcraft-cli --project p.fcproj export out.aac --format aac`, then `filmcraft-cli import out.aac`.

**Expected:** the file imports as an audio clip (ffprobe reads it as `aac`).

**Actual:**
```
filmcraft-cli: import: …/tone.aac: media: unsupported media: tone.aac: unrecognised format
```

**Cause:** `audio::opener` in `crates/codecs/src/audio.rs` only accepts `mp3 | mp2 | flac | ogg | oga | aif | aiff | aifc` by extension, so `.aac` gets past every opener without matching. The decoding pieces already exist (`adts_split` in the same file, `filmcraft_aac::config::split_adts` and `Decoder::from_adts`); nothing connects them to a standalone-file opener. There's no content-based fallback either: `mpeg_audio_layer` correctly rejects layer `00`, so an ADTS stream isn't sniffed as MPEG audio.

**Environment:** Linux (Fedora 44, KDE Plasma, Wayland), filmcraft 0.6.0, ffmpeg 8.1.3. The code paths above are unchanged on `main` @ 0541d4d1.

title: Import and Media Browser offer .y4m and .ale files that can never be imported
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Two file types are offered for import but can never be imported.

### `.y4m`
`y4m` is in `VIDEO_EXTENSIONS` (`crates/media/src/lib.rs`), so File ▸ Import and the Media Browser list Y4M files. But no opener reads YUV4MPEG2: that extension list is the only reference to it in the tree.

```sh
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc2=s=320x180:r=25:d=2 -pix_fmt yuv420p clip.y4m
filmcraft-cli import clip.y4m
# filmcraft-cli: import: …/clip.y4m: media: unsupported media: clip.y4m: unrecognised format
```

### `.ale`
The Media Browser lists `.ale` as a **project** file (`PROJECT_EXTENSIONS` in `crates/engine/src/media_browser.rs`), and FilmCraft writes ALE itself (File ▸ Export ▸ Avid Log Exchange). But nothing reads it: importing one from the browser fails the same way.

```sh
filmcraft-cli --project p.fcproj exec file.exportAle '{"path":"/tmp/clips.ale","items":[1]}'
filmcraft-cli exec mediaBrowser.import '{"paths":["/tmp/clips.ale"]}'
# filmcraft-cli: mediaBrowser.import: /tmp/clips.ale: media: unsupported media: clips.ale: unrecognised format
```

**Expected:** either read them (Y4M is a text header plus raw planar frames; ALE could become clips or offline clips carrying their log columns), or drop them from the lists so users aren't offered files that always fail.

**Environment:** Linux (Fedora 44, KDE Plasma, Wayland), filmcraft 0.6.0, ffmpeg 8.1.3. Both lists are unchanged on `main` @ 0541d4d1.

title: YCbCr TIFF stills fail to decode (e.g. any TIFF ffmpeg writes from YUV footage)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Uncompressed or PackBits TIFFs stored as YCbCr (PhotometricInterpretation 6) fail to decode. ffmpeg writes this kind of TIFF whenever the source is YUV, so an ordinary frame grab from H.264 footage (`ffmpeg -i clip.mp4 -frames:v 1 grab.tiff`) can't be imported, and neither can ffmpeg-made TIFF image sequences. RGB TIFFs and JPEG-compressed YCbCr TIFFs open fine.

**Repro:**
```sh
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc2=s=64x48 -frames:v 1 -pix_fmt yuv420p ycbcr.tiff
filmcraft-cli probe ycbcr.tiff
```
The file's tags: BitsPerSample 8,8,8, Compression 32773 (PackBits), Photometric 6 (YCbCr), SamplesPerPixel 3. `-pix_fmt yuv444p` fails the same way; `-pix_fmt rgb24` works.

**Expected:** the still imports.

**Actual:**
```
filmcraft-cli: ycbcr.tiff: decode error: ycbcr.tiff: The encoder or decoder for Tiff does not support the color type `Unknown(24)`
```

**Cause:** `crates/media/src/still.rs` decodes stills with `image::load_from_memory`. The `tiff` decoder underneath only handles YCbCr when it comes in as JPEG compression. Uncompressed and PackBits YCbCr (with or without `YCbCrSubSampling`) is rejected, so FilmCraft needs its own YCbCr→RGB path for these files.

**Environment:** Linux (Fedora 44, KDE Plasma, Wayland), filmcraft 0.6.0, ffmpeg 8.1.3. `still.rs` is unchanged on `main` @ 0541d4d1.

title: UI flickers on mouse movement in windowed mode with DX12 and Vulkan on Intel iGPU (GL works)
author: jlnzll
body:
## Description
The FilmCraft window flickers whenever I move the mouse over it, i.e. whenever it
redraws. It does not flicker in fullscreen mode. Possibly related:
storytold/lightcraft#326 (Dell Latitude 9450, also Intel Core Ultra iGPU) and
storytold/vectorcraft#752 (DX12 flicker, but caused by G-SYNC on NVIDIA – not
applicable here, this machine has no discrete GPU).

## Observations
- Flickers only while the mouse moves over the window
- Happens on both the internal laptop panel and an external Dell monitor
- Windowed mode: flickers / Fullscreen: no flicker
- Default backend (DX12): flickers
- `WGPU_BACKEND=vulkan`: still flickers
- `WGPU_BACKEND=gl`: **no flicker**

## System
- Device: Dell Latitude 7450
- OS: Windows 11 Pro 25H2 (build 26200.9457)
- CPU: Intel Core Ultra 7 165U
- GPU: Intel Graphics (integrated only), driver 32.0.101.8860 (2026-06-25)
- Displays: internal panel + external Dell monitor (flickers on both)
- FilmCraft version: 0.6.0

## Workaround
`setx WGPU_BACKEND gl`

title: H.264 export hangs at 0 % CPU (rayon deadlock in `rgba_to_yuv420_8`), H.264 source, macOS — related to #1283
author: olympusbackup111-cpu
body:
**Version:** filmcraft-cli 0.6.0 (release v0.6.0, macOS universal), macOS 14.5, Apple M2 Pro, 16 GB RAM.

### What happens

Exporting a 17.9 s vertical sequence to H.264 hangs most of the time. After about 1.5 s of output (an `out.mp4` of ~3.8 MB with no `moov` atom) the process drops to 0 % CPU and never returns. Rendering single frames from the same project works (`render --seconds S`, ~0.15 s per 1080×1920 frame).

This is like #1283, but the source is **H.264** (no VP9 anywhere) and the hang is in the **encoder** path, not in a decoder.

### Source and project

- One source clip: H.264 High, 1920×1080 with a 90° rotation tag (displayed 1080×1920), 29.97 fps (VFR from the camera, avg 2818125/94094), AAC 48 kHz stereo, MP4 from a Nikon camera, 26 s.
- Sequence imported from FCPXML 1.9 (`file.import`): 11 cuts of the same clip on V1/A1, custom 1080×1920 29.97. Import reports `linkedMedia: 1`, no errors, and the rotation is applied correctly.
- A Subtitle caption track imported from SRT (`captions.import`, 13 captions) and styled with `captions.setStyle`.

I can't share the footage (it's a client's), but I can share the FCPXML, the SRT and the `.fcproj`.

### Steps

```sh
filmcraft-cli --save-as p.fcproj run import.jsonl          # {"id":"file.import","params":{"paths":["reel.fcpxml"]}}
filmcraft-cli --project p.fcproj --save run captions.jsonl # captions.import + captions.setStyle
filmcraft-cli --project p.fcproj export out.mp4 --format h264 --gpu-rendering off --settings '{"burnCaptions":false}'
```

### Results (each run killed after 25–300 s)

| Run | GPU rendering | burnCaptions | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | auto | true (caption size 64) | **finished**, 23 s, peak RSS 1.5 GB |

title: Complete Cross-Platform GPU Rendering and Hardware Acceleration
author: kaivyy
body:
Problem

FilmCraft already has a cross-platform GPU compositor using "wgpu"/WGSL, GPU-accelerated effects, and platform-specific hardware decoding and encoding paths. However, several parts of the video pipeline still rely on CPU processing, and hardware acceleration is not yet equally available across Windows, Linux, and macOS.

According to the current roadmap, the remaining gaps include Linux hardware decoding, zero-copy frame transfer, GPU acceleration for remaining effects, and GPU-based export rendering.

This limits playback performance on demanding footage and prevents the application from fully benefiting from available GPU and hardware media engines.

Proposed solution

Implement a unified, capability-driven hardware acceleration architecture while preserving FilmCraft's cross-platform design.

1. Platform-specific hardware decoding

- Windows: continue using Media Foundation / Direct3D 11.
- macOS: use VideoToolbox.
- Linux: implement VA-API decoding, with Vulkan Video considered where appropriate.
- Preserve the existing software decoders as reliable fallbacks.

2. GPU-resident rendering pipeline

- Import hardware-decoded frames into GPU textures with minimal or zero-copy transfers where supported.
- Move remaining high-impact effects, transitions, blend modes, and adjustment layers to the existing WGSL compositor.
- Avoid unnecessary GPU-to-CPU-to-GPU transfers.

3. GPU export and hardware encoding

- Route export rendering through the existing GPU compositor when supported.
- Support platform-appropriate hardware encoders, including VideoToolbox, Media Foundation, and VA-API.
- Retain software encoding as a fallback.

4. Optional NVIDIA acceleration

- Continue the proposal in "Issue #473" (https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/issues/473) for NVIDIA-specific acceleration.
- Use NVENC for supported hardware encoding and consider NVDEC for decoding.
- Evaluate CUDA selectively for compute-heavy operations where it offers a measurable advantage over WG…

body:
## Summary

FilmCraft locks winit 0.30.13 without a winit patch, so it should have the Windows 11 mixed-DPI drag bug found in GridCraft (storytold/gridcraft#760, fix in storytold/gridcraft#761). Dragging the window across the boundary between monitors with different display scales makes it flip between the two scales and grow by their ratio.

**Expected effect in FilmCraft:** the window balloons and jumps during the drag. Past 8192 px the surface fails to configure. Once the GPU compositor has started, FilmCraft's uncaptured-error handler logs that instead of crashing; before then, or with the compositor disabled, it would be fatal.

This comes from reading FilmCraft's code at its current `main`, not from a run of FilmCraft. GridCraft, on the same stack, was reproduced and fixed on hardware.

## What happens (measured in GridCraft)

Windows 11 24H2, a 3440×1440 monitor at 100 % next to a 3840×2400 panel at 250 %. Dragging the window from the 250 % panel toward the top edge of the 100 % monitor, client size per step: 3600×2250 → 1440×900 → 3600×2250 → **9048×5757**. title: [Performance] Implement GPU-Resident Frame Pipeline for Zero-Copy Playback and Export
author: kaivyy
body:
[Performance] Implement GPU-Resident Frame Pipeline for Zero-Copy Playback and Export

Summary

FilmCraft already supports GPU compositing through "wgpu"/WGSL and hardware video decoding and encoding on supported platforms. However, decoded frames can still travel through CPU memory before reaching the GPU compositor, and GPU-rendered export frames can be read back to CPU memory before encoding.

This introduces unnecessary memory transfers, CPU overhead, and latency, particularly for 4K/8K footage, high-bit-depth media, multi-layer timelines, and effect-heavy projects.

The goal is to establish a GPU-resident frame pipeline that keeps frames on the GPU from hardware decoding through compositing and, where supported, hardware encoding.

Current problems

1. Hardware decoding does not always preserve GPU-resident frames

Some hardware decoding paths read frames back into CPU memory before uploading them to "wgpu" textures.

In "crates/gpu/src/lib.rs", "plane_texture()" uploads frame planes through "queue.write_texture()". This is useful for software-decoded frames but introduces additional transfers when the source frame already resides on the GPU.

2. GPU export still crosses the CPU boundary

"crates/gpu/src/export_renderer.rs" exposes rendered output as a CPU-side "Image". The underlying GPU readback path maps staging buffers and reconstructs CPU pixel data.

This prevents supported hardware encoders from consuming the rendered GPU resource directly.

3. Cross-platform GPU resource interoperability is incomplete

Native GPU resources have different ownership, synchronization, and import requirements:

- Windows: D3D11/D3D12 resources and shared handles.
- Linux: VA-API surfaces, DMA-BUF, and Vulkan resources.
- macOS: VideoToolbox pixel buffers, IOSurface, and Metal textures.

A shared abstraction is needed without forcing all platforms to use the same native API.

Proposed solution

Phase 1: Introduce a GPU-resident frame abstraction

Add an internal frame repres…

title: mpegts: MPEG-1 program stream cut inside a pack header panics (ps.rs slice out of range)
author: vangel76
body:
## Problem

`crates/mpegts/src/ps.rs` panics on an MPEG-1 program stream that ends inside its last pack header.

`packet_len` returns `Some(12)` for an MPEG-1 pack header (`b[4] >> 4 == 2`) as soon as `b.len() >= 6`. `scan` then reads the SCR with `pes::timestamp(&head[4..9])`. At the end of the file `head` can be only 6 to 8 bytes long, so the slice panics with `range end index 9 out of range`.

Minimal input (a whole file): `00 00 01 BA 21 00 00`. Any MPEG-1 PS cut inside its last pack header does the same.

A crash here loses the user's work (AGENTS.md section 0, never crash). The existing truncation fuzz test only covers transport streams.

The MPEG-2 branch is not affected: `packet_len` requires `b.get(13)`, so the 6 bytes `scan` reads are always there.

## Fix

Require the full 12-byte MPEG-1 pack header in `packet_len`; a shorter tail is then "not a packet" and goes through the normal resync path. Add program stream truncation tests (MPEG-1 and MPEG-2, every byte length).

title: mpegts: TS parse failure re-reads a whole block per packet (hostile file hangs the scan)
author: vangel76
body:
## Problem

`crates/mpegts/src/ts.rs`, `scan()`: every packet-parse failure takes the "lost sync" branch, which sets `k = usize::MAX`, breaks out of the block loop and re-reads a whole block (4096 packets, about 770 KB) from the new offset, while the offset only advances about one packet.

`packet()` returns `None` both for a bad sync byte and for an adaptation_field_length that runs past the packet (start > 188), including perfectly aligned packets. So a file of aligned packets `47 11 00 30 FF ...` (adaptation_field_length 255) makes `ByteSource::read_at` fetch roughly 1500x the file size: a 564 KB file caused 846 MB of reads, and a 1 GB file would read petabytes (effectively a hang on a hostile or damaged file).

Related, same code:
- `None => off = pos + got as u64` overshoots by `k * packet_size` and skips unread data (should be `off + got`).
- The 5-packet `first_sync` window only searches the current block and only start positions `0..packet_size`; beyond that it falls back to a single `0x47`, which can be a payload byte.

## Expected

- A bad adaptation field in an aligned packet is a warning (packet treated as having no payload), not lost sync.
- Resync happens inside the already-loaded block; the block is refilled from the file only when it is exhausted, so total reads stay close to the file size.
- Offsets stay exact after a resync.

title: mpegts: frame_info panics on a 6-byte AC-3 prefix; hostile streams grow chunks, units and allocations without bound
author: vangel76
body:
Hostile or damaged MPEG-TS files can panic `frame_info`, grow memory without bound, and index data that should be dropped (crates/mpegts).

Found by an audit, each confirmed with a throwaway test:

1. **Panic.** `frame_info(&Codec::Ac3, &[0x0B,0x77,0,0,0x1E,0x40])` (exactly 6 bytes) panics with index out of bounds at `es.rs` `b[6]`: `frame_len(Ac3)` guarantees 6 bytes, the code reads byte 6. Reachable through the public `fixed_packet_samples` in crates/codecs/src/audio.rs. E-AC-3 with fscod 3 and fscod2 3 also yields sample rate 0 instead of `None`.
2. **Chunk list grows for ever.** In the PES-delimited modes (LPCM, subtitles, unknown/private PIDs, H.264/HEVC) `Splitter::feed` pushes a chunk per TS packet but never pops, because the window that drives the pruning is unused there. 5000 feeds kept 5000 chunks until `finish()`.
3. **Unbounded allocation.** `read_unit` reserves `u.size` bytes up front (up to 4 GiB); an H.264 PID without PTS/DTS becomes a single unit of the whole PID. The unit table is uncapped: 4-byte E-AC-3 "frames" (`0B 77 00 01`, frmsiz 1) turned 40000 bytes into 9999 units of 64 bytes (16x amplification); ADTS about 9x, MPEG-2 start codes about 7x.
4. **Non-PES data is not dropped.** After a unit start that is not a PES header, `PesAsm` says "drop until the next unit start" but continuation packets are passed through (an ADTS stream behind a 184-byte garbage unit start produced 10 units). A unit-start packet with no payload (adaptation field only) resets the PES in progress.

Proposed fix, all in crates/mpegts: bounds-checked `frame_info`; no chunk bookkeeping in the PES modes; minimum E-AC-3 frame length, a per-stream cap on the unit table with a warning, `read_unit` preallocation capped and units over 128 MiB refused; a `dropping` state in `PesAsm` and AF-only unit starts ignored. Each with a regression test.

title: mpegts: H.264 recovery points are not random-access points; several access units in one PES become one unit
author: vangel76
body:
## Problem

`crates/mpegts/src/es.rs` forms H.264 / HEVC units wrongly in two ways.

1. **Recovery points are not random-access points.** An H.264 unit is `key` only for an IDR slice (NAL type 5). Broadcast, camcorder and cut transport streams often have non-IDR I pictures marked by a recovery point SEI (payload type 6) and no IDR after the first one, or none at all. `crates/codecs/src/mpeg.rs` then fails with "no random-access picture in the video stream" (file cannot be opened), or seeks always go back to the start.
2. **A unit is a PES packet, not an access unit.** The crate docs say H.264/HEVC are split at access unit delimiters / first slice, but the code starts a unit only at a PES with a timestamp. Muxers that put several access units in one PES (only the first has a PTS) give one merged unit: several frames are handed to the decoder under one PTS, and `key` / `disposable` are OR-combined over all of them.

## Fix

- Split H.264 / HEVC units at access-unit boundaries (ISO/IEC 14496-10 7.4.1.2.3, ISO/IEC 23008-2 7.4.2.4.4): AUD, parameter sets, SEI, or the first slice of a picture after the last VCL NAL of the previous one. The first access unit of a PES keeps the PES timestamps, later ones have none.
- H.264: a unit with a recovery point SEI is `key`.
- Tests: synthetic Annex-B streams in PES, plus an ffmpeg-generated open-GOP stream cut at a non-IDR recovery point (opens, decodes, matches the sequential decode).

title: mpegts: TS error/scrambled/duplicate packets reach the splitter; PMT changes half-apply
author: vangel76
body:
## Problem

`crates/mpegts/src/ts.rs` (transport stream scan and unit read):

1. `transport_error_indicator`, `transport_scrambling_control` and duplicate packets (same continuity counter, same content) are ignored. A flagged packet's garbage or encrypted payload goes into the elementary-stream splitter, and a duplicated packet's payload is fed twice.
2. PAT/PMT handling ignores `current_next_indicator` and `section_number`. A new PMT version only adds PIDs (`es.contains_key` -> `continue`), so a PID that changes codec keeps the old splitter and removed PIDs stay. The CRC is computed before the (cheap) version check, and the PAT is re-parsed on every repeat after the PMT PID is known.

## Expected

- TEI packets are dropped and counted in the scan warnings.
- Scrambled packets are skipped with a warning (not an error).
- Exact duplicate packets (same PID, same counter as the previous payload packet, identical payload) are dropped and counted; anything else is kept.
- The first PMT wins; a later differing PMT is ignored with one warning. Sections with `current_next_indicator` 0 are ignored. The PAT is not processed again once the PMT PID is known.

title: mpegts: pcr_range mixes all PIDs and ignores the PMT PCR_PID; timestamps share one unwrapper; SCR not unwrapped; language keeps NUL bytes
author: vangel76
body:
Found while auditing `crates/mpegts` (separate from #1429, #1430, #1432, #1436, #1437).

**1. `pcr_range` mixes the PCR of every PID on one timeline.** `ts::scan` takes a PCR from any packet that carries one and unwraps all of them against a single `last_pcr`. The PMT's `PCR_PID` (section bytes 8..9) is never read. Two PIDs with PCR bases 1000 and 2^32+5000, alternating, give `pcr_range = (300000, 1288515988800)` instead of a range of about 24 300 000 ticks.

**2. One `Unwrap` is shared by all elementary streams** (`ts.rs`, `ps.rs`). A PID with an independent time base flips the shared `last`. A reordered pre-wrap timestamp that arrives right after a first small one (base == 0) is not mapped below the wrap, so it comes back as about 2^33 and the next real wrap shifts everything after it. The doc says "relative to the first one seen" but the code returns absolute values. `base += WRAP` is unchecked.

**3. `File::pcr_range` doc says "First and last" but the value is min/max.** The program stream SCR is not unwrapped at all although the doc says "unwrapped", so a 33-bit SCR wrap gives a bogus range.

**4. PMT language is not sanitised.** `ISO_639_language_descriptor` bytes `00 00 00` give `Some("\0\0\0")`; `from_utf8_lossy(..).trim()` keeps NUL and control bytes.

Plan: read the PMT `PCR_PID` and only use that PID's PCR (first PCR PID seen when no PMT is known), one unwrapper per PID/stream, unwrap the SCR, correct both docs, accept only three ASCII letters as language. Each point gets a regression test.

title: mpegts: remove dead fields and stale docs, avoid copies and zero-fills
author: vangel76
body:
An audit of `crates/mpegts` found dead fields, stale docs and avoidable work. None of it changes behaviour.

Simplifications:
- `PesHeader.packet_length` is never read; `stream_id` is only read by one test.
- `Unit.pos` is documented as the "index of the packet" for transport streams, but it is a byte offset.
- `frame_bytes` in `es.rs` has a stale doc line above the real doc comment.

Avoidable work:
- `ps.rs` copies the 32-byte head and every pack, PSM and PES packet (up to 64 KB) with `to_vec()` before looking at it.
- `ps.rs` `Win::get` zero-fills at least 1 MiB on every window miss, even near the end of the file where only a few bytes can be read; the misses repeat for each packet whose length runs past the end.
- `crc32_mpeg` is a bitwise loop (8 shifts per byte) used for every PAT/PMT section.

I will do these in one PR, one commit each, with equality tests against the old implementations and counting tests (no timing). Items that sit in hunks of open PRs (#1431, #1433, #1434, #1438, #1440) are left out and will be listed in the PR.

title: Windows: allow --graphics gl as an opt-in for Intel Gen 9 iGPUs (DX12 falls back to the CPU compositor there)
author: malikbello
body:
On Intel Gen 9 / 9.5 graphics (UHD 620 here), OpenGL is the only backend where FilmCraft's GPU compositor runs, but it can only be reached through `WGPU_BACKEND=gl`. Could `--graphics` accept `gl` as an explicit opt-in?

## Why

- **Vulkan:** crashes in Intel's `igvk64.dll` (0xc0000005), as in #512, #1037 and #1425.
- **DirectX 12:** starts, but FXC can't compile the `fx` kernel, so it composites on the CPU (`GPU compositor failed to initialise; compositing on the CPU`).
- **The fallback order from #820:** reading `apps/filmcraft/src/graphics.rs` on main, Windows goes default (Vulkan + DX12), then DX12, then software. On these machines it ends on the CPU path. I haven't built main; this is from reading the code.

I understand why GL stays out of the automatic order on Windows (the `atio6axx.dll` crash in #477). So this asks only for a choice the user makes, never one made automatically.

## Measurements

FilmCraft 0.6.0 portable, Windows 11 Pro (build 26300), Dell Latitude 5400 (i7-8665U, 16 GB), Intel UHD 620 driver 31.0.101.2137, built-in demo project. Two runs, in alternating order. Playback was started with Space; after 5 s I read `shown` / `dropped` from `ui_inspect` over the control channel. The export was `filmcraft-cli --demo export out.mp4 --format h264 --start 2 --end 7`.

| `WGPU_BACKEND` | Start-up | GPU compositor | 5 s playback, shown / dropped | 5 s H.264 export |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| unset | crashes in `igvk64.dll` | n/a | n/a | n/a |
| `dx12` | 2.1 s, 2.6 s (23 s on the very first start) | no, CPU fallback | 44 / 60, 51 / 51 | 37.9 s, 41.6 s |
| `gl` | 1.5 s, 1.0 s | yes, nothing in the log | 71 / 33, 69 / 42 | 36.4 s, 36.8 s |

Playback is noticeably better on GL. Export time is the same either way, so exports look encoder-bound.

## Proposal

- `--graphics gl` (and the same choice wherever the graphics mode is offered in the app), never picked by the automatic fallback.
- Optionally, a hint in the Intel crash notice from #820: "On Int…

title: Hardware HEVC decoding falls back to software when an in-band PPS differs from hvcC only by a trailing zero byte
author: TramEFX
body:
**Version:** v0.6.0 (2ff3f5e); the same code is on main (71438c6). Windows 11, AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT, Media Foundation with the HEVC Video Extension 2.5.33.

**What happens:** a 3840×2160 60 fps HEVC Main MP4, muxed by ffmpeg (`Lavf60.16.100`), loses hardware decoding at its first sample:

```
Media Foundation HEVC failed (decode error: in-band parameter sets differ from the sample entry); continuing with the software decoder
```

The whole stream then decodes in software: about 17 fps in order at 4K for this file, so it cannot play in real time.

**Why:** `NalStreamInfo::parameters_changed` (`crates/codecs/src/hw.rs:176`) compares each in-band VPS/SPS/PPS byte for byte with the `hvcC` copies, and `HybridDecoder::decode` (`crates/platform/src/hybrid.rs:188`) falls back on any difference. In this file the VPS and SPS are identical. The PPS differs only by one zero byte after its RBSP trailing bits:

- `hvcC` PPS: `44 01 e0 f7 c0 4c 90 00`
- in-band PPS (first sample): `44 01 e0 f7 c0 4c 90`

So the same PPS reads as a parameter-set change.

**Suggested fix:** compare parameter sets with trailing zero bytes removed (or compare their RBSPs).

**Impact:** possibly common: many capture and screen-recording tools mux with ffmpeg. I can't share the file (a personal recording), but the bytes above are the whole difference between its stored and in-band parameter sets.

title: [Bug] Adjustment Layer with 3D/Transform effects does not replace underlying buffer (background remains visible underneath)
author: Mattys03
body:
### Describe the bug
When applying a 3D effect, perspective distortion, or transform/motion properties to an Adjustment Layer, the compositor renders the transformed adjustment layer on top of the sequence, but the original underlying clips (e.g., on track V1) remain visible and untransformed in the background.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Place a video or image clip on track V1.
2. Place an Adjustment Layer on track V2 directly above it.
3. Apply a 3D / Perspective effect or modify Transform/Motion properties on the Adjustment Layer (rotate, skew, or scale down).
4. Observe the Program monitor.

### Expected behavior (Premiere Pro parity)
An adjustment layer should capture and transform the underlying composite buffer. The transformed output should replace the layers beneath it. Areas outside the transformed adjustment layer boundaries should show empty/transparent/black background, rather than leaving the original untransformed V1 clip visible underneath.

### Actual behavior
The underlying V1 clip continues to render statically in its original position, while the adjustment layer's transformed version is drawn over it as a duplicate overlay.

### Environment
- OS: Windows 11
- Filmcraft version: latest build

title: GPU export deadlocks at a random frame: workers block in `RendererPool::with` while renderer holders wait on stolen ProRes decode work (0.7.2, macOS)
author: andrewuscf
body:
**Version:** FilmCraft 0.7.2 desktop app (`71438c6`), macOS 27.0.1, MacBook Pro M3 Max (16 cores), 128 GB.

### What happens

With GPU rendering on (`gpuRendering: auto`, the default), an H.264 export of a 4K sequence cut from a ProRes clip stops making frames at a random point. FilmCraft then sits at about 0% CPU for good. `jobs.cancel` doesn't end it; the app has to be quit. With `gpuRendering: off`, the same exports finish every time.

### Repro (generated media)

```sh
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc2=size=3840x2160:rate=25:duration=30 -c:v prores_ks -profile:v 3 -pix_fmt yuv422p10le pattern.mov
```

1. New project with a 3840×2160, 25 fps sequence.
2. Import `pattern.mov` and place it 10 times end to end on V1 (5:00 total).
3. Export Media: H.264, hardware encoding Auto, GPU rendering Auto, entire sequence.

I drove these steps through the control channel (`file.newSequence`, `file.import`, `timeline.place` ×10, then `file.exportMedia` with `format: "h264"` and `settings: {"gpuRendering": "auto"}`).

| GPU rendering | Result |
|---|---|
| auto | stuck at frame 728 / 7,500 after 80 s, 7% CPU |
| off | finished 7,500 / 7,500 in 120 s |

The same happened on a longer 4K 25 fps sequence (one ProRes clip cut many times, under PNG stills and text). With `auto` it got stuck twice, at frame 2,592 and at frame 1,120. With `off` it finished every time.

### Where it's stuck (`sample` of the stuck repro, condensed)

```
4 workers hold a GPU renderer and wait for their ProRes decode's stolen bands:
  render_batch → Pipeline::frame → RendererPool::with → (GPU render) → filmcraft_prores::decode::decode_frame_into
    → bands.par_iter_mut() (prores/src/decode.rs:219) → WorkerThread::wait_until_cold → cond_wait

4 workers stole a frame job while waiting inside a join, and now wait for a free renderer:
  … decode_frame_into → wait_until_cold → render_batch → Pipeline::frame → RendererPool::with
    → Condvar::wait (export/src/pipeline.rs:83)
  One of these is itself a renderer holde…

title: [UX / Parity] Zoom shortcuts (+ / -) should zoom the active panel (Effect Controls / Keyframe editor) instead of always targeting the main timeline
author: Mattys03
body:
### Describe the issue / Parity gap
In Premiere Pro, horizontal timeline zoom shortcuts (`+` / `=` to zoom in, `-` to zoom out) are context-sensitive to the currently active/focused panel:
- When the sequence **Timeline** has focus, `+` / `-` zooms the sequence timeline tracks.
- When the **Effect Controls** panel (keyframe track / graph editor) has focus, `+` / `-` zooms into the keyframe editor's time ruler, allowing fine adjustment of keyframes and bezier curves without altering the sequence timeline zoom.

In Filmcraft, pressing the zoom shortcuts always routes the zoom command to the main sequence timeline at the bottom, even when the Effect Controls / Keyframe Graph Editor panel is clicked and focused.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Select a clip with animated parameters (e.g., Scale / Position keyframes or curves).
2. Click inside the **Effect Controls / Clip Properties** keyframe or graph area on the left to focus it.
3. Press `+` (zoom in) or `-` (zoom out).
4. Observe that the main sequence timeline at the bottom zooms in/out instead of zooming the keyframe graph ruler.

### Expected behavior (Premiere Pro parity)
Keyboard zoom shortcuts should be dispatched to the currently focused panel:
- If Effect Controls / Keyframe Graph Editor is focused -> zoom the keyframe editor time axis.
- If Sequence Timeline is focused -> zoom the sequence timeline.

### Environment
- OS: Windows 11
- Filmcraft version: latest build

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1e0f2284-a393-4975-b705-c53d8f8e1b32

title: [Bug / Parity] Right-clicking Timeline Time Ruler opens clip context menu instead of ruler menu (Mark In/Out, Mark Selection)
author: Mattys03
body:
### Describe the bug / Parity gap
When right-clicking on the **Timeline Time Ruler** (the top timecode ruler area where the playhead indicator moves):
1. **Bug:** Filmcraft currently opens the **Clip Context Menu** (showing "Edit Original", "Cut", "Copy", "Label", "Speed/Duration", etc.), as if a timeline clip was right-clicked.
2. **Missing Parity:** The Time Ruler lacks its dedicated context menu found in Premiere Pro, preventing quick In/Out range operations (especially "Mark Selection").

### Steps to reproduce
1. Select any clip on the timeline.
2. Move the cursor up to the grey **Time Ruler bar** (above the video tracks).
3. Right-click anywhere on the time ruler.
4. Notice that the clip context menu pops up instead of a time ruler menu.

### Expected behavior (Premiere Pro parity)
Right-clicking the timeline time ruler should NOT trigger the clip context menu. Instead, it should open the **Time Ruler Context Menu** with timeline marking actions:
- **Mark In** (`I`)
- **Mark Out** (`O`)
- **Mark Selection** (sets In and Out points to match the boundaries of selected clip(s))
- **Mark Clip** (`X`)
- **Clear In**
- **Clear Out**
- **Clear In and Out**

### Environment
- OS: Windows 11
- Filmcraft version: latest build

title: bug(mcp): bridge stops responding after a slow command; every later call times out until the MCP host restarts
author: sudsarkar13
body:
**Environment**
- FilmCraft **0.6.0** (Linux x86_64), started with `filmcraft --control 47800`, driven through the FilmCraft MCP server (bridge mode) from the Claude desktop app 2.7032.0 (Electron 44.4.3). Not yet retested on 0.7.2.
- Ubuntu Linux x64, Lenovo IdeaPad Flex 5 14ALC05
- Media: 1920x1080, 60 fps H.264/AAC MP4, 18 min 40 s, 86 MB; edited into 1080x1920 30 fps sequences

**What happens**
During one editing session, a command did not answer within the MCP client's 60 s limit. After that, **every** command timed out the same way, including read-only ones (`project_inspect`, `command_list`, `export.queue.list`). Restarting FilmCraft alone did not restore it; only restarting the MCP host (which restarts the MCP server process) did. This happened four times in one session.

Commands that preceded a hang: `render_frame` (filed separately), `ui_screenshot`, and also ordinary edits: `file.newSequence`, `timeline.place` (sourceIn about 1091 s into an 18-min file), `captions.setStyle`, and `export.queue.list` while an export was running. Several of these had actually been applied (seen later via `project_inspect`), so the work was done but the reply never arrived.

**Expected**
- A slow command should not block the bridge for later calls (or should fail with an error), and the bridge should recover on its own.
- A call that times out on the client side should still be discoverable as applied / not applied.

Possibly related: #91, #92 (bridge export timeouts, closed), #1477.

title: bug(export): a file.exportMedia job started with wait:false can't be tracked over the bridge (not in export.queue.list)
author: sudsarkar13
body:
**Environment**
- FilmCraft **0.6.0** (Linux x86_64), started with `filmcraft --control 47800`, driven through the FilmCraft MCP server (bridge mode). Not yet retested on 0.7.2.
- Ubuntu Linux x64, Lenovo IdeaPad Flex 5 14ALC05 (CPU export, no NVIDIA GPU)

**Steps**
1. `file.exportMedia {"path": "/home/.../clip.mp4", "format": "h264", "width": 1080, "height": 1920, "fps": 30, "bitrateMode": "crf", "crf": 20, "audio": true, "burnCaptions": true, "loudnessLufs": -14, "sequence": 11, "range": "entire", "wait": false}` returns `{"job": 1, "path": "..."}`.
2. About 45 seconds later, `export.queue.list` returns `{"items": [], "running": false}`, while the MP4 is still growing on disk (it kept growing for roughly another minute).

**Actual**
There's no way to get the status or progress of job 1. The only signal is the file size changing. Reading the file before it finishes gives "moov atom not found". A ~20 s 1080x1920 export took 2-4 minutes on this machine, so an agent has to poll the file system and guess when it's done.

**Expected**
The job returned by `file.exportMedia` is queryable by id (or listed in `export.queue.list` with progress), with a clear completion / failure state.

Related (closed): #91, #92 for the `wait: true` case.

title: mcp: usability gaps for agents (command_list output size, crop not discoverable in effects.list, null return values)
author: sudsarkar13
body:
**Environment**
- FilmCraft **0.6.0** (Linux x86_64), started with `filmcraft --control 47800`, driven through the FilmCraft MCP server (bridge mode) by an AI agent. Not yet retested on 0.7.2.

Three small things that made agent-driven editing harder:

**1. `command_list` output is too large for agents**
Calling `command_list` without a filter returns about 188,000 characters (~7,900 lines of JSON), more than an agent's context can take in one go. A compact mode (ids + labels only) or pagination would help; the `filter` / `enabled_only` options work but you need to know what to filter for first.

**2. `crop` is hard to discover**
`effects.list {"kind": "Video", "folder": "Video Effects/Transform", "detail": true}` does not list `crop`, but `effects.apply {"clips": [15], "effect": "crop"}` works (params top/bottom/left/right/feather/zoom). It would help if `effects.list` made crop findable (e.g. listed in Transform, as in Premiere, or searchable by name).

**3. Some commands return `null` instead of the created ids**
`file.newProject` and `effects.apply` return `null`. Other commands return what they created (`file.newSequence` -> `{"sequence": 42}`, `timeline.place` -> `{"clips": [44, 45]}`), which saves an extra `sequence_inspect` round trip. Returning the new project id / the applied effect's index would make these consistent.

title: Feature: Drag to check or uncheck multiple checkboxes
author: Gamedirection
body:
### Description

Allow checking or unchecking several checkboxes in one drag, as in the other Craft apps. All Craft apps must work the same way.

- VectorCraft: storytold/vectorcraft#1477, PR storytold/vectorcraft#1600
- PhotoCraft: storytold/photocraft#3333, PR storytold/photocraft#3521
- PDFCraft: storytold/pdfcraft#1662

### Requested behaviour

- Press on a checkbox and drag over its neighbours. Each checkbox that the pointer goes over takes the new state of the first one, until you release the button.
- A click toggles one checkbox, as before.
- A mixed (dash) checkbox stays as it is during a drag.
- Put the change in the shared checkbox widget of FilmCraft, so Preferences, dialogs and panels all get it at the same time.

### Reference

VectorCraft PR #1600 and PhotoCraft PR #3521 use the same design. A `drag_toggle` helper in the shared checkbox keeps the new state while the primary button is down. Every checkbox that the pointer goes over takes that state. A test presses on the first checkbox, drags over the next ones, and checks that they all have the same state.

title: GPU export composites an untagged portrait H.264 clip ~15 levels darker than the CPU path
author: bsoulai
body:
Found while working on #799, on the 0.6.0 release CLI first and then on a branch of 0.7.2 (same picture, bit-identical GPU output on both).

**Setup.** A 2160x3840 sequence. At one frame the picture is an untagged 1080x1920 H.264 clip (a "breaking news" bumper, portrait, no colour tags in the container) scaled 200 % to fill, with a 40 % opacity texture layer over it. `file.exportFrame` at that time, full resolution, `gpuRendering: "auto"` vs `"off"`.

**Result.** GPU vs CPU on 8-bit values: p99 27–28, mean 1.8–2.4. The GPU picture is about 15 levels darker across the bright band of the bumper. The golden tolerance in the repo is p99 ≤ 6 and mean < 1.5.

Other frames of the same sequence, where the layers are ProRes 4444 and a tagged 1080x1920 H.264 talking-head clip, pass (p99 2, mean 0.12–0.16). So the compositor is not the difference; it's how the two paths treat this one clip.

**Guess, not verified:** the CPU and GPU paths assume different YCbCr matrices or ranges for an untagged portrait H.264 clip (601 vs 709, or limited vs full range), and the texture layer does not matter.

**Repro.** Any untagged 1080x1920 H.264 clip scaled up on a 2160x3840 sequence, exportFrame with gpuRendering auto and off, compare. I can share the measured numbers for the specific frame; the footage itself is from a production and I'd rather not attach it, but a synthetic untagged portrait clip should show it if the guess is right.

title: FCP7 XML import: Premiere writes nested-sequence clips with center -0.5 -0.5 (anchor top-left); they land at the top-left corner instead of centred
author: bsoulai
body:
**Version:** FilmCraft 0.7.2 (release, macOS universal CLI and app), macOS, Apple M1 Max. Also seen on 0.6.0.

### What happens

Importing a Final Cut Pro 7 XML exported by Premiere Pro (27.1 Beta, `exportAsFinalCutProXML`) of a 2160x3840 sequence: every **media** clip whose Motion `center` is `0 0` in the XML lands correctly at the sequence centre (position 1080, 1920). Every **nested sequence** clip with the same `center` `0 0` lands at position **0, 0**, i.e. its centre at the top-left corner of the frame, so only its bottom-right quadrant is visible.

Two nests in this project, both wrong the same way:

- the outer sequence holds the whole episode as one nest (`LCB Scene 1 v5 (thought)`, XML `center` horiz 0 vert 0, `scale` 200): imported position `Vec2 { x: 0.0, y: 0.0 }`, scale 200
- inside it, a `LCB TV Texture` nest on V10 (scale 200): imported position `0.0, 0.0`

Readback after `file.import` + `sequence.open`, via `inspect sequence` (same sequence, same import):

```
V1  breaking-news.mp4           pos Vec2 { x: 1080.0, y: 1920.0 }  scale 200   <- media, correct
V1  lcb-bg-tv-wall-approved.mov pos Vec2 { x: 1080.0, y: 1920.0 }  scale 100   <- media, correct
V4  lcb-eyes-blue-4k.mov        pos Vec2 { x: 1080.0, y: 1920.0 }  scale 100   <- media, correct
V10 LCB TV Texture (nest)       pos Vec2 { x: 0.0, y: 0.0 }        scale 200   <- nest, wrong
outer V1 LCB Scene 1 v5 (nest)  pos Vec2 { x: 0.0, y: 0.0 }        scale 200   <- nest, wrong
outer V2 Graphic (media)        pos Vec2 { x: 1080.0, y: 1920.0 }  scale 100   <- media, correct
```

In FCP7 XML `center` is relative to the sequence centre (`0 0` = centred), which the importer already applies to media clipitems; the nested-sequence clipitem path seems to take `0 0` literally.

### Expected

A nested sequence with `center` `0 0` is centred like any other clip (1080, 1920 on this sequence).

### Workaround

`effects.setParam` on each nest clip: `motion` / `position` = `[1080, 1920]`. That is what we do aft…

title: Unreadable-media placeholder is opaque and full-frame: one unsupported .aegraphic overlay hides the whole composition
author: bsoulai
body:
**Version:** FilmCraft 0.7.2 (release, macOS universal), Apple M1 Max. Same on 0.6.0.

### What happens

A Premiere Pro FCP7 XML import brings Motion Graphics Template instances in as `.aegraphic` movie items (`Motion Graphics Template Media/<uuid>/LCB Countdown.aegraphic` etc.). FilmCraft cannot read them, which is fair. But the placeholder it draws for an unreadable clip is an **opaque, full-frame card** ("MEDIA UNREADABLE / LCB Countdown.aegraphic / File ▸ Link Media… reconnects it") sized to the layer, and these template layers are full-frame overlays on the top tracks (V5 to V8 here). One unsupported overlay therefore covers the whole composition: the keyed talent, the wall, the other graphics, everything under it is invisible in the Program monitor and in every exported frame, and four stacked templates make it four cards deep.

Exported frame at 5 s of an 11-track 2160x3840 episode after import: the entire frame is the card for the top-most `.aegraphic`, nothing of the eight tracks beneath it shows.

### Expected (either would do)

1. The unreadable-media card is translucent or confined (a badge in a corner of the layer's bounds, or a thin hatched border), so the rest of the composition stays visible while the clip is offline. The Project panel already marks the item; the Program monitor doesn't need to shout at full size.
2. `.aegraphic` (and `.mogrt`) is recognised as a known-unsupported format and imported as an **empty graphic layer** with the template's name and its `Graphic Parameters` values kept as metadata, rather than an unreadable movie. That keeps the track structure and timing for a rebuild with `graphics.template.*` (which is what we do by hand today: all four of our templates were rebuilt as FilmCraft graphics templates).

### Repro

Export any Premiere sequence containing a .mogrt instance as FCP7 XML, `file.import` it, render a frame under the template's span.

title: Auto Reframe Sequence command is absent; only per-clip Auto Reframe effect is available
author: earlvanze
body:
## Report

title: Unicode image-sequence filenames trigger a UTF-8 boundary panic
author: nuclearspike
body:
A valid numbered image sequence such as `é0001.png` can hit an internal UTF-8 boundary panic and fail to import. The same failure applies to CJK and emoji characters immediately before the frame number.

1. Put small PNGs named `é0001.png` and `é0002.png` together.
2. Import the first with `file.import {"paths":["/path/é0001.png"],"imageSequence":true}`.
3. The shared filename parser slices inside `é` instead of identifying the sequence. The command returns an error for the valid import.

Expected: retain the entire UTF-8 prefix, padding and sibling paths, then open/play the frames. `Numbered::parse` adds one to the byte offset where the preceding character begins, assuming that character is ASCII.

Reproduced at `71438c627b5cbcfb550526c3971f4d0037733c5c`. The retained parser regression and `import_unicode_image_sequence_with_missing_frames` engine regression both fail on baseline production with `start byte index 1 is not a char boundary`, then pass after the repair. The engine regression exercises `Session::execute("file.import", ...)`, decoded frame values, missing-frame handling, explicit sequence import and timeline placement; the existing ASCII case remains intact and passes on baseline too.

The repaired parser regression covers accented, CJK, emoji and decomposed prefixes, with positive and negative sibling/digit controls. `cargo test --release -p filmcraft-media` passes 66 tests; `cargo test --release -p filmcraft-engine image_sequence_tests::` passes 7. Tested headlessly on macOS 27.0 (26A428), Apple Silicon, Rust 1.97.1. Desktop UI, Windows and Linux were not exercised locally.

title: Feature (new Craft App/Protocol) - Newtek NDI replacement...
author: gNovp
body:
This suggestion isn't only related to FilmCraft, but to all video related Craft Apps in fact. I just didn't know where to submit this, so feel free to move that topic where it fits.

### What is NDI ?
NDI is a great protocol and suite of apps developped by Newtek, allowing LAN transmission of live video and audio. It is widely used nowadays in the broadcast industry, and other usecases like live shows etc. It's typical usecase is to screencapture the display of a computer, and display it live on other computers in the same network.

This allows multiple usecases, like:
- Digital Signage (sending live video to screens in venues)
- Using the local network to ingest multiple computers into OBS Studio (via the DistroAV plugin here: https://github.com/DistroAV/DistroAV), or other apps with a plugin (like Premiere Pro)
- Showing easily a computer screen over the network

It's free (as in money), but proprietary software running only on Windows and Mac since years (Newtek ignoring the growing userbase of Linux users). Plus it now requires installation and registration, whereas it wasn't the case in earlier releases (these were portable apps in the beginning).

### What could be developped ?
The NDI suite of apps has multiple programs, but only a few are really key: ScreenCapture utility and NDI Monitor. In addition, a third party plugin has been developped for OBS Studio (DistroAV), and other third party integrations are available in live creative software (Editing software, VJing tools, etc).

title: Crash (SIGSEGV) when cancelling an NVENC export: Session dropped with pictures still in flight
author: Jonathan-de-Villiers
body:
## Summary

Cancelling an export that uses the NVENC encoder segfaults the whole app (Linux, NVIDIA). It happens every time we cancel. The output file is left unfinished (`moov atom not found`).

**Environment:** FilmCraft v0.6.0 (main @ 78fe0102), Arch Linux / Hyprland, RTX 3050 Laptop GPU, NVIDIA driver 610.57.04, NVDEC decoding on.

## Backtrace (crashing thread = export worker)

```
#0  libnvcuvid.so.1 + 0xdc2eb          <- SEGV_MAPERR
#1  libnvcuvid.so.1 + 0xdec74
#2-6 libnvidia-encode.so.1
#7  drop_glue<filmcraft_platform::nvenc::session::Session>
#8  drop_glue<filmcraft_platform::nvenc::export::NvencEncoder>
#9  drop_glue<filmcraft_export::job::Exporter>
#10 filmcraft_export::export
#11 filmcraft_engine::export_tools::guard_job<spawn_export::{closure#4}>
```

A second core from a cancel has a corrupted crashing stack (gdb can't unwind it). That fits memory being freed while still in use.

## Likely cause

On cancel:

1. `crates/export/src/job.rs:442` sees `progress.cancel` and returns `Err(ExportError::Cancelled)`.
2. The `Exporter` is dropped, and with it `NvencEncoder` and `Nvenc`, **without `Nvenc::flush()` ever running**. `flush()` (`crates/platform/src/nvenc/mod.rs:448`) is the only place that sends EOS and locks/reads the pictures still in flight.
3. `Nvenc` has no `Drop`, so `impl Drop for Session` (`crates/platform/src/nvenc/session.rs:632`) calls `nvEncDestroyInputBuffer` / `nvEncDestroyBitstreamBuffer` / `nvEncDestroyEncoder` while `pending` is non-empty, i.e. on buffers NVENC is still encoding into.

On a normal finish, `flush()` drains `pending` first, which explains why only cancelled exports crash.

## Proposed fix

Add `impl Drop for Nvenc` that, when `pending` is non-empty, calls `session.end_of_stream()` and then `read_oldest()` until `ready == 0`, ignoring errors. That way no buffer is in flight when `Session` destroys it. If that alone isn't enough, also check that the shared CUDA context (used by NVDEC too) is current during teardown.

title: Still images ignore EXIF orientation (portrait phone photos import sideways)
author: Jonathan-de-Villiers
body:
## Summary

Portrait phone photos (JPEG with an EXIF `Orientation` tag) import at their stored size and show **sideways** in the Program monitor. ffmpeg, image viewers and browsers show them upright.

**Environment:** FilmCraft v0.6.0 (main @ 78fe0102), Linux.

## Details

An iPhone JPEG stored as 5712×4284 with `Orientation = 6` (rotate 90° CW) is placed at 5712×4284. The Motion anchor is `(2856, 2142)`, the unrotated size.

## Repro

1. Import a portrait iPhone photo.
2. Place it in a sequence. The picture is rotated 90°.

## Workaround

Motion ▸ Rotation `90`, then scale to fit by hand.

## Proposed fix

PR #2 applied the container display matrix for phone **video**. Stills need the same: in the still-image decoder, read EXIF `Orientation` (0x0112, values 1–8 including the mirrored ones) and apply the rotate/flip on decode. Alternatively, expose it like video's display matrix, so the Motion anchor and "Scale to Frame Size" use the upright dimensions. A test fixture per orientation value would cover it. (#1068 and #826 touched the stills import path.)

title: bug(control): requests stall/time out while the window is hidden on Wayland; timed-out commands still run
author: Jonathan-de-Villiers
body:
## Summary

When driving the running app over `--control <port>`, requests sometimes wait 15–110 s, or indefinitely. Anything over 60 s comes back as `{"ok": false, "error": "timeout"}` (`apps/filmcraft/src/control_server.rs:77`). **The command still runs later**, so a client that retries on timeout applies the edit twice.

**Environment:** FilmCraft v0.6.0 (main @ 78fe0102), Linux, Hyprland (Wayland).

## Root cause

During a 10+ minute stall, the FilmCraft window was on a Hyprland workspace that wasn't shown (hidden, not minimised). The main thread was asleep in `epoll_wait` (0 % CPU) and the GPU was idle. On Wayland a hidden surface gets no frame callbacks, so `ctx.request_repaint()` in `serve()` never produces a frame. The queued request is not drained until the window is visible again.

This is the same class of problem as macOS App Nap, which `app_nap.rs` already works around, but on Wayland.

## Repro

1. `filmcraft --control 9876`
2. Move the window to a workspace that isn't shown.
3. Send `{"method":"perf.stats"}`. No reply comes for as long as the window stays hidden (`timeout` after 60 s).

## Suggestions

1. Don't drain control requests only inside the egui frame. Handle them from an event-loop wake-up (`EventLoopProxy::send_event` + `user_event`, which winit delivers even when no frame is requested) or on a timer.
2. On timeout, say whether the command was dropped or is still queued (or return a request id that can be polled), so clients don't double-apply edits.

Related: #91 (closed, different cause), #1538 (MCP bridge stops responding after a slow command).

title: Whisper transcription on NVIDIA GPUs (candle CUDA backend)
author: Jonathan-de-Villiers
body:
## Summary

Whisper transcription runs CPU-only (`Device::Cpu` is hard-coded in `crates/speech/src/whisper/model.rs`). On longer clips that's slow: an 8.5 min clip on `whisper-small` takes minutes, while an NVIDIA GPU sits idle. Proposal: an opt-in CUDA backend alongside the Metal one in #1178.

## Proposal

1. **Cargo feature**, opt-in so CI / wasm / non-CUDA users are unaffected:
   `whisper-cuda = ["whisper", "candle-core/cuda", "candle-nn/cuda"]` in `crates/speech`, forwarded through `filmcraft-engine`, `filmcraft` and `filmcraft-cli` like `whisper` is today. This mirrors the `metal` feature in #1178.
2. **Device selection** in `Model::load`: `Device::cuda_if_available(0)` when compiled in, else CPU. Add an override (e.g. `FILMCRAFT_SPEECH_DEVICE=cpu|cuda` or a `device` param on `transcript.generate`) to force CPU when the GPU is busy or out of memory.
3. **Precision:** consider `DType::F16` on CUDA (halves VRAM); keep F32 on CPU.
4. Make sure every tensor in the model/decoder code uses `self.device`, not `Device::Cpu`.
5. Report the device in `transcript.models` output (e.g. `"device": "cuda:0"`).
6. Document the feature and the CUDA toolkit requirement in `docs/transcripts.md`.

Related: #1178 (Metal), #982 (STT in official builds), #473 (NVIDIA CUDA/NVENC fast lane).

```

```

Start FilmCraft and attempt to open a file (File → Open, drag in a clip, etc.).

A file-open dialog opens (native portal, GTK, or any usable picker).

title: Unicode file URLs trigger a UTF-8 boundary panic during EDL import
author: nuclearspike
body:
Importing an EDL containing `file:///日本語.mov` panics in `file_url_to_path` before the media reference can be imported. Reproduced against main `fae7f8a9be09bd74f95fbe08c3d98adc17fe1030`.

Pass this synthetic EDL to `filmcraft_interchange::import(bytes, Format::Edl, None)`:

```text
TITLE: Unicode media
FCM: NON-DROP FRAME
001 AX V C 00:00:00:00 00:00:01:00 00:00:00:00 00:00:01:00
* SOURCE FILE: file:///日本語.mov

title: Timeline: zooming all the way out shows hours of empty space and the clips vanish
author: ReReddo
body:
**What happens**
Zoom out (Alt+wheel, the minus key, the zoom bar's handles, or the Zoom tool with Alt). The Timeline keeps zooming until the ruler shows many hours, although its extent is the sequence plus ten minutes. A 38 second sequence ends up a few pixels wide, and an empty sequence shows eight hours.

**Expected**
The farthest zoom-out shows the whole Timeline extent in the view and no more (the zoom bar's thumb fills its track). A 38 second sequence then shows its clips across the first sixteenth of the view, as it does when the bar is full.

**Cause**
Every zoom path clamps to a fixed floor of 0.05 points per second. The scroll limit already follows the extent, so only the zoom floor is missing.

**Proposed**
One lower bound, view width divided by `timeline_extent(sequence)`, applied where the zoom is applied.

**Expected**

title: Dock: dragging a divider also resizes panels that are not next to it
author: ReReddo
body:
**What happens**
Drag the divider between two panels: panels elsewhere in the same row also change size. Some narrow panels (Tools, the audio meters) end up much wider than they were set, and snap to a smaller size when their own divider is touched.

**Expected**
A divider moves only the two panels beside it. The others keep their size, and fixed-size panels keep theirs.

**Cause**
Splits are stored as ratios. Moving an outer divider changes the space of a whole subtree, and every ratio split inside it rescales, so panels that were never touched are resized.

**Proposed**
When a divider moves, the ratios of the splits behind it are adjusted in the same step so only the panel next to the divider takes the change.

title: Windows: GPU export silently renders on the CPU (export instance takes DX12, FXC fails on `fx`)
author: brunomcps
body:
On Windows the **export** renderer silently composites every frame on the CPU, even with `--gpu-rendering auto` on a machine with a working NVIDIA GPU. The cause is the same FXC failure the window already avoids: `ExportRenderer::new()` creates its own `wgpu::Instance::default()` and takes the default adapter, which on Windows is a DX12 one, so the `fx` compute pipeline goes through FXC and the device is retired before the first frame.

## What I see

FilmCraft 0.7.2 (official MSI and a build of the `v0.7.2` tag), Windows 11 Home build 26300, Samsung Galaxy Book (22 logical CPUs, 32 GB), NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4050 Laptop (driver 32.0.16.1742) + Intel Arc iGPU.

Project: a 3840×2160 30 fps sequence, 2 minutes of H.264 4K camera footage on V1 and four 1080p ProRes 4444 clips with alpha on V2/V3 (fit to frame).

`filmcraft-cli --project p.fcproj export out.mp4 --format h264 --gpu-rendering auto --settings '{"hardwareEncoding":"auto"}'`

With a few `eprintln!`s added to read `filmcraft_gpu::export_renderer::timing::get()` and `filmcraft_export::gpu_render_stats()` after the export (the CLI never initialises a logger, so the `log::error!` in `mark_device_failed` is not visible):

```
[diag pipeline] gpu_rendering=Auto renderer_pool=true
GPU export disabled: GPU error: Validation Error
Caused by:
  In Device::create_compute_pipeline, label = 'fx'
    Internal error: FXC D3DCompile error (0x80004005): internal error: compilation aborted unexpectedly
gpu render stats: frames=0 fallbacks=60 device_failed=true
```

`nvidia-smi` agrees: 0 % 3D utilisation during the export, only the encoder busy.

## Measurements (same 2-minute sequence, same machine)

| Build | Export time | GPU frames |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.7.2 official, `--gpu-rendering auto` | 494 s (no hardware encode) / ~17 fps with `hardwareEncoding: auto` | 0 (all CPU) |
| 0.7.2 + export instance on **Vulkan** | 174 s | 3600 / 3600, 0 fallbacks |
| + `map_accumulator` f16→f32 rows converted with `par_chunks_exact_mut` …

title: Add Linux loongarch64 build
author: MQ-mengqing
body:
Since #830 add riscv build, I'd like to ask whether **Linux loongarch64** build could be considered as well.

FilmCraft compiles and runs fine natively on a loongarch64 Arch Linux machine, and `cargo test --workspace` passes there.
With just the one-line packaging diff below plus a small cross-build script, I was able to produce a working `filmcraft-<v>-linux-loongarch64.tar.gz` on Ubuntu 24.04 (amd64)  at commit `78fe0102bd0bbe9e55070a4fb4a3924faa545d02`, and the tarball installs and runs  on the ArchLinux (loongarch64) machine.

<details>
<summary>The only source change needed (packaging/linux/package.sh)</summary>

```diff
--- a/packaging/linux/package.sh
+++ b/packaging/linux/package.sh
@@ -36,6 +36,7 @@ done

 ARCH="${CROSS_ARCH:-$(uname -m)}"
 case "$ARCH" in
+  loongarch64) DEB_ARCH=loong64 ;;
   riscv64) DEB_ARCH=riscv64 ;;
   x86_64) DEB_ARCH=amd64 ;;
   aarch64 | arm64) ARCH=aarch64; DEB_ARCH=arm64 ;;
```

</details>

<details>
<summary> And the cross-build script I used (Ubuntu 24.04 amd64 → tar.gz) (supported by GLM5.3)</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Cross-build FilmCraft for loongarch64 on Ubuntu 24.04 (amd64).
# Tested at filmcraft commit 78fe0102bd0bbe9e55070a4fb4a3924faa545d02
# + the one-line DEB_ARCH=loong64 mapping in packaging/linux/package.sh.
set -euo pipefail

TARGET=loongarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
SYSROOT=/usr/loongarch64-linux-gnu          # Ubuntu cross toolchain's own sysroot

echo "==> [1/5] Ubuntu cross toolchain + qemu (needs the 'universe' component)"
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
  gcc-14-loongarch64-linux-gnu \
  libc6-dev-loong64-cross \
  qemu-user pkg-config curl ca-certificates

# Ubuntu's cross gcc ships a versioned binary name only; probe both.
CC_BIN="$(command -v loongarch64-linux-gnu-gcc || command -v loongarch64-linux-gnu-gcc-14 || true)"
[ -n "$CC_BIN" ] || { echo "error: no loongarch64 cross gcc found" >&2; exit 1; }
ls "$SYSROOT/lib/ld-linux-loongarch-lp64d.so.1" >/dev/null…

title: playhead.set is ignored during playback but reports success; 47% dropped frames on one 1080p60 H.264 clip (M3 Max)
author: PhywithAA
body:

The test video was a 74.2 s **H.264 High, 1920×1080, 60 fps** MP4 with no audio (a manim animation). Import, Sequence From Clip, markers, Add Edit and text titles all work, and with explicit times the cuts are exact. Two problems:

### 1. Moving the playhead while playback runs is ignored, but the commands report success

With Program playback running (`ui.inspect` → `playback.playing: true`), I ran ten times:

```json

- **Expected:** the playhead jumps to each time (as in Premiere, where playback continues from there or stops), and the marker and cut land there.

author: padab

# HEVC (H.265) export unavailable on Linux with NVIDIA: "no encoder registered"

## Summary

On Linux with an NVIDIA GPU, H.265 (HEVC) export is not available. `filmcraft-cli export --format hevc` fails with "no encoder registered", and the HEVC option is not usable in the export dialog. H.264 export works.

The README says H.265 export is hardware-only (NVENC on Windows, VideoToolbox on macOS) and does not mention Linux, so I assume this is simply not implemented there yet. I could not find an existing issue for NVENC HEVC on Linux. #30 covers hardware acceleration in general, and PR #1612 adds VA-API encoding, which as far as I understand does not apply to NVIDIA (the NVIDIA VA-API driver only supports decoding). title: AI Video generation in the timeline (V2V): a working prototype and design questions
author: vark-debug
body:
## What this is about

A **discussion proposal, not a merge request**. The prototype below explores a gap that the commercial competition is structurally unlikely to close:

**Premiere Pro already ships text-to-video and image-to-video generation — but has no video-to-video channel, and none is expected: a timeline-native "keep this clip's motion, change what I describe" would eat directly into After Effects' role, so Adobe has little incentive to build it.** FilmCraft has no such boundary to protect. An open-source editor can offer timeline-adjacent v2v as a first-class feature — this is a place where FilmCraft can lead instead of follow.

To be explicit up front: **I am not suggesting this prototype be merged.** It is a fork branch kept intentionally rough — just enough to prove the interaction works end-to-end (it does, against MiniMax H3). It exists so the discussion can start from a working reference instead of a wish list.

**Reference implementation:** [`vark-debug/filmcraft@feature/ai-video-generate`](https://github.com/vark-debug/filmcraft/tree/feature/ai-video-generate) (~1500 lines, quality gates green, stub provider so the pipeline is testable without an API key).

## The gap this explores

- **t2v / i2v (Premiere has these):** generate a clip from a prompt or a still, then edit it like any media. Valuable, but the generation happens *before* editing begins.
- **v2v (nobody has this in the timeline):** "take *this* clip from *my* sequence — its motion, its framing, its timing — and change only what I describe." That is a different workflow, and the closer the entry point sits to the clip itself, the more it changes how the tool gets used: it stops being a generator you visit and becomes something you edit with.

## How the prototype works today

1. **`clip.aiVideo`** (`Clip ▸ AI Video…`, `Cmd+Alt+G`): an inline one-row prompt floats above the selected clip (its bottom-right corner on the clip's top-left). Enter or OK submits; a click outside cancels.

title: probe reports duration in an undocumented unit (not nanoseconds)
author: tcae83-debug
body:
## What happens

`filmcraft-cli probe` returns a `duration` field whose unit is not documented and is **not** nanoseconds. The measurement itself is correct — the value is exactly proportional to the real duration — but nothing can consume it without guessing.

## Reproduction

Tested with FilmCraft 0.7.2 on Windows 10 Famille 22H2 (build 19045.7725, x86_64), on two H.264 files produced by ffmpeg 9.0.1 and measured with `ffprobe` as the reference:

```
# file A: real duration 2.000000 s
filmcraft-cli probe essai-video.mp4    ->  "duration": 508032000000
# file B: real duration 3.000000 s
filmcraft-cli probe essai-video2.mp4   ->  "duration": 762048000000
```

`508032000000 / 2 = 762048000000 / 3 = 254016000000` — exactly proportional per second, on both files, so the underlying measurement is right and only the unit is unexplained. If the field were meant to be nanoseconds, a 2 s clip would read `2000000000`, i.e. a factor of 2.54e11 off.

## Expected

Either seconds (or nanoseconds) under an explicit name — `duration_ns`, or a documented unit in the field's schema — or the unit stated in `filmcraft-cli probe --help`. As it stands, any automation reading `probe` has to hard-code a magic constant, which will silently break if the unit is ever changed.

## Secondary point, same version

In a script executed by `filmcraft-cli run <script.jsonl>`, `file.newSequenceFromClip` fails right after an import unless the item is passed explicitly:

title: Linux: File > Open's "FilmCraft Project" filter hides .filmcraft files (empty bundled MIME package)
author: niiithish
body:
**Version:** FilmCraft 0.7.2, installed from the Linux x86_64 tarball into `/opt/filmcraft`
**Desktop:** Hyprland, with the GTK file chooser through xdg-desktop-portal

### What happens
In the File > Open dialog, the "FilmCraft Project" filter hides every `.filmcraft` file. A folder with a saved project, for example `edit/mysa-one-main-pipe.filmcraft`, shows only its subfolders. The file appears in the file manager, and FilmCraft opens it fine if you type the path with Ctrl+L.

### Why
- The bundled MIME package `/opt/filmcraft/share/mime/packages/ai.storyteller.filmcraft.xml` is empty: it contains `<mime-info>` with no `<mime-type>`, so `*.filmcraft` is never registered.
- As a result `xdg-mime query filetype project.filmcraft` returns `application/json` (content sniffing).
- So a portal filter keyed on a FilmCraft MIME type matches nothing.

### Expected
Saved projects show up under the "FilmCraft Project" filter.

### Suggested fix
- Define the project type in the MIME package, for example `application/x-filmcraft-project` with `<glob pattern="*.filmcraft"/>`, and list it in the `.desktop` file's `MimeType=`.
- Have the tarball install step run `update-mime-database` (or document it).
- Make the dialog filter by glob (`*.filmcraft`) as well as by MIME type, so it still works when the type isn't registered.
- Add an "All files" filter to the dialog.
