author: amark2005
body:

title: Playback: Ultra Key + Lumetri with an input LUT runs the whole 4K layer on the CPU (~2 fps); key has no GPU op, LUT disqualifies Lumetri
author: bsoulai
body:
## Summary

A 9:16 timeline with one 4K green-screen take (Ultra Key + Lumetri with an input LUT) over a 1080p background plays at about **2 fps** on an M1 Max, with GPU rendering on or off. The user's workaround is to switch the video tracks off to keep working. Decode is not the cost (the 4K H.264 take decodes at 139 fps); the layer's effect chain is, because of three things in `crates/render`:

1. **Ultra Key has no GPU op.** `crates/gpu/src/fx.rs` has no key op; `crates/render/src/vfx/color.rs:159` (`ultra_key`) is CPU only.
2. **A chain goes to the GPU only when every effect in it has a GPU op** (`crates/render/src/plan.rs:444`, `Option<Vec<FxOp>>` collect). One CPU-only effect sends the whole layer, Lumetri included, back to the CPU.
3. **Lumetri is CPU-only as soon as it carries an input LUT, a look LUT, HSL, curves, wheels or sharpen** (`crates/render/src/gpufx.rs:532`, `gpu_capable`). A grade brought in as an input LUT, which is the normal way to carry a colourist's look across, forces the slow path on its own.

Lines are on `main` at cee1feb1. #30 tracks hardware acceleration broadly; this is the specific case where the GPU compositor is already there and the key + grade combination defeats it.

## Measurements

2 s (60 frames) export of the same range, `--no-audio`, 1080x1920 30 fps sequence, 4K (2160x3840) H.264 High take keyed over a 1080x1920 H.264 wall, Apple M1 Max, quiet machine. CPU column: release 0.7.2 CLI (`--gpu-rendering off`). GPU column: a CLI built with the wgpu backends from #1559 (`--gpu-rendering auto`, the export result reports all 60 frames on `Apple M1 Max (Metal)`, `cpuFrames: 0`).

| Effects on the 4K layer | CPU fps | GPU fps |
|---|---|---|
| Ultra Key + Lumetri (input LUT, HSL on) | 2.0 | 2.1 |
| Lumetri only (input LUT, HSL on) | 1.6 | 2.6 |
| Ultra Key only | 3.1 | 4.2 |
| Lumetri with the input LUT removed and HSL off, no key | – | **25.0** |
| Same GPU-eligible Lumetri + Ultra Key | – | 3.4 |

title: AV1 HW decoder detected but Media Foundation rejects decode; falls back to slow software decode (2K/4K uneditable)
author: pixelsdontmove
body:
Environment
- FilmCraft 0.7.2 on Windows x86_64

Problem
The AV1 hardware decoder (Media Foundation AV1 Video Extension) is discovered, but for some AV1 files the Media Foundation MFT immediately fails and FilmCraft falls back to the software decoder. On 2K/4K AV1 clips the software fallback is too slow for interactive scrubbing/editing, making those clips effectively uneditable.

Observed log lines
2026-10-13T14:54:16.536Z INFO  [main] filmcraft: FilmCraft 0.7.2 (windows x86_64)
2026-10-13T14:54:28.266Z INFO  [filmcraft-frames-4] filmcraft_platform::media_foundation: hardware decoding: AV1VideoExtension on AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700
2026-10-13T14:54:28.266Z WARN  [decode-2] filmcraft_platform::hybrid: Media Foundation AV1 failed (decode error: in-band parameter sets differ from the sample entry); continuing with the software decoder

Observed behavior
- The system sees an AV1 hardware decoder but Media Foundation rejects decoding for some files due to the reported error. FilmCraft then uses its software decoder, which is too slow for 2K/4K interactive editing. Playback is smooth for a few frames, then freezes.

Steps to reproduce (what I did)
1. Launch the FilmCraft 0.7.2 on Windows.
2. Import an AV1 clip at 2K or 4K resolution that contains parameter sets differing from the sample entry. (eg screenrecord from Adrenaline Software)
3. Observe FilmCraft logs show the AV1VideoExtension detection followed immediately by the MF failure and a switch to software decoding.

Notes
- I do not have a solution, I'm stupid; reporting the failure and logs for triage and prioritization.

Currently, there is no convenient way to copy and paste effects or their settings, which makes it tedious to reproduce the same effect configuration across multiple clips. Users have to manually recreate or adjust each effect, even when they want to reuse an existing configuration.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

I would like to see a copy-and-paste feature for effects and effect settings, allowing users to easily reuse existing configurations throughout their editing workflow.

Ideally, this feature would support the following operations:

- Copy and paste individual effect settings: Copy the settings of a specific effect and paste them onto the same type of effect elsewhere, replacing its current settings.
- Replace existing effect settings: When pasting settings onto an existing effect, replace its current configuration with the copied one.
- Copy and paste entire effects: Copy an entire effect, including all its settings, and paste it onto another clip, without having to recreate them manually.

These operations could be accessible through a context menu (right-click), keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V or Cmd+C / Cmd+V on macOS), or another interface consistent with the application's existing workflow.

title: FCP7 XML import: clips with <start>/<end> -1 next to a transition are skipped (and the transitions with them)
author: bsoulai
body:
**Version:** FilmCraft 0.7.2 (`filmcraft-cli 0.7.2`, macOS 26.2, M1 Max)

**What happens**
Importing an FCP 7 XML (`xmeml` v5) where clips are joined by transitions skips every clip that touches a transition, then skips the transitions too:

```
clip "LCB 002 - … take 1 (eyes LT).mov" has neither start nor end; skipped (×4)
transition "Cross Dissolve" at frame 285 has no adjacent clip; skipped
transition "Cross Dissolve" at frame 601 has no adjacent clip; skipped
transition "Cross Dissolve" at frame 827 has no adjacent clip; skipped
```

A 6-piece cut came in with 2 pieces and holes where the other 4 were.

**Why**
In FCP 7 XML a clipitem whose edge sits under a transition carries `<start>-1</start>` and/or `<end>-1</end>`. That is how the format says "this edge is defined by the neighbouring `transitionitem`", not that the times are missing. DaVinci Resolve and Premiere both write it this way. Excerpt from a Resolve 21.1.1 export (one V2 track, 30 fps):

```xml
<clipitem><start>54</start><end>-1</end><in>589</in><out>787</out>…</clipitem>
<transitionitem><start>246</start><end>258</end><alignment>center</alignment>…</transitionitem>
<clipitem><start>-1</start><end>-1</end><in>789</in><out>828</out>…</clipitem>
<transitionitem><start>285</start><end>297</end>…</transitionitem>
<clipitem><start>-1</start><end>-1</end><in>835</in><out>1151</out>…</clipitem>
…
<clipitem><start>-1</start><end>1171</end><in>1870</in><out>2132</out>…</clipitem>
```

**Expected**
Resolve the `-1` edges from the adjacent transition. For a centre-aligned transition the cut is at `(transition.start + transition.end) / 2`. We checked the resulting timeline against the source Resolve timeline's own API readback. For a clip that follows a transition, Resolve writes `in`/`out` shifted back by `cut - transition.start`. Its true source in at the cut is `in + (cut - transition.start)`, and `out - in` is the clip's real length. With that rule the six pieces land at 54/252/291/607/833/909 with source …

title: Import: phone clips with millisecond-rounded frame times read as 30.303 / 58.824 fps, so New Sequence From Clip drops frames
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
**Version:** FilmCraft 0.7.2, windows-x64 portable, Windows 11 Pro 25H2 (build 26200). The code path is unchanged on `main` (cee1feb).

### What happens

Phones and messaging apps often store frame times rounded to whole milliseconds inside a 90 kHz MP4 track. A 30 fps clip then has frame durations of 33 and 34 ms (2970 and 3060 units), a 60 fps clip 16 and 17 ms (1440 and 1530 units). FilmCraft takes the clip's frame rate from the median sample duration and keeps it when it is not within 0.005 fps of a standard rate:

| Fixture | ffprobe `r_frame_rate` / mean rate | FilmCraft `frame_rate` |
|---|---|---|
| `fps30_ms_timestamps.mp4` (120 frames) | 30/1 / 29.998 | 30303/1000 (30.303) |
| `fps60_ms_timestamps.mp4` (240 frames) | 60/1 / 60.005 | 7353/125 (58.824) |

The rate then carries through the edit:

- Sequence ▸ New Sequence From Clip creates a 30.303 fps / 58.824 fps sequence.
- An export of that sequence is written at that rate (`r_frame_rate=7353/125`).
- For the 60 fps clip the sequence has 235 frames instead of 240, so 5 source frames are never shown or exported.

In a test run over 92 real video files (mostly phone clips), 34 phone clips got a rate that is not a standard one:

| FilmCraft rate | Clips | ffprobe `r_frame_rate` |
|---|---|---|
| 30.02 (1501/50) | 15 | 30/1 |
| 29.95 | 11 | mostly 18000/601 (29.95), some 30000/1001 or 30/1 |
| 30.01 (3001/100) | 4 | 30000/1001 or 30/1 |
| 30.303 (30303/1000) | 2 | 30/1 |

author: KNUFFIXX
body:
**Version:** FilmCraft 0.7.2, windows-x64 portable, Windows 11 Pro 25H2 (build 26200). No related change on `main` since the release (cee1feb).

### What happens

A 5.1 AC-3 or E-AC-3 track in an `.mp4` is listed with 2 channels (Media File Properties / `mediaBrowser.probe`), and only the front left and right channels reach the mix. In a stereo sequence the centre (dialogue), LFE and both surround channels are silent. | File | FilmCraft channels | Export L | Export R |
|---|---|---|---|
| `surround51_ac3.mp4` | 2 | FL | FR |
| `surround51_eac3.mp4` | 2 | FL | FR |

title: Timeline: Unable to select individual clip portions after cut, or single clips in vertically stacked tracks (keeps selecting all)
author: backpropagation6
body:
### Problem Description

In the Timeline, clip selection does not properly isolate individual clip segments or individual tracks in two common scenarios:

1. **After cutting / splitting a clip**: When a clip is cut into multiple segments, clicking to select a single split portion often fails to isolate that portion; instead, it continues to select the entire clip / all portions as if they are still fully linked or grouped together.
2. **Vertically stacked clips across tracks**: When multiple clips are placed on top of each other across different tracks (e.g., V1 and V2 at the same timeframe), clicking on a specific clip to select only that clip frequently selects the entire stack / all overlapping clips instead of targeting just the single clicked clip.

### Steps to Reproduce

**Scenario A (Split clip selection):**
1. Place a clip on the timeline.
2. Cut the clip into multiple portions using the cut/razor tool or split shortcut.
3. Switch back to the selection tool and click on a single cut portion.
4. **Result:** It is almost impossible to select only that specific segment; FilmCraft keeps selecting all portions or the whole clip.

**Scenario B (Stacked / Overlapping clips):**
1. Place two or more clips stacked on top of each other on separate tracks (e.g., track V1 and V2 at the same timeframe).
2. Click directly on one of the clips to select only that layer.
3. **Result:** Instead of selecting only the clicked clip, it selects all stacked clips / everything across tracks.

### Expected Behavior

- Clicking on a cut clip segment should reliably select only that individual segment.
- Clicking on a clip in a multi-track stacked setup should select only the clip on that specific track, without inadvertently selecting clips placed above or below it.

A talking-head show shot on green: one long take per episode, cut into many pieces with jump cuts and punch-ins (different Scale/Position per piece). The key and grade are the same for every piece. title: mpegts/avi: redundant PES header length check and doubled frame_info call
author: vangel76
body:
Two small cleanups left over from the mpegts audit (no behaviour change intended).

1. `PesAsm::packet` (crates/mpegts/src/ts.rs) checks `self.hdr.len() >= h.header_len` after `pes::parse`. `pes::parse` only returns `Some` when `header_len <= b.len()` on every path (plain streams: len >= 6; ISO syntax: explicit `b.len() < header_len` check; MPEG-1: every advance is preceded by a successful `get`), so the check is dead. The following `h.header_len - before` is an unchecked subtraction; it should be `saturating_sub`.

2. crates/codecs/src/avi.rs (MPEG audio chunk scan) calls `filmcraft_mpegts::frame_info(ts, here)` twice for the same frame: once to fill `info` for the first frame and again for the per-frame sample count. One call per frame is enough.

Not touched here: shared EsState / finish loop, in-place Psi drain, ts::read buffer reuse (overlap open #1438).

body:
An audit of `crates/cfb` (after #585) found one real bug and a few small hardening, doc and cleanup items.

**Bug: `validate_name` accepts U+0000.** `Writer::stream(ROOT, "a\0b", ..)` succeeds, but the directory entry is NUL-terminated, so `CompoundFile::open` reads the name back as `"a"` and `find("a\0b")` returns `NotFound`. "a\0b" and "a\0c" are also distinct to the writer but identical on read. Fix: reject U+0000 (MS-CFB 2.6.1 names are NUL-terminated UTF-16).

**Hardening (32-bit / wasm32).** `read_mini_chain` computes `s as usize * 64` and `at + 64` unchecked, which overflows on a 32-bit `usize` (panic in debug, wrong data in release). `sector()` does `n as usize + 1` before its `MAXREGSECT` check. Fix: `usize::try_from` plus `checked_mul` / `checked_add`, range check first. Not reachable on 64-bit.

**Docs.** `Entry::children` says "sorted by compare_names", which only holds for well-formed files (the reader does not validate the sibling tree order).

**Cleanup / optimisation.**
- Dead code: the `FREESECT` check in `read_chain` (caught earlier by `> MAXREGSECT`) and the `steps` counter in `build_tree` (the owner set already prevents revisits).
- `compare_names` allocates two `Vec<u16>` per comparison, and `child()` calls it once per sibling. Compare via iterators instead, same ordering.
- `read_chain` starts from `Vec::new()`; pre-size it with a capacity bounded by the file length.

Deliberately not changed: tolerant handling of sector shift / version / mini cutoff, truncated last sector and oversized root mini-stream size.

title: TTML import drops body and timed-span text styles
author: nuclearspike
body:
TTML/DFXP import silently drops supported styles inherited from the body or defined on a timed span emitted as a cue. Reproduced on main `6c3948a36c80e4996d924766ba7157eec4fca85e` (the parser is unchanged through current main `105c09bd`): copies of the two shipped regression assertions fail 0/2 before the repair, while the patched cases pass. Parse either synthetic document with `filmcraft_captions::parse(bytes, Format::Ttml)` or `Format::Dfxp`: ```xml

Hello

 ``` ```xml

Hello

``` Expected: one cue at 1–2 seconds with stored text `Hello`. Actual: plain `Hello` at the correct times, without warning. Bold, underline and referenced styles are also affected. The engine caption importer calls this parser. The [TTML1 Second Edition body definition](https://www.w3.org/TR/2013/REC-ttml1-20130924/#document-structure-vocabulary-body) and [content style inheritance](https://www.w3.org/TR/2013/REC-ttml1-20130924/#semantics-style-inheritance-content) describe these supported forms. Body traversal starts with default formatting, and timed-span collection omits its cue root's resolved formatting. The linked TTML-only repair preserves the inherited and cue-root styles as balanced inline tags, including descendant resets. Its tests cover both reproductions, recognized styling namespaces and whitespace handling.

title: Windows GPU export: intermittent dark source frames with hardware decoding
author: Gustitolito
body:
Intermittent dark source frames during Windows hardware-decoded GPU exports

## Observed behavior

During repeated full-sequence exports on Windows, a few isolated source-video
frames were almost black, while burned captions and a composited logo remained
normal. The exports completed successfully and an external complete decode
reported no bitstream errors. This is a visual failure despite successful export.

The issue appeared in the existing float GPU export path, not just in the proposed
packed RGBA8 readback path. Repeated reference exports also differed. I have not
established whether the defect is in Media Foundation, frame caching/lifetime,
render upload, or their interaction; the root cause is not proven.

## Environment and evidence

- FilmCraft 0.7.2, upstream commit `cee1feb185e675a108f78067f71ad86a640ace3d`.
- Standalone CLI with native wgpu backends explicitly enabled; the unmodified
  standalone GPU dependency otherwise requests only WGSL and can lack a backend.
- Windows, Ryzen 5 4500, 16 GB RAM, RTX 3080, NVIDIA driver 616.92.
- Release build with thin LTO and one codegen unit; NVENC H.264 Main, 1080p,
  30000/1001, VBR 10/12 Mbps, burned captions. Source media is private.
- 468.734-second sequence, 14,048 output frames. All frames used GPU rendering,
  with no compositor fallback. Decode counters reported Media Foundation active.
- Two reference exports differed in 4,914 decoded video frames (most differences

title: [Bug] Interlaced H.264 MP4 files from Blackmagic HyperDeck are unreadable
author: Akifere
body:
FilmCraft version: 0.7.2
Operating system: macOS
Hardware: MacBook Pro M2

Description:
MP4 files recorded on a Blackmagic HyperDeck are not recognized correctly by FilmCraft. The files appear without thumbnails, and selecting them displays the error "Media unreadable, reconnect it."

The same files play correctly in QuickTime Player and can be imported and edited in Adobe Premiere Pro.

I tested a short sample clip (1920x1080, 25 fps, H.264, 8-bit 4:2:0, interlaced, Top Field First, AAC audio).

Steps to reproduce:
1. Import the original HyperDeck MP4 into FilmCraft.
2. Observe that no thumbnail is generated.
3. Select the clip and observe the "Media unreadable, reconnect it" error.

Additional testing:
- Remuxing the original file with FFmpeg without re-encoding did not fix the issue.
- Re-encoding the video as progressive H.264 fixed the issue.
- Progressive H.264 worked with both Main and High profiles.
- Re-encoding as interlaced H.264 still failed with both Main and High profiles.

This suggests that the issue may be related to decoding interlaced H.264 video rather than the H.264 profile itself.

Expected behavior:
FilmCraft should import and decode this valid H.264 MP4 file, or provide a more informative error if the format is unsupported.

Actual behavior:
The file is marked as unreadable, despite working correctly in other media applications.

title: Captions export (SCC/MCC): a caption that follows the previous one closely pops on about a second late
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
**Version:** FilmCraft 0.7.2, windows-x64 portable, Windows 11 Pro 25H2 (build 26200).

### What happens

When a caption starts shortly after the previous one ends, the SCC (and MCC) export loads the new caption only after the previous caption's end time. Pop-on text needs about one frame per two characters to transmit, so a longer caption pops on late by its whole transmission time.

Two captions (`scc_tight.srt`):

| # | SRT | in the exported SCC | read back by FilmCraft |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 00:00:01,000 → 00:00:02,000 | load from 00:00:00;15, EOC at 1.00 s | 00:00:01:00 |
| 2 | 00:00:02,240 → 00:00:05,000 | line starts at 00:00:02;00 with EDM, EOC is word 39 → 3.27 s | **00:00:03:07** |

Caption 2 shows from 3.27 s instead of 2.24 s, about a second late. Its data could be sent right after caption 1's EOC (1.0 s): the next caption builds in non-displayed memory while the current one is on screen, and the EDM for caption 1 can go into that stream at 2.0 s. Then caption 2 would pop on at about 2.27 s.

When the load fits between the previous EOC and the next start, the writer already overlaps it: in `scc_timing.srt` (captions at 1.0–3.0 s and 3.2–6.0 s) caption 2 is loaded during caption 1 and pops on at exactly 3.2 s. The delay only appears when the load does not fit.

title: EDL round trip: a FilmCraft EDL from a 25 fps sequence is re-imported at 24 fps, and file.import cannot set the rate
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
**Version:** FilmCraft 0.7.2, windows-x64 portable, Windows 11 Pro 25H2 (build 26200).

### What happens

An EDL that FilmCraft writes for a 25 fps sequence comes back at 24 fps when it is imported again. The importer reports `EDL has no frame rate; assumed 24 fps (set ImportOptions::edl_frame_rate to override)`, but `file.import` (and so the CLI and MCP) has no parameter to pass that rate.

Test sequence: 640×360, 25 fps, three clips (100 frames each) with a 12-frame cross dissolve.

| | original | FCP7 XML / FCPXML / OTIO / AAF re-import | EDL re-import |
|---|---|---|---|
| frame rate | 25 | 25 | **24** |
| size | 640×360 | 640×360 | 1920×1080 (an EDL has no size, expected) |
| length | 300 frames | 300 frames, identical picture by picture | **288 frames** (12 s at 24 fps) |
| dissolve | 3.76–4.24 s | same | 3.79–4.29 s (`03:19` read as 3 s + 19/24) |

The 25 fps clips then play in a 24 fps sequence, so a frame in every 25 is never shown or exported.

The other four formats re-import frame-exact. The EDL itself is correct CMX 3600 (`FCM: NON-DROP FRAME`, timecodes at 25 fps). Its highest frame field is 19, so `guess_rate` cannot tell 24 from 25, and every timecode is read at 24 fps.

### Expected

The EDL comes back at 25 fps. Possible ways, any of them would do:

- `file.import` takes an optional EDL frame rate (and the import dialog offers it).
- Without a rate, use the frame rate of the media the EDL links (`* SOURCE FILE:` comments; both clips here are 25 fps) or of the active sequence before falling back to 24.
- FilmCraft's own EDL export writes the rate in a comment that the importer reads back.

title: Proposal for reimplementing transitions

body:
Hi, I think this is better than posting on discord because at least this platform is on the open web.

So fireship made a video on this app https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=wajoP_5Cpw8&pp=0gcJCY8Co7VqN5tD and his complaint is transition parity which filmcraft did not meet. I am not able to confirm transition parity at this time, but I would like to propose a method to reimplement transitions 

The idea is a grid of squares with alternating colors, like a test pattern but to analyze geometry in 2 dimensions. Like a convergence grid pattern like that used to adjust CRTs, but to adjust for color distortion, the square areas created by the grid can be filled with non repeating colors in the same way used in cartography to prevent colors from repeating next to each other. title: export: PNG Sequence writes 4-channel RGBA files even with Include Alpha Channel off
author: Tokarzewski
body:
**Version:** filmcraft-cli 0.7.2 (Windows release build). Source read at main `cee1feb1` (2026-10-13): the PNG branch is unchanged there.

With `alpha` off, PNG Sequence flattens the picture over black (the pixel values are right) but still writes a colour-type 6 (RGBA) PNG whose alpha channel is 255 everywhere. TIFF and Targa sequences honour the same setting and write 3-channel files, so only PNG ignores it. Downstream tools then see an alpha channel that is not there (FilmCraft's own `probe` reports `has_alpha: true`, `RGBA 8-bit` for the alpha-off files), and every file carries a fourth channel of constant data. Nothing is wrong with the colours, so this is a small correctness and size issue, not a wrong picture.

**Steps**

```sh
# src_000.png ... src_004.png: five 64x36 RGBA PNGs, every pixel (200,100,50,alpha 128)
for a in false true; do
filmcraft-cli --data-dir data run - <<JSONL
{"id":"file.newProject","params":{"name":"t"}}
{"id":"file.import","params":{"paths":["src_000.png"],"imageSequence":true}}
{"id":"file.newSequence","params":{"name":"S","width":64,"height":36,"fps":30}}
{"id":"timeline.place","params":{"items":[1],"track":"V1","seconds":0}}
{"id":"file.exportMedia","params":{"path":"alpha_$a.png","wait":true,"format":"png","settings":{"alpha":$a}}}
JSONL
done
python -c "
for a in ('false','true'):
    b = open('alpha_%s000.png' % a, 'rb').read()
    print(a, 'colour type', b[25], 'bit depth', b[24])"
```

Both runs exit 0. Then `filmcraft-cli probe alpha_false000.png`.

**Observed**

```
false colour type 6 bit depth 8
true colour type 6 bit depth 8
```

`probe alpha_false000.png` reports `"has_alpha": true` and `"pixel_format": "RGBA 8-bit"`.

Decoded first pixel: `alpha: false` gives (147, 72, 34, 255), i.e. flattened over black as documented; `alpha: true` gives (200, 100, 50, 128).

For comparison, with a 64x36 source the same `alpha` switch gives 7122 bytes (off) and 9430 bytes (on) for TIFF, and 6956 and 9260 bytes for Targa: the third and fo…

title: [LEGAL] Potential trademark conflict: 'Lumetri' name is a registered trademark of Adobe
author: Gatifulaa
body:
The project currently uses the term **"Lumetri"** within the codebase/UI. Please note that *"Lumetri"* is a registered trademark owned by **Adobe Systems Incorporated** (widely used across multiple Adobe applications for color grading).

> **Note:** This also aligns with the project guidelines in `AGENTS.md`, which explicitly state that no Adobe assets or proprietary branding of any kind should be used.

### Risk

Using a proprietary trademark owned by another company in an open-source project can lead to legal action (such as a Cease & Desist or a DMCA/trademark takedown request) which could negatively impact the repository or project distribution.

### Suggested Solution

To avoid breaking project file compatibility while eliminating trademark risks, consider renaming the public UI/branding while keeping internal aliases:

1. **Rename visible terms in UI/Docs:** Change public labels to generic terms or a custom open name. My top recommendation is **Iris** or **Iris Correction** (or generic terms like *Color Wheels* / *Color Grading* / *Primary & Secondary Color Correction*).

2. **Keep internal aliases/real-time remapping:** Keep "Lumetri" strictly as a hidden fallback or runtime alias to parse imported Adobe files automatically without exposing the trademark in the user interface.

A graphic layer with **Fill off** and **Stroke on** renders as a solid shape in the stroke colour when the stroke type is **Outer** (the default). Center and Inner draw the expected outline. Text and shape layers behave the same way.

The project stores the right values (`inspect sequence` shows `fill: Bool(false)`, `stroke: Bool(true)`), so this looks like a render problem, not a parameter problem. It happens whether the properties are set with `graphics.set` or with `effects.setParam` on the layer's `effectIndex`.

title: graphics.set with `time` overwrites the static value instead of setting a keyframe, with no error
author: dzenn000
body:
**Version:** filmcraft-cli 0.7.2, macOS 27 (Apple silicon), headless engine.

### What happens

`graphics.set` advertises an optional `time` parameter (`describe graphics.set`: `"time":ticks?`), but passing it does not create a keyframe. Each call just overwrites the static value: the last call wins and the layer does not animate. The command returns `null` and no error or warning, so a script gets no sign that its animation was dropped.

### Steps to reproduce

```jsonl
{"id":"file.newProject","params":{"name":"R"}}
{"id":"file.newSequence","params":{"name":"R","width":1920,"height":1080,"fps":30,"video":4,"audio":1}}
{"id":"graphics.newEllipse","params":{"position":[300,540],"size":[200,200],"track":1,"time":0,"seconds":2}}
{"id":"graphics.set","params":{"clip":8,"layer":0,"time":0,"props":{"position":[300,540]}}}
{"id":"graphics.set","params":{"clip":8,"layer":0,"time":381024000000,"props":{"position":[1600,540]}}}
```

Then render frames at 0.2 s and 1.8 s, and look at `inspect sequence`.

### Result

- Both frames show the ellipse at x = 1600.
- `inspect sequence` shows the layer's `position` as `{"keyframes": 0, "value": Vec2 { x: 1600, y: 540 }}`.

### Expected

One of these:
- With `time`, `graphics.set` sets keyframes on the listed properties, the same way `effects.setParam … "keyframe": true` does; or
- if `time` means something else (for example, which keyframe to edit), document that, and return an error when no keyframe exists at that time instead of silently changing the static value.

### Workaround

Call `effects.setParam` with `"effect": <effectIndex from graphics.list>`, `"time": …` and `"keyframe": true`. That works as expected.

title: effects.apply inserts the new effect at index 0, shifting Motion/Opacity and every graphics.list effectIndex
author: dzenn000
body:
**Version:** filmcraft-cli 0.7.2, macOS 27 (Apple silicon), headless engine.

### What happens

`effects.apply` adds the new effect at **index 0** of the clip's effect list, in front of the intrinsic Motion / Opacity / Time Remapping and the graphic-layer effects. Every existing effect index moves up by one, including the `effectIndex` values that `graphics.list` reports for graphic layers.

Rendering looks correct (a Gaussian Blur applied this way still blurs the drawn shape). The problem is for anything that addresses effects by number: a script that read `effectIndex` from `graphics.list`, applied an effect, and then keyframes a layer with the old index fails with `no param \`position\``, or writes to the wrong effect when the parameter name happens to exist there.

### Steps to reproduce

```jsonl
{"id":"file.newProject","params":{"name":"R"}}
{"id":"file.newSequence","params":{"name":"R","width":1920,"height":1080,"fps":30,"video":4,"audio":1}}
{"id":"graphics.newEllipse","params":{"position":[960,540],"size":[400,400],"track":1,"time":0,"seconds":2}}
```

```
filmcraft-cli --project r.fcproj exec graphics.list clip=8      # layer 0: "effectIndex": 3

Applied effects go **after** the intrinsic and graphic-layer effects, as in Premiere's Effect Controls: `motion, opacity, time_remap, graphic_shape, gaussian_blur`. Indices already handed out stay valid, and the list order matches the processing order.

title: A timeline move can place the same clip identity on more than one track
author: nuclearspike
body:
On current main, a `timeline.move` request that lists one clip twice can leave that same ClipId on both destination tracks. Later selection and identity-based edits cannot distinguish those placements.

To reproduce through MCP's `command_run`:
1. Create a project and a 25 fps sequence with two video tracks and two audio tracks.
2. Add a four-second offline video with audio and place it on V1/A1 at time 0.
3. Use that video's returned clip ID in both rows below (8 is the ID in my fresh-project fixture):
```json
{
  "id": "timeline.move",
  "params": {
    "moves": [
      {"clip": 8, "track": "V1", "time": 2032128000000},
      {"clip": 8, "track": "V2", "time": 2032128000000}
    ],
    "linked": false
  }
}
```
4. Inspect the sequence: the same clip ID appears on both tracks. This also reproduces with `insert: true`.

Expected: reject a repeated identity in an explicit move plan, leaving the idle project's contents and Undo/Redo history intact so the caller can correct the request. Selection-derived moves should handle repeated selection entries once.

Copies need different handling: with `copy: true`, repeating a source is valid. In the same fixture, requesting one copy on `new` and one on V2 currently routes both to the new track; overwrite reports two copy IDs but only one remains. Each copy should receive a fresh ID and retain its own requested destination.

Confirmed against main `cee1feb185e675a108f78067f71ad86a640ace3d` with synthetic offline media.

title: 'Interpret Footage' color space override cannot be applied to multiple selected clips at once
author: guiireader-cell
body:
When selecting multiple clips in the Project panel and attempting to batch-apply Interpret Footage (e.g., overriding the color space from Rec.2100 HLG / BT.2020 to Rec. 709 for HDR footage), the change only applies to a single clip (or fails to apply across the entire selection). To get the correct color interpretation, the user is forced to manually open Interpret Footage and change the settings for every single take individually.

Steps to Reproduce

Import multiple HDR/HLG video files (e.g., 10-bit HLG MP4 files from a smartphone or cinema camera) into the Project panel.

Select all imported clips (using Ctrl + A or Shift + Click).

Right-click the selection and go to Modify > Interpret Footage....

Change Color Space Override to Rec. 709 (or another desired profile) and click OK.

Inspect the selected clips in the Project panel or timeline.

Expected Behavior

The Interpret Footage color space override should be updated for all selected clips simultaneously.

Actual Behavior

The color space override is only applied to one clip (the active/focused clip in the selection) or ignored for the rest of the batch, requiring the action to be repeated manually take-by-take.

Impact

This creates a significant workflow bottleneck when working with multi-take projects recorded in HDR/HLG (such as modern mobile or log recordings), as users must manually edit footage settings dozens or hundreds of times.

PS: Perhaps this problem can also occur with other options.

Environment
App Version: Version 0.8.0 (portable)
OS: Windows 11

title: Truncated TGA images can consume their footer or metadata as missing pixels
author: nuclearspike
body:
A TGA declaring two pixels but storing only one opens successfully by reading its footer as the second pixel. I reproduced this on main `f03e21556d8e3a7155b91892d958debd5255d7af`: the built CLI reports a valid 2×1 still, and an imported timeline frame renders red followed by a fabricated black pixel.

Create the small synthetic input:

```python
from pathlib import Path
header = bytearray(18)
header[2] = 2
header[12:16] = bytes([2, 0, 1, 0])
header[16:18] = bytes([24, 32])
Path("truncated.tga").write_bytes(
    header + bytes([0, 0, 255]) + bytes(8) + b"TRUEVISION-XFILE.\0"
)
```

Then run `filmcraft-cli probe truncated.tga`, or import it with `file.import`.

Expected: a decode error for the missing pixel, so the source can be repaired and retried. Actual: successful import; the footer supplies image data.

The decoder can also consume optional metadata as missing RLE or pixel data when a referenced region starts inside the image body. The linked repair bounds image reads at a recognized TGA 2.0 footer and at applicable referenced metadata starts. Complete images remain readable when optional pointers are out of range or before the calculated pixel-data start; malformed pointers before that start can still supply missing palette bytes. A footerless image whose final 26 bytes mimic a full TGA 2.0 trailer is byte-ambiguous and may be rejected, even when its apparent trailer starts in a declared image ID rather than pixel bytes. Tests cover the reported truncation, metadata boundaries, and complete-image controls.

Tested headlessly on macOS 27.0 arm64. The repaired CLI rejects the malformed input without changing the saved project bytes, then imports a repaired file at the same path; after save/reopen, the existing bin and imported shot are present. A public-media-opener regression checks the decoded pixels.

title: Counting Leader beep duration ignores its source frame rate
author: nuclearspike
body:
Universal Counting Leader gates each beep for approximately 1/24 second regardless of the frame rate stored on the source. At 60 fps and 48 kHz, the first beep lasts 2,000 sample positions instead of one frame's 800.

To reproduce:

1. Create a 60 fps sequence with 48 kHz audio.
2. Create a three-second Universal Counting Leader and place its audio at the start of A1.
3. Export the sequence as a stereo WAV. Inspect the first beep: it continues past sample 799, through sample 1999. Expected: silence from sample 800 until the next second mark.

The built headless CLI reproduces the same path:

```sh
filmcraft-cli --data-dir leader-check-state run - <<'JSONL'
{"id":"file.newProject","params":{"name":"Leader timing"}}
{"id":"file.newSequence","params":{"name":"Leader60","width":64,"height":36,"fps":60,"sampleRate":48000,"video":1,"audio":1}}
{"id":"file.newCountingLeader","params":{"seconds":3,"width":64,"height":36}}
{"id":"timeline.place","params":{"item":4,"track":"A1","seconds":0}}
{"id":"file.exportMedia","params":{"format":"wav","path":"leader.wav","wait":true}}
JSONL
python3 - <<'PY'
import array, wave
with wave.open("leader.wav", "rb") as f:
    assert (f.getframerate(), f.getnchannels(), f.getsampwidth()) == (48000, 2, 2)
    samples = array.array("h", f.readframes(48000))[::2]
    print("Last nonzero position:", max(i for i, value in enumerate(samples) if value))
PY
```

Current output: `1999`; expected: `799`. WAV samples are little-endian; the diagnostic above was run on arm64 macOS.

`new_generator` already gives the source the active sequence's frame rate, but `generators.rs::audio_sample` ignores it and uses `t.fract() < 1.0 / 24.0`. Floating-point rounding can also leak a boundary sample at 24 fps, and the default 24000/1001 rate is cut short.

Reproduced on main `f03e21556d8e3a7155b91892d958debd5255d7af` (0.8.0), macOS 27.0 arm64, official Rust 1.97.1, using the built CLI and public generator API. Physical audio playback and native-window interaction we…

title: Panels are locked within MDI boundaries and cannot span multiple monitors
author: DeeCee63
body:
Undocked/floating panels cannot be dragged outside the boundaries of the main application window. Even when a panel is pulled out of a dock group, it hits a hard, invisible wall at the edge of the master program window. System-level window manipulation (such as the Win + Shift + Arrow shortcut) fails to force the panel onto a secondary display because the panel is treated as an internal child element rather than a native operating system window.
Steps to reproduce
1. Launch FilmCraft on a system with a multi-monitor setup (Windows 10).
2. Click and drag a panel tab (e.g., Timeline or Program Monitor) to undock it into a floating state.
3. Attempt to drag that floating panel past the outer border of the main FilmCraft window onto a second monitor.
4. Result: The panel stops abruptly at the application window's edge and cannot cross screen boundaries.

Expected behavior
Undocked panels should spawn as independent, native OS top-level windows. This would allow editors to distribute layouts across multiple physical monitors, similar to the multi-window behavior found in Adobe Premiere Pro or Photoshop.
Workaround attempted
The only way to use multiple screens currently is to run FilmCraft in windowed mode and manually stretch the master window frame across both desktops.

• OS: Windows 10 Home
• Version: 22H2
• OS Build: 19045.6466

title: Corrupt AAC packet with oversized MP4 duration allocates silence from untrusted timing metadata
author: nuclearspike
body:
Playing or exporting an MP4/M4A with a damaged AAC access unit and an oversized `stts` sample duration can consume memory far out of proportion to the file or the audio requested. If the decoder rejects the packet, `Mp4Source::audio_packet` allocates `sample.duration` floating-point samples for every channel. The duration comes from the file, while a short playback or export request needs only a small output window.

To reproduce on unpatched upstream `f03e215` (the same fallback remains on current `main`), build a one-track MP4 with AAC-LC 48 kHz stereo configuration, an empty access unit, and sample duration 1,000,000; ask the source for 128 audio frames. Trace allocations in `Mp4Source::audio_packet` or inspect its `Err(_)` branch: it creates two 1,000,000-sample float vectors before the 128-frame request returns silence.

Expected: a decoder failure is concealed within the requested audio window without allocating from the file's untrusted duration value. This matters during playback and export of received media, where an out-of-memory failure can interrupt work and lose unsaved changes.

title: macOS: dragging a LUT from Finder onto the open Input LUT file dialog aborts the app (SIGABRT — winit re-entrant event handling)
author: vark-debug
body:
## Summary

On macOS, dragging a LUT file from Finder **onto the open Input LUT file dialog** (Lumetri Color ▸ Input LUT ▸ Browse…) aborts the whole application: winit asserts re-entrant event handling and the queued-event closure is `panic_cannot_unwind`, so the app dies with SIGABRT. Reproduces every time (3/3 attempts, three macOS crash reports). Picking a file *by clicking* inside the dialog is not affected — the crash is triggered by the drag interacting with the dialog.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Import a 4K S-Log3 clip onto the timeline.
2. Select the clip, add **Lumetri Color**.
3. In Lumetri Color ▸ Basic ▸ Input LUT, click **Browse…** — the native macOS open panel opens.
4. Drag a `.cube` LUT from Finder **onto the open file dialog**.

→ The entire application aborts (SIGABRT). Reproduced 3/3 times (`FilmCraft-2026-10-15-155402/155418/160059.ips`).

## Expected

Dropping a file onto the open dialog either selects the dropped file or is ignored — the app must never abort.

## Actual

The process aborts on the main thread. The app's panic hook (the last-resort guard) does capture the panic, but the fatal panic happens inside a `panic_cannot_unwind` closure queued by winit, so the guard cannot save the process.

**The app's own crash log** (`<data dir>/Logs/crash-20741.log`, path redacted):

title: AAF/OMF import can replace existing files while extracting embedded audio
author: nuclearspike
body:
### Problem
Importing an AAF or OMF with embedded audio extracts WAVs to predictable names beside the document. If one of those names is occupied, the native host's atomic rename replaces the existing file. A repeat import can also replace a browser virtual-file entry at the same path. The previous media bytes cannot be recovered by undoing the project import.

### Reproduction
Export or obtain an AAF/OMF with embedded audio, then put distinct bytes at its generated WAV path (for example, `cut Media/Take 1.wav`). Import the document. The existing bytes are replaced. A synthetic regression pre-creates the path with `ORIGINAL USER DATA` and checks it remains unchanged while the imported clip points to a different, correctly extracted WAV.

### Expected
Reserve a new filename without replacing an occupied file or symlink, write the complete WAV, and update the imported media reference to the filename actually used. Report a write failure without overwriting existing media.

This report concerns embedded-audio filename collisions.

title: Chinese UI glyph fallback incomplete: wrong simplified forms (确) and missing glyphs (运)
author: vark-debug
body:
# Title: 中文 UI 字形回退不完整：简体字形错误（确→日字形）与缺字（运）

## 问题描述

在简体中文界面下，部分 UI 中文文本出现两类问题：

1. **字形错误**：如「确定」的「确」渲染为非简体（日式/繁式）字形
2. **缺字**：如「运动」的「运」（简体独有码位，繁体为「運」）渲染为缺字框（tofu）

根因：`crates/ui-egui/src/cjk.rs` 在没有 craft-fonts 中文字体时，会从系统字体中随机挑选一个覆盖样例字符串的 CJK 字体作为回退。该挑选不区分简体/日文字形优先级：

- macOS 上容易选中日文优先的字体（如 Hiragino），共用码位使用日文字形；
- 日文字体不含简体独有字（运、简、单……），导致缺字；
- 样例字符串 `SAMPLE`（"中文轨道配乐音效简体汉语繁體漢語车"）未覆盖这两个失败场景，挑选器自己检测不出问题。

## 建议方案

1. **首选：在 craft-fonts 仓库加入 Noto Sans SC（思源黑体 SC）子集**
   - 授权 SIL OFL 1.1，符合 AGENTS.md §1 资产要求
   - 标记 script 为 `Hans`，`cjk.rs` 的 craft-fonts 路径会自动优先使用
   - 字重建议 Regular(400) / Medium(500) / Bold(700)，对齐现有 `inter` / `inter-medium` / `inter-semibold` 家族
   - 原始 TTF 约 10MB/字重，用 `pyftsubset` 按 GB2312 + 常用符号子集化后可压到 1–2MB
   - 衬线场景可一并加入 Noto Serif SC，替换/补充现有 Noto Serif Regular 的中文覆盖

2. **回退改进：`cjk.rs` 的系统字体挑选应验证简体字形**
   - 扩充 `SAMPLE` 加入简体独有字（如「运确简单」），确保选中的字体真正覆盖
   - `PREFERRED` 列表在 macOS 上把日文优先字体（Hiragino 等）排除或降低优先级，优先 PingFang SC
   - 考虑对共用码位校验字形形态（或至少保证简体独有码位全覆盖，避免"半简半繁"混排）

## 背景

- 现状：Inter 拉丁 UI 字体与中文回退字体的风格衔接良好，但中文覆盖完全依赖运行时挑选的系统字体，跨平台行为不确定
- 相关代码：`crates/ui-egui/src/cjk.rs`（中文/韩文回退）、`crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs` 的 `install()`（字体栈安装，日文在中文之前）
- 字体规范：AGENTS.md §1.9 / craftrules `standards/fonts.md`（字体进 craft-fonts，不进本仓库）

title: Importing an FCP7 XML / FCPXML / OTIO / EDL ignores the Project panel's current bin (everything lands at the project root)
author: Sixelax
body:
What happens

I open the Project panel, navigate into a bin (e.g. Avis / Kordex), then File > Import an FCP7 XML. The media items and the sequence are all created at the project root, not in the bin I was in. Importing a plain video file does respect the bin.

Cause (from reading the code)

file.import computes bin from the bin param (the UI sends app.import_bin()), and passes it to media / image-sequence / caption imports. For interchange documents it calls crate::interchange::import(s, &path, &b, fmt), which has no bin parameter and hard-codes it:

crates/engine/src/interchange.rs

let seqs = filmcraft_interchange::merge_into(proj, fragment, None);
merge_into already accepts bin: Option<BinId> and falls back to the root if the bin is not found, so only the plumbing is missing.

Proposed fix (4 lines, 3 files; NOT compiled or tested on my side, I do not have a Rust toolchain)

interchange::import(..., bin: Option<BinId>) and pass bin to merge_into.
commands.rs (file.import): pass bin.
aaf_omf.rs (file.importAaf): pass None (unchanged behaviour).

title: [Audit] 5 defects with evidence and fix PRs: ipcm zero-bits division, FCPXML media cycle, TTML nesting depth, moved auto-points look unmodified, VTT arrow round trip
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
Round-4 audit: 5 defects on current `main`, each with an independent fix PR whose regression test fails on `main` and passes on the branch. None re-reports the round-1 topics (#1888: file:// char boundary; playhead; renderer-pool deadlocks).

### 1. `decode_pcm` divides by zero when an `ipcm`/`fpcm` entry declares `bits == 0` — crash
`crates/codecs/src/audio.rs:730` guards `channels` but takes `bits` straight from the file: `0.div_ceil(8)` is 0 → `data.len() / 0` panics the audio worker. The `sowt`/`twos`/`raw` arms default 0 to 16/8 and MXF's `decode_pcm` rejects `bps == 0`; the isobmff path never got the guard.
**Fix:** #2047

### 2. FCPXML import: self-referential `<media>` recurses until stack overflow — crash
The `media_items` memo fills only after the nested `sequence()` returns, so `<media id="b">` whose spine references `b` loops `media → sequence → storyline → element → media` and aborts with a stack overflow. FCP7 import, OTIO export and the FCPXML *exporter* all carry cycle guards; only this path missed one.
**Fix:** #2048

### 3. TTML import: unbounded `<div>`/`<span>` recursion — crash at depth
`walk`/`collect` take no depth parameter (`crates/captions/src/ttml.rs:559`, `:437`) while every other nestable-document walker in the repo is capped (AAF/OMF 32, store 200, comp 16, render 8). Measured: a 1000-deep document is walked in full on main, emitting cues with no warning.
**Fix:** #2049

### 4. `has_modified_intrinsics` never fires for moved auto-points — correctness
`param_eq_default`'s Vec2 arm ignores `v` (`crates/project/src/lib.rs:693`): any value equals a NaN "auto" default, so moved clips look untouched to the fx badge, the render fast path and multicam `take_intrinsics`. The interchange twin `param_modified` uses the correct both-NaN rule.
**Fix:** #2050

### 5. WebVTT `-->` escaping corrupts cue text on round trip — correctness/data corruption
The writer escapes `-->` as `-->` (`vtt.rs:140`) but the parser never decodes it: `A --> B` round-t…

title: A moved auto point never counts as modified
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
`param_eq_default`'s Vec2 arm ignores `v` (`crates/project/src/lib.rs:693`): any value equals a NaN "auto" default, so moved clips look untouched to the fx badge, the render fast path and multicam `take_intrinsics`. The interchange twin `param_modified` uses the correct both-NaN rule.

Fix: #2050

title: A self-referential FCPXML <media> recurses until the stack overflows
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
The `media_items` memo fills only after the nested `sequence()` returns, so `<media id="b">` whose spine references `b` loops `media → sequence → storyline → element → media` and aborts with a stack overflow. FCP7 import, OTIO export and the FCPXML *exporter* all carry cycle guards; only this path missed one.

Fix: #2048

title: An ipcm/fpcm entry declaring bits == 0 divides by zero in decode_pcm
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
`crates/codecs/src/audio.rs:730` guards `channels` but takes `bits` straight from the file: `0.div_ceil(8)` is 0 → `data.len() / 0` panics the audio worker. The `sowt`/`twos`/`raw` arms default 0 to 16/8 and MXF's `decode_pcm` rejects `bps == 0`; the isobmff path never got the guard.

Fix: #2047

title: TTML import recurses once per nesting level with no bound
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
`walk`/`collect` take no depth parameter (`crates/captions/src/ttml.rs:559`, `:437`) while every other nestable-document walker in the repo is capped (AAF/OMF 32, store 200, comp 16, render 8). Measured: a 1000-deep document is walked in full on main, emitting cues with no warning.

Fix: #2049

title: A cue-text arrow corrupts on the VTT write/parse round trip
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
The writer escapes `-->` as `-->` (`vtt.rs:140`) but the parser never decodes it: `A --> B` round-trips to `A --> B` on every VTT sidecar/export cycle.

Fix: #2051

title: Web: register a remote URL in the virtual FS (HTTP range reads), so a host page can open a project without downloading its media first
author: romanpert
body:
**Version:** web build 0.8.0. `apps/filmcraft-web` and `docs/web.md` are unchanged on `main` (8309f21).

**What happens**

To open a saved project through `window.filmcraft`, a host page first has to put every media file into the virtual FS:

- `importFiles(files)` takes `File` objects. Each one is registered under `/files/<name>` and imported with `file.import`, which also adds an item to the current bin (`apps/filmcraft-web/src/import.rs`, `import_files`).
- `importUrl(url)` fetches the whole response into a `Blob` (`api.rs`, `fetch_file`) and then imports it the same way.
- `openProject` then finds the media at the `/files/…` paths stored in the `.fcproj`.

When the footage lives on a server, the page has to download every byte before the project can open. Once a file is registered, `BlobReader` reads it on demand in 1 MiB chunks, and that part works well; the cost is getting the bytes into a `Blob` in the first place.

Measured with a 25-minute 1080p30 clip at 8 Mbps (1.53 GB), the browser on a PC reaching our server at 7–10 MB/s:

- the original: ~170 s to download before the project could open;
- a 720p proxy (282 MB): ~32 s, against 4.7 s with the browser on the same machine as the server.

**Proposal**

`window.filmcraft.registerUrl(url, path, { size? })`: a virtual-FS entry backed by a URL instead of a `Blob`.

- It is read with HTTP `Range` requests, through the same 1 MiB chunk cache and `WouldBlock`/retry path that `BlobReader` already uses.
- It does not import anything: it only makes the bytes available at `path`.
- `openProject` then resolves `path` as usual, and probing, playback and export fetch only the ranges they read.
- `size` (or a `HEAD`) gives the length up front.

Related, but not the same: #930 lets a parent page on the same origin hand media to FilmCraft as Blobs at the paths a project refers to. The bytes still arrive whole, and it needs a same-origin parent.

**Context:** we embed the FilmCraft web build (pinned 0.8.0) in a sandboxed ifr…

title: **Requirements distilled from the Fireship video**
author: k-dot-greyz
body:
**Requirements distilled from the Fireship video** (“Every app on Earth is now open source… whether it likes it or not”, Oct 12 2026) and related public context on ArtCraft / REA.

The video tests the claim that AI + reverse-engineering tooling now makes proprietary software effectively open-source. It shows Brandon Thomas’s ArtCraft suite (Rust clean-room recreations of Adobe Creative Cloud apps: PhotoCraft ≈ Photoshop, FilmCraft ≈ Premiere, etc.) and the REA MCP server that lets agents drive Ghidra/Hopper/IDA (and other analyzers) on binaries, Electron, .NET, etc.

### Core problems raised
- **ArtCraft/FilmCraft is not yet usable as a replacement**: UI mimics Premiere, but timeline/audio playback is sluggish, transitions are glitchy/poor, and overall performance is disappointing despite Rust. Early-alpha status across the suite (PhotoCraft more advanced; others “in development”).
- **Analysis ≠ polished product**: REA + AI can extract C-like pseudocode, symbols, call graphs, etc., from a local Premiere install and feed them to a coding agent for a simpler Rust feature. It is useful for learning behavior, not a turnkey full-app recovery.
- **Business-model drivers**: Adobe subscriptions + cancellation fees + no official Linux support create strong demand for free, native, cross-platform alternatives.
- **Tooling friction**: Decompilation output is low-level and imperfect; human/AI interpretation and clean reimplementation are still required. Legal boundary (clean-room from observable behavior/public specs vs. direct decompilation of Adobe code) matters.

### Actionable open-source requirements
To address the gaps in an open-source way, prioritize these:

1. **Performance & playback engine (highest priority for FilmCraft / video)**  
   - Smooth, real-time timeline scrubbing and playback on modest hardware.

title: **FilmCraft sitrep (core 80/20 workflows)**
author: k-dot-greyz
body:
**FilmCraft sitrep (core 80/20 workflows according to grok)**  
Repo cloned from `github.com/storytold/filmcraft` (shallow, main as of ~Oct 15 2026). Latest release noted: v0.8.0 (Oct 14). Status self-assessed as **alpha**.

### Headline numbers (from project docs, re-measured ~Oct 10 against Premiere Pro 26.5.2)
- Feature breadth: ~86% (menus ~92%, effects/transitions essentially complete)
- Ready for real work: ~56% (range ~51–61%)
- Essentials user: ~60%
- Stage: alpha (alpha gate passes on the main platform for the six core daily workflows)
- Remaining to beta: roughly 400–700 Opus-scale agent-hours (plus `.prproj`)

Architecture is a layered Cargo workspace (codecs/containers → foundations → edit/interchange → render/gpu/export → engine → ui-egui/automation). Command-driven engine (650+ commands) exposed via UI, CLI, JSON control channel, and MCP. Integer tick timebase (254,016,000,000/sec) for exact frame math. Own Rust codecs for H.264/HEVC/ProRes/AAC/etc. (not FFmpeg-dependent for the main path). GPU compositor via wgpu with CPU fallback.

### Core 80/20 workflows status

| Workflow | Status for daily use | Notes / gaps |
|----------|----------------------|--------------|
| **Import & organize** | Functional on supported media | H.264, HEVC, ProRes, VP9, AV1 decode, MP4/MOV/MKV/MXF, image sequences, multi-track audio. Hardware decode available (VideoToolbox / Media Foundation / VA-API). Gaps: 10-bit / 4:2:2 camera originals often need hardware (G3); limited real-world corpus testing; some containers/codecs still incomplete; no camera RAW. |
| **Timeline assemble & trim** | Core tools present | Three-point editing, ripple/roll/slip/slide/rate-stretch, razor, nesting, markers, snapping, unlimited undo, atomic saves + auto-save + crash recovery. Integer timebase avoids drift. UI still has fidelity gaps (handles, docking, filmstrip, transition editing controls — G8). |
| **Playback & scrub** | Works, but performance is the weak point | GPU compositor exists; man…

title: **High-leverage refactor cascade vectors for FilmCraft core**
author: k-dot-greyz
body:
**High-leverage refactor cascade vectors for FilmCraft core according to grok**

Reviewed the engine, project, render, and edit crates in the local clone. The foundation is better than most early NLE codebases (layered crates, command dispatch, COW project, pure edit algebra). The risks that will compound if left alone are concentration of logic and growing god objects.

### Cascade risk 1: `commands.rs` as a 4,400-line monolith (highest leverage)

- ~165 `cmd!` + 16 `query!` entries live in one file.
- Each command both validates and mutates, often reaching into multiple subsystems.
- New features will keep appending here. Review, testing, and agent schema generation all become harder.

**Cascade effect if left alone**  
Every new panel, effect, or interchange format adds another closure in the same file. Enablement logic, parameter parsing, and undo grouping become inconsistent. Bugs in one command are harder to isolate.

**Recommended vector**
- Split by domain into modules that the registry just collects: `commands/file.rs`, `commands/timeline.rs`, `commands/effects.rs`, `commands/audio.rs`, `commands/color.rs`, etc.
- Keep the `CommandSpec` + `cmd!`/`query!` macros.
- Move parameter parsing and pure validation into the domain modules so the closures stay thin.
- This is a mechanical change that immediately improves reviewability and makes future command additions local.

### Cascade risk 2: `Session` is becoming a god object

- `Session` holds project, history, media pool, prefs, jobs, voice-over, multicam recorder, TTS cache, export queue, media jobs, mask jobs, scene jobs, shortcuts, offline state, browser state, and more.
- ~47 public methods already. Several long-running features (voice-over, multicam live switch, TTS, proxy jobs) already live as fields on the session.

**Cascade effect if left alone**  
Every new background workflow adds another field and pump method. Lifetime and cancellation logic scatter. Testing a single feature requires constructing a…

title: Native PipeWire/PulseAudio audio backend, or a clear warning instead of a silent fallback to a raw ALSA hardware device
author: win-hafus
body:
## Summary
On Linux, filmcraft appears to output audio only through ALSA. On a PipeWire system where the ALSA plugin for PipeWire is not installed/configured, the app silently falls back to a raw hardware device and bypasses the sound server entirely. This ignores the user's default sink (e.g. Bluetooth headphones) and makes the app invisible in the PipeWire graph.

## What happened
- Setup: Gentoo, Hyprland, PipeWire + WirePlumber, `pipewire-pulse` installed, Bluetooth headphones set as the default sink.
- Other applications play to the headphones normally.
- filmcraft 0.8.0 (AppImage) played preview audio through the speakers instead, and never showed up in coppwr, so I couldn't re-route it.
- Log output on launch:
```
  ALSA lib .../pcm.c:2722:(snd_pcm_open_noupdate) [error.pcm] Unknown PCM pipewire
  ALSA lib .../pcm.c:2722:(snd_pcm_open_noupdate) [error.pcm] Unknown PCM pulse
  ALSA lib .../pcm.c:2722:(snd_pcm_open_noupdate) [error.pcm] Unknown PCM jack
  ALSA lib .../pcm.c:2722:(snd_pcm_open_noupdate) [error.pcm] Unknown PCM oss
  WARN [main] filmcraft::audio: the default audio output device cannot be opened; falling back to 'HD-Audio Generic'
```
- Root cause on my side: PipeWire was built without the `pipewire-alsa` USE flag, so `/etc/alsa/conf.d/` had no PipeWire configs. After enabling it and rebuilding, the errors disappeared and audio went to the headphones.

So this is not a bug in filmcraft itself, but the failure mode is confusing: the user gets no error in the UI, audio just plays on the wrong device, and the log message doesn't hint at the cause.

## Proposed improvements
1. **Native PipeWire / PulseAudio backend** (if the audio library used supports it), so the app works with the system default sink regardless of whether the ALSA compatibility plugin is installed. This is especially relevant for the AppImage, which can't rely on the host's ALSA configuration.
2. **Visible warning** in the UI (and a more descriptive log message) when the default out…

title: Suggestion: live-linked compositions between apps (Dynamic Link-style interop)
author: Jaimetud
body:
One of Adobe's best workflow features is Dynamic Link — sending a Premiere sequence to After Effects as a live-linked comp instead of rendering an intermediate file. Changes on either side update without re-exporting.

Would love to see something similar across the Craft apps, starting with FilmCraft ↔ EffectCraft: right-click a FilmCraft sequence → "Send to EffectCraft," opening as a live-linked comp where edits on either side reflect without an intermediate render.

Longer term this could extend to other pairs (PhotoCraft ↔ DesignCraft, VectorCraft ↔ FilmCraft for motion graphics) through a shared project-linking protocol.

I know the apps currently exchange data via interchange formats (XML, AAF, IDML, SVG, PDF), which works — this would be the step up from file-based round-tripping to live linking.

Thanks for the daily builds, genuinely exciting to watch the suite come together.

title: Export: SDR ProRes, DNxHR, MJPEG and APV files carry no colr colour tags (QuickTime / Final Cut see no colour)
author: ssandweiss
body:
**What happens:** SDR exports in MOV formats carry no colour description that Apple's media stack reads. `export::ColorTags::apply_to` writes the sample entry's `colr` box only for HDR (it returns early otherwise), so these exports have none:

- **ProRes, DNxHR, MJPEG and APV:** AVFoundation, which QuickTime Player and Final Cut Pro use, sees no colour primaries, transfer function or matrix for them. They only read `colr`, not ProRes's frame header or DNx's own fields. Each app then has to guess.
- **H.264 and HEVC** are fine: AVFoundation takes BT.709 from the stream's VUI.

Checked on current `main` (8309f21): export the demo with `file.exportMedia` in each format, then read the track's `CMFormatDescription` colour extensions. H.264 and HEVC report `ITU_R_709_2` for all three. ProRes, DNxHR, MJPEG and APV report none. ffprobe reports bt709 for all of them, because it parses the codec headers.

**Expected:** like Premiere and Final Cut exports, every video sample entry gets a `colr` box with the export's primaries, transfer and matrix: nclc for MOV, nclx (with the range flag) for MP4. Typically that's 1/1/1 for SDR BT.709.

I'm working on this and will open a PR shortly. (PR #1827 already adds `colr` for its new uncompressed formats; this covers the rest.)

title: macOS: dragging a video from Photos.app imports a JPEG poster frame instead of the movie
author: scottyallen
body:
## What happens

Dragging a video out of Photos.app into FilmCraft imports a **still image** instead of the video. The clip lands in the Project panel as a JPEG, and on the timeline it behaves as a still.

The drop reports success, so nothing signals that the wrong media came in until the still shows up in the edit.

## Why

Photos.app offers the movie only as a *file promise*. The only real path on the drag pasteboard is a JPEG poster frame inside the Photos library, and winit asks the pasteboard for `NSFilenamesPboardType` alone, so that poster frame is what reaches `handle_drops`.

The pasteboard from a Photos.app video drag (macOS 26):

```
com.apple.pasteboard.promised-suggested-file-name = IMG_5691.MOV
com.apple.pasteboard.promised-file-content-type  = com.apple.quicktime-movie
public.file-url       = …/Photos Library.photoslibrary/resources/derivatives/D/<uuid>_1_102_o.jpeg
NSFilenamesPboardType = [ …/derivatives/D/<uuid>_1_102_o.jpeg ]
```

Mapping the path back to the original is not a workaround: an iCloud asset has no local original at all (the library's `originals/` holds no file for that UUID) until the promise is fulfilled and Photos downloads it.

This is not specific to Photos: any source that hands over promised files rather than paths (Mail attachments, some browser drags) is affected the same way. Upstream gap: [rust-windowing/winit#2201](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/issues/2201).

## Steps to reproduce

1. macOS, open FilmCraft with any sequence.
2. Open Photos.app and drag a video onto the Project panel or the Timeline.
3. The imported item is a JPEG, not the movie.

## Environment

macOS 26 (Apple silicon), FilmCraft at 8309f21.

## Fix

[#2147](https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/pull/2147) handles the promises: they are claimed during `performDragOperation:` and fulfilled on the next run-loop turn, and the resolved files are imported as the drop they belong to.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: [Feature Request] [SoundCraft] Import legacy Pro Tools sessions, including Pro Tools First projects
author: pajzd
body:
Feature request: Import legacy Pro Tools sessions, including Pro Tools First projects

Summary

Please investigate support for importing legacy Pro Tools session files, including projects created with Pro Tools First, so users can recover and continue working on audio projects even when the original application is discontinued or a subscription ends.

The problem

I invested time and money in Pro Tools and created projects I expected to be able to access later. After my subscription was cancelled, I lost access to my projects through the software. 

I had understood that I would still be able to open the version I had paid for, even without renewing the subscription, but in practice I could no longer access my projects as expected.

Audio projects are long-term creative work. They should not become stranded because a product is discontinued or access to the original application changes.

Proposed solution

Please investigate importing as many Pro Tools session generations and formats as technically feasible, including:

Legacy Pro Tools session files, including .ptx where feasible.

Pro Tools First projects and their associated media and project structures.

Audio media, track names and ordering, clip positions, edits, fades, and other session metadata wherever recoverable.

Clear reporting of what could and could not be recovered when exact reconstruction is not possible.

A best-effort recovery path would still be valuable if some session details cannot be reconstructed perfectly.

Relationship to existing interchange support

FilmCraft already supports AAF and OMF interchange. That is useful, but it does not necessarily recover a native Pro Tools session—especially a Pro Tools First project—when the user can no longer open the original application to export an interchange file. The goal is to explore recovery from the original session or project files and any associated media that remains available.

title: Exported video leads audio by ~0.2 s on phone HEVC footage (constant offset)
author: sidharthwarrier
body:
**Version:** FilmCraft 0.8.0, commit c2f65871, filmcraft-cli built on Linux (debian:bookworm-slim, rust 1.95), CPU-only, no GPU.

**Source file:** phone recording, MP4, HEVC Main 3840×2160, variable frame rate (~29.88 fps, 1,852 stts entries), AAC stereo 48 kHz. Has a video edit list (elst media_time 8034/90000 ≈ 0.089 s) and B-frame ctts.

**Steps:**
1. file.import the clip
2. file.newSequenceFromClip
3. export with --format h264 --start 10 --end 20 --scale 0.5

title: FCPXML import skips `<title>`, so titles from DaVinci Resolve / Final Cut are lost
author: LaBMediaGroup
body:
**Version:** web build 0.8.0 and `main` (c2f6587).

**What happens**

Importing an FCPXML timeline drops every title clip. `crates/interchange/src/fcpxml.rs` (around line 402)
matches `"title" | "video" | "audio" | "sync-clip" | "mc-clip" | "live-drawing"` and skips them with
"FCPXML <title> elements are not supported and were skipped". DaVinci Resolve writes its Text and Text+
titles as `<title>` elements in its FCPXML 1.9–1.11 export, so a trailer or short cut in Resolve comes
into FilmCraft with its title cards missing and gaps where they were.

**Proposal**

Import `<title>` as a FilmCraft text/graphics clip on its lane: the text from `<text>/<text-style>`
(content, font, size, colour, alignment from the referenced `text-style-def`), its position and duration
from the element, and `adjust-transform` if present. Effects/animation that can't be mapped could import
as plain static text with a report entry, the way other unsupported parts are reported. Export the same
way so a round trip keeps the titles.

**Sample:** a minimal Resolve FCPXML 1.10 with one video clip and one Text title (happy to share the file).

title: Web: relink imported timeline media by file name
author: LaBMediaGroup
body:
**Version:** web build 0.8.0 and `main` (c2f6587).

**What happens**

Timelines exported from an NLE (Resolve FCPXML/OTIO, Premiere XML) reference media by absolute
`file:///Users/...` URLs. On the web every clip imports offline:

- relative paths resolve against the document's virtual folder `/files` (`crates/engine/src/interchange.rs:31`),
  but absolute URLs never match a registered `/files/<name>`;
- `media.autoRelink { folder }` scans with `std::fs::read_dir` (`relink.rs:478`), which finds nothing in
  the browser;
- relative paths aren't percent-decoded (`crates/interchange/src/common.rs`, `file_url_to_path`), so
  `Clip%20A.mov` doesn't match `Clip A.mov` even when the user imports the media first.

So a browser user who imports the media files and then the timeline still has to Locate… clip by clip.

**Proposal**

When an imported timeline's media path doesn't resolve on the web, fall back to matching by decoded file
name against files already registered in the virtual FS (and against files picked in the same import),
then by name stem, and report what was linked and what stayed offline. Percent-decode file URLs in
`file_url_to_path` for relative paths too. Same behaviour could back `media.autoRelink` on the web, over
the virtual table instead of `read_dir`.

**Sample:** a Resolve FCPXML 1.10 with two video and two audio clips at absolute paths, plus the four
media files (happy to share them; a few seconds each).

title: [Linux] Voice-over shows Recording after the audio input backend fails

body:
### Description
When starting voice-over recording on Linux, FilmCraft can enter `Recording` while microphone audio is not being captured. The countdown also appears to depend on timeline position: moving the playhead backward while the countdown runs makes the remaining delay grow. After waiting until the app reports `Recording`, no mic audio starts.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Open a project and start voice-over recording from the timeline.
2. While the pre-roll/countdown is running, move the playhead backward.
3. Wait until the countdown reaches the recording point.
4. Observe that FilmCraft shows `Recording`, but microphone audio is not captured.

### Expected behavior
The countdown should reach a stable recording point and capture microphone audio. If the input device cannot be opened or read, FilmCraft should stop the recording attempt and show an actionable error instead of remaining in `Recording`.

### Actual behavior
The remaining countdown grows as the playhead is moved backward. FilmCraft later shows `Recording`, but no voice-over audio is captured.

- FilmCraft 0.8.0, Linux x86_64
- CachyOS Linux, kernel 7.2.9-2-cachyos
- PipeWire 1.6.9, WirePlumber 0.5.18
- USB input: Fifine Microphone (VID:PID 3142:a010)

filmcraft: audio input error: A backend-specific error has occurred: `alsa::poll()` returned POLLERR

title: [Bug Report] [FilmCraft] FCPXML import ignores spatial conform: a 4K clip in a 1080p sequence lands at scale 100 (cropped) instead of fit
author: Wbunker
body:
**Version:** FilmCraft 0.8.0, Linux x86_64 (.deb), headless `filmcraft-cli`

**What happens:** importing an FCPXML whose sequence is 1920×1080 and whose clip is a 3840×2160 source puts the clip on the timeline at scale 100. The export is a 2× centre crop of the source.

**Expected:** FCPXML's default spatial conform is `fit` (no `<adjust-conform>` element means fit), so the clip should land at scale 50, the way Final Cut and DaVinci Resolve open the same file. An explicit `<adjust-conform type="fit"/>` inside the `<asset-clip>` is ignored as well.

**Repro:**
```sh
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc2=size=3840x2160:rate=30:duration=2 -c:v prores cam4k.mov
# t.fcpxml: <format id="r1" frameDuration="1/30s" width="1920" height="1080"/>, one <asset-clip> of cam4k.mov in the spine
filmcraft-cli --save-as t.fcproj exec file.newProject

filmcraft-cli --project t.fcproj inspect sequence   # motion.scale = 100
filmcraft-cli --project t.fcproj export out.mov --format prores

title: Oversized frame metadata can enter saved projects
author: nuclearspike
body:
A `.fcproj` can store dimensions above FilmCraft's existing 32,768-pixel side and 268,435,456-pixel area limits on media video metadata, graphics, and adjustment layers. Project decode currently accepts a 1,000,000×1,000,000 value on each item kind. Media import, relink, refresh, creation commands, and interchange fragments can also introduce dimensions that a stricter decoder would reject on the next open. Rendering from oversized metadata can request excessive memory; the hazardous render was not run.

Safe reproduction: encode a project with an offline media item whose reported video size is 1,000,000×1,000,000, then decode it. Repeat with a graphic and an adjustment-layer canvas. On unpatched main, each decode succeeds. A Y4M source reporting 32,769×1 can be imported and stored; an interchange XML can likewise report oversized source or sequence dimensions. The regression tests exercise these paths without rendering a hazardous frame.

Expected: reject dimensions outside the shared project limit before `file.open` replaces the open project or ingest stores the out-of-range values. Creation, import, relink, refresh, interchange, manual and automatic save, recovery-journal snapshots, template and selection export, and Project Manager output should enforce the same limit so a new save cannot overwrite the last reopenable project file. Preserve valid boundary sizes and the exact `(0,0)` unknown-video marker. Older files that already contain out-of-range metadata must remain on disk and produce an item-specific error instead of a crash; they may need repair before opening.

title: Image-sequence frames bypass the project frame-size limit
author: nuclearspike
body:
An image sequence can contain a frame whose decoded dimensions exceed FilmCraft's supported frame-size limit. The first frame becomes sequence metadata, and later frames can enter the cache and composition without checking that limit. A small safe reproduction uses a PNG with width 32,769 and height 1, which exceeds the existing 32,768-pixel side limit without requiring a large allocation.

Construct an `ImageSequenceSource` with that frame first, or with a valid 16×8 first frame followed by an out-of-range frame. Before the fix, source creation or a later frame request accepts the decoded oversized frame. Expected: reject the frame before sequence metadata, cache, or composition uses it. The existing eight-candidate search may hold a nearby verified frame. A later rejected frame should be retried on the next request when the host supplies live file reads; a rejected first frame requires reopening or reimporting the sequence. The check runs after still-image decoding, so decoder-internal and accepted-frame rendering allocations are separate problems.

A user reports that a mouse wheel configured to shrink/enlarge web pages unexpectedly resized the entire FilmCraft interface. Scrolling in the enlargement direction continued, but scrolling the other way did not reverse the change.

Source: <https://discord.com/channels/1359579021108842617/1557517316995162214/1560885425827090503> (2026-10-17 05:21 UTC).

That does not establish correct handling of this wheel mapping or a fix in the reporter's build.

Related but distinct: #1983 and open PR #2168 address toolbar items becoming unreachable at large UI scale, not asymmetric whole-interface zoom. title: Feature Request - Add Copy and Paste Functionality for Shapes in the Shapes Panel
author: AJMakesStuff
body:
Currently, the Shapes panel does not provide an option to copy and paste individual shapes within a shape layer.

It would be useful to have functionality similar to Adobe Premiere Pro, where users can easily duplicate shapes within the same graphics layer without having to manually recreate them.

### **Current Behavior**

- There is no dedicated copy or paste option for individual shapes within a shape layer.
- Users must manually recreate shapes when they want multiple instances of the same shape.
- This makes working with multiple similar shapes unnecessarily time-consuming.

### **Expected Behavior**

Users should be able to:

- Copy: Copy a selected shape using Ctrl+C or a right-click context menu.
- Paste: Paste the copied shape using Ctrl+V within the same or another shape layer.
- Duplicate: Quickly duplicate a selected shape using Ctrl+D.
- Preserve Properties: Retain the original shape's dimensions, position, fill, stroke, opacity, and other styling properties.
- Independent Editing: Modify duplicated shapes without affecting the original.

### **Suggested Implementation**

Introduce copy, paste, and duplicate actions within the Shapes panel, similar to the workflow available in Adobe Premiere Pro's graphics editing tools.

These actions should be accessible through keyboard shortcuts and a right-click context menu.

### **Benefits**

This would improve the overall workflow when working with multiple shapes, reduce repetitive actions, and make the Shapes panel more intuitive and efficient.

title: Offline placeholders allocate from source dimensions
author: nuclearspike
body:
An offline media item retains its source's video dimensions. Its placeholder generator uses those dimensions to build a float image and RGBA8 copy. Valid high-resolution metadata, such as 15,360×8,640, can therefore demand substantial preview memory even though an offline warning does not need a source-sized raster. Concurrent frame workers can multiply this work. The hazardous large render was not run.

Safe reproduction: create a `SlateSource` with high-resolution metadata and request a full-scale frame; inspect its generated dimensions and allocations. On unpatched main, the slate scales from the full source size and the direct slate helper has no size limit. The regression tests use dimensions without rendering a hazardous frame.

Expected: preserve source metadata and render a bounded placeholder for valid high-resolution metadata, while bounding retained slate image data per active media pool and serializing generation within each pool generation. The slate source should also produce bounded frames from malformed metadata; the existing Source-monitor widget does not show `(0,0)` video metadata, so that widget path is outside this report. Direct helpers should return an error for invalid requested raster dimensions, and hostile names should not force unbounded text layout. Ordinary display aspect ratios should remain useful; extreme source aspect ratios may have no readable warning text in Source-monitor Fit; that display limitation is outside this allocation report.
