title: Timeline clipboard paste ignores the chosen destination track
author: earlvanze
body:
A user asks whether copied media/audio clips can be pasted onto a specific timeline track: https://discord.com/channels/1359579021108842617/1557517316995162214/1560998043258593301 (2026-10-17). Their version and OS are not yet known.

Current main source at 09aaf9bf15d510eda1c413c0ccabb1d7e08b41c5, `crates/engine/src/commands.rs`, `paste()`, places copied timeline items using their saved track index (`tracks.get(ti).or(tracks.last())`). It does not consult the destination targeting state. This is a source-level finding, not a GUI reproduction of the user's attachment.

Please support choosing the destination track for Paste/Paste Insert of copied timeline clips, retaining relative track offsets and linked audio/video relationships, and respecting locks and undo. Suggested regression case: copy from A1, select A2 as the destination, then paste at the playhead and verify the clip lands on A2. Include video and multi-track cases.

This is separate from OS clipboard file/image paste, implemented in #615: `paste_media.rs` already starts from the source-patched destination and seeks a free track when needed. It is also separate from copying effects and the macOS duplicate-paste issue #1773.

Existing open issues/PRs and roadmap/gaps were checked for timeline destination paste; no focused match was found. Temporary workaround for timeline copies: paste into an empty area on the original track, then move the pasted clip to the desired track while preserving its time position.

author: Silvazrlq

# Mapa de integração VA-API para exportação

Auditoria somente leitura do snapshot `/home/silvaz/FilmCraftV/upstream`, orientada pelo `goal-objective.md`. Nenhum código, build ou teste foi alterado/executado. `upstream/AGENTS.md` e `upstream/CLAUDE.md` foram lidos.

## Conclusão executiva

O upstream já tem um contrato de encoder plugável, multiplexador MP4/MOV com sample entries para AVC/HEVC/AV1 e encoder H.264 software. Não tem encode VA-API: `platform/src/vaapi/` implementa decode H.264/HEVC; `platform::register()` no Linux registra NVENC para encode e registra VA-API somente como decoder. O código de #1256 é uma base concreta para H.264 8-bit SDR; #408 fornece referência antiga para H.264/HEVC, mas ambas as PRs permanecem abertas e fora de `main` segundo o snapshot salvo.

## Codecs de export realmente disponíveis

| Codec/formato | Estado efetivo no upstream | Limite para VA-API |
|---|---|---|
| H.264/AVC | Encoder Rust embutido, qualquer sistema; NVENC no Linux/Windows quando `HardwareEncoding::Auto`; VideoToolbox no macOS. Linux VA-API ainda ausente. Perfil software High; opções de perfil export incluem Baseline/Main/High. | #1256 aceita Baseline/Main/High, 8-bit 4:2:0 SDR, CBR/VBR, progressive, MP4/MOV. Declina HDR, MXF, CRF, two-pass e outras configurações sem suporte. |

title: Status bar: painted text can never be selected or copied
author: switch87
body:
## The defect

The status bar at the bottom of the window paints its text:

```rust
ui.painter().text(
    egui::pos2(sb.min.x + 10.0, sb.center().y),
    egui::Align2::LEFT_CENTER,
    hint,
    Tokens::ui(11.0),
    t.text_dim,
);
```

Painted text is pixels. It can be read, but never selected, copied,
searched for, or enlarged by the user's font scaling — and this bar is
where Filmcraft puts exactly the strings a person wants to take
somewhere else: a rendered path, a file it could not open, the reason an
export stopped, the frame range it just wrote.

The toast had the same defect (drawn as painted text, and in fact never
drawn at all); it is being fixed to use a `Label`, which can be selected
and copied. This issue asks for the same treatment for the status bar.

## What it should look like

- The hint and the transient status messages are a `Label` in the same
  20 px bar, left-aligned, ellipsized at the bar's right edge.
- The 8 s auto-clear of `status_seen` stays: the message disappears on
  time, it just is not painted any more.
- Selecting text in the bar should not fight the rest of the UI for
  mouse input: the label is selectable but the bar itself stays inert
  (no click-through to whatever is underneath it).

## Why now

The toast renderer landed as a shared, panic-guarded piece of UI that
draws the engine's messages; the status bar is the other half of the
same story — the messages that stay instead of disappearing after
3.5 seconds. Doing both means every message Filmcraft can produce is
either copied with the mouse or read aloud with the text tool.

title: [Bug Report] [FilmCraft] Audio bar lag + overall slowness, Transition quality
author: ticket-craft
body:
### Description

1. Audio bar lag + overall slowness — The killer was in panels/meters.rs: while an audio device was playing, the UI thread re-rendered the entire programme audio mix every single frame (decode + effects + mixer graph) just to feed the loudness meter — a duplicate of the work the audio mixing thread was already doing. It created a feedback loop (slower frame → more audio to re-mix next frame → even slower), plus lock contention with the real audio thread. On top: meters max-merged peaks from the mixing thread (which runs 0.2 s ahead of the device) without timestamps, every finished frame job woke the UI for a full re-layout, and the GPU compositor allocated fresh wgpu textures + uniform buffers for every layer of every displayed frame.

2. Transition quality — Smooth dissolves/soft wipes quantized to 8-bit with no dithering (visible staircasing/banding on gradients), playback defaulted to half resolution (transitions rendered soft, then upscaled), and wipe anti-aliasing defaulted to Low and was halved again at half-res playback (aliased diagonal edges exactly when playing).

Reported behavior: the user cannot use the downloadable Text to Speech model. OS, application version, installation source, exact error and reproduction steps are pending. The attached screenshot could not be retrieved during triage (HTTP 403); no screenshot contents or specific error are inferred.

Source inspection at cb14e31cf1486b094837cb0440c5a7510e08a204:
- `crates/tts/README.md` and `crates/tts/src/catalog.rs` document the approximately 336 MB Kokoro-82M natural-voice package.

- `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/tts.rs` offers natural-voice download controls and surfaces download errors in the status message.
- `crates/speech/src/models.rs::download_files` performs HTTP downloads and pinned size/checksum verification.

title: Feature Request: Differential Updates for Windows  Problem
author: Mohamed-Amir60
body:
Windows users currently need to download the full FilmCraft MSI installer for each release. For frequent updates, this can consume unnecessary bandwidth and time when only a small portion of the application has changed.

Proposed solution

Consider implementing an in-app update system with differential downloads:

* Check the installed version against the latest release.
* Download only changed files or binary patches where practical.
* Verify downloaded content using cryptographic hashes and trusted signatures.
* Apply updates safely, with rollback support if an update fails.
* Keep the full MSI installer available as a fallback for fresh installations and failed updates.

Suggested implementation approach

Start with a signed update manifest and content-hash-based file updates. Evaluate binary delta patches later if they offer meaningful bandwidth savings without excessive maintenance complexity.

Expected benefits

* Smaller downloads for routine updates.
* Faster updates for users with limited bandwidth.
* A smoother release experience as FilmCraft evolves.
* Fewer manual installation steps.

The updater should preserve user projects, preferences, and other application data across upgrades.

title: Captions: add a drop-shadow style control
author: earlvanze
body:
## Request

A user asked how to add a shadow to captions.

## Current behaviour

Caption track styling supports text colour, background box, outline, alignment, position, margin, and line spacing. It has no drop-shadow control. Graphic text has configurable shadow controls, but caption tracks do not.

Add a caption-track shadow setting with colour, opacity, angle, distance, size, and blur controls, rendered consistently in the Program monitor and burned-in exports. Preserve the setting in project files and expose it through `captions.setStyle`.

title: Feature: installable transition packs and reusable transition bundles

title: Bug: timeline audio crackles during playback, investigate VFR and output underruns
author: earlvanze
body:
### Bug

Timeline audio crackles during editing. The reporter suspects a variable-frame-rate source, but the report does not yet establish the source format, operating system, device, or project sample rate.

### Initial investigation

FilmCraft exposes playback audio underrun and missing-frame counters through `perf.stats`; this report should distinguish decoder/timing trouble from device-output underruns.

### Needed to reproduce

- FilmCraft version and operating system
- Source file codec, frame-rate mode, and audio sample rate

title: Support uncompressed QuickTime video (raw  24-bit RGB and v210) in MOV files
author: svarzaru
body:
FilmCraft reports MOV files with uncompressed video as unreadable. It reads the container and the sample description, then stops without reading any sample data.

Files

These MOV files come from a virtual drive (Two Left Wheels 360) that serves stitched 360° camera recordings to video editors. They use uncompressed video so that every frame has a fixed size and position:

8-bit sources: video sample description raw with depth 24, which is packed 8-bit RGB with 3 bytes per pixel and no padding. A typical clip is 7680×3840.
10-bit sources: v210, which is 10-bit 4:2:2 YCbCr.
Audio: fl32, 32-bit float PCM at 48 kHz, stereo, in a version 1 QuickTime sound description.
Layout: each frame is one sample, all samples are the same size, and the moov is at the start of the file.
DaVinci Resolve and FFmpeg read these files.

What happens

FilmCraft 0.6.0 on Windows 11 opens the file, reads the start and the end, walks the boxes up to the sample description (about 20 KB), and then shows "the file is unreadable". It never requests a frame.

Request

Please support raw  (24-bit RGB) and v210 video in MOV files, and fl32 audio if it isn't supported yet. Neither video format needs a decoder: a raw  frame is the pixels as they are, and v210 is a fixed bit packing. Uncompressed video is also common for intermediate files and for capture from other tools.

I can provide a short sample file in each format.

title: audio-dsp: tempo alternatives (half/double), double-time check and free-time detection
author: 4waymedia
body:
## Summary

`audio_dsp::remix::analyze` picks one tempo: the strongest prior-weighted autocorrelation peak between 50 and 200 BPM. It returns `NoBeat` below a pulse of 0.1. That works for Remix. Features that show or act on the beat grid need more: suggested cuts on music, BPM display, beat markers. They need to know when the tempo might be half or double, when the tracker locked onto half-time, and when music has no steady pulse at all.

This proposes additive changes to the analysis in `crates/audio-dsp/src/remix.rs`. Remix's planner and its existing tests keep working unchanged.

## Proposal

| # | Change | Why |
|---|--------|-----|
| 1 | **Tempo candidates.** Keep the best 3 weighted autocorrelation peaks (parabolically refined), plus the chosen tempo's ×½ and ×2 with their scores | Octave errors are the most common tempo mistake. A UI can offer "half time / double time" in one click instead of re-analysing |
| 2 | **Double-time check.** After tracking, compare onset strength halfway between beats with strength on the beats. If the off-beats are ≥ 0.8 as strong (and 2× stays ≤ 200 BPM), double the tempo and track again | Equal clicks at 174 BPM read as 87 today, because the prior pulls toward 120. Kick-and-snare music with quieter hats in between is unaffected |
| 3 | **BPM from the beats.** `bpm` from a least-squares line through the tracked beat times (≥ 8 beats), else from the period as today | One frame of autocorrelation lag is ±2–5 % of the tempo. The slope over a whole track is a small fraction of a BPM |
| 4 | **Steady or free time.** Pulse clarity (normalised autocorrelation at the period, 0–1) and the coefficient of variation of beat intervals. Clarity < 0.25 or variation > 0.08 → `Rhythm::Free` | Ambient, rubato and spoken pieces shouldn't get a beat grid by default. Callers can cut on sections and swells instead |

Remix's own behaviour: (1), (3) and (4) are information only. `period` stays consistent with `bpm`, and the `MIN_PULSE` → `NoBeat` rule …

title: nvenc_hevc_hdr_export`: `the_factory_rejects_mismatched_pictures_and_clamps_hostile_floats` fails since SDR exports gained a `colr` box (#2142)
author: DWHowes
body:
On `main` at 48088e3a, Windows 10, Rust 1.99.0 (MSVC), NVIDIA GTX 1660 Ti (NVENC HEVC Main 10 available), this test fails:

```
---- the_factory_rejects_mismatched_pictures_and_clamps_hostile_floats stdout ----
panicked at crates\platform\tests\nvenc_hevc_hdr_export.rs:352:5:
assertion failed: eight.sample_entry().video.as_ref().unwrap().color.is_none()
```

Reproduce with `cargo test -p filmcraft-platform --test nvenc_hevc_hdr_export`. The test returns early with "SKIPPED: no NVENC HEVC Main 10 here" on machines without an NVIDIA encoder, so it probably doesn't run in CI. Everything else in the workspace passes here (3,544 passed, 46 ignored).

**Cause.** 678fe732, "fix(export): tag SDR exports with a colr box (#2142)", changed `ColorSignal::apply_to` (`crates/export/src/lib.rs`) so that SDR exports also get a `colr` box. `NvencEncoder::sample_entry` (`crates/platform/src/nvenc/export.rs`) calls `self.signal.apply_to(&mut e, false)` for HEVC, so the SDR (Main, 8-bit) encoder's sample entry now carries `colr` nclx BT.709 (1/1/1, limited range). The test still asserts the pre-#2142 behaviour:

```rust
// the sample entry of the HDR encoder carries colr + mdcv + clli, the SDR one nothing HDR
assert!(eight.sample_entry().video.as_ref().unwrap().color.is_none());
```

The intent in the comment ("nothing HDR") still holds. The SDR entry has no `mdcv` or `clli`, and its `colr` is BT.709, not PQ or HLG. Only the assertion is out of date. The comment in `nvenc/export.rs` ("SDR stays as it was, with the VUI only") is also out of date since #2142.

**Suggested fix:** assert what "nothing HDR" now means for the SDR entry:

```rust
let v8 = eight.sample_entry().video.unwrap();
assert!(matches!(v8.color, Some(filmcraft_isobmff::ColorInfo::Nclx { primaries: 1, transfer: 1, matrix: 1, full_range: false })));
assert!(v8.mastering_display.is_none() && v8.content_light.is_none());
```

title: Severe timeline playhead lag in FilmCraft 0.9.0 on Windows with AMD Radeon
author: M71-ISA
body:
# Severe timeline playhead lag in FilmCraft 0.9.0 on Windows with Radeon RX 550

## Description

Dragging the timeline playhead is noticeably sluggish and unresponsive. Both the playhead movement and the video preview lag behind the mouse movement.

The issue also occurs in a completely empty project, so it does not appear to depend on the video codec, timeline complexity, or applied effects.

## Environment

- **Application:** FilmCraft 0.9.0
- **Operating system:** Windows 11 Pro 24H2
- **GPU:** AMD Radeon RX 550, 4 GB VRAM
- **GPU acceleration report:** `Radeon RX550/550 Series`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Launch FilmCraft 0.9.0.
2. Create a new, empty project.
3. Drag the playhead along the timeline.
4. Observe the playhead movement and preview response.

## Actual behavior

- The playhead does not follow the mouse smoothly.
- The preview also responds sluggishly.
- GPU 3D utilization rises noticeably during the interaction, reaching approximately 22% in my testing.
- The lag persists on every attempt, even after leaving the application idle for 30 seconds.
- Reducing the visible timeline area does not improve responsiveness.
- Launching the application with `WGPU_BACKEND=gl` does not resolve the issue.

## Expected behavior

The playhead should follow mouse movement smoothly, and the preview should respond promptly, including when working with an empty project.

## Additional information

The issue appears to affect timeline interaction itself, not only video decoding or playback. I have not yet established whether the cause is related to GPU rendering, event handling, or another part of the rendering pipeline.

Could the maintainers investigate timeline scrubbing responsiveness on Windows with AMD Radeon RX 550 hardware, particularly in version 0.9.0?

title: Feature (Beyond Premiere): Video De-Noise with motion compensation, Diffusion and a VHS Look
author: danielbanariba
body:
## What it is

I'm moving a Premiere edit of live concert footage to Linux, and three things it leans on are missing here: a video denoise that does not ghost on fast motion, a diffusion (mist) look, and a VHS look. This proposes them as three video effects, CPU first, and asks the folder question from #1175 once for all of them. I'll implement them one at a time, starting with the denoise.

Today there is Noise, VR De-Noise (spatial only, VR layouts), the obsolete Median and the Lights & Glows set, but no general or temporal denoise. The VHS Damage transition exists (`vtransition.rs`) but there is no clip-level VHS effect. I am **not** proposing bloom: Wonder Glow already blurs thresholded highlights at three radii. Halation is #1175.

Measured on that footage: a temporal filter without motion compensation (FFmpeg's hqdn3d, run only as an external reference) leaves a doubled hand and smeared guitar strings at the strength that removes the noise. A useful denoise needs motion compensation, or temporal weights that back off where frames differ.

## Proposal

### 1. Video De-Noise (first)

| Id | Name | Default | Range | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|

The one thing I really miss is small custom scripts that automate repetitive timeline edits. In Vegas Pro 18, `Tools > Scripting` lists every script in a folder, and each one can have a keyboard shortcut (screenshot 4). My two most-used scripts: - **Cut silences** from a clip. - **Gap between blocks v2**: I select several clips, enter N seconds, and every block is spaced exactly N seconds from the previous one, with optional ripple for everything after (screenshots 1–3: before, dialog, after). Together they turn a raw talking-head take into a tightly spaced sequence in a couple of keystrokes. title: Toasts are never drawn: FilmcraftApp::toast is written and never read
author: scottyallen
body:
`FilmcraftApp::toast` is written in three places and read in none, so no toast ever reaches the screen.

- `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:431` declares `pub toast: Option<(String, f64)>` (message, the time it was set).
- It is set at `lib.rs:1791` and `lib.rs:1794` (Refresh media), and at `lib.rs:1849`, which is where every `Event::Toast` the engine raises ends up.
- Nothing else in the workspace reads it. `grep -rn "toast" crates apps --include=*.rs` outside `crates/engine` and the tests returns only those lines plus `apps/filmcraft-web`, which keeps its own local `toast` variable and deliberately routes it through `app.status(t)` instead (`apps/filmcraft-web/src/lib.rs:195`).

So the 15 `Session::toast` / `Session::error_toast` calls in `crates/engine` reach the Events panel log and nothing visible. Among them are things worth seeing: a project upgraded to a new schema version, recovered unsaved changes, media files that are missing, Scene Edit Detection finding no cut points, a failed mask track, a render job that ended with errors.

Two ways to settle it, and I don't know which the maintainers want:

1. **Draw them.** A toast overlay in the main window, fading after a few seconds, red for `Event::Toast { error: true }`. That is a new piece of UI and wants a look at how Premiere does it.
2. **Drop the field and route to the status bar.** `Session::toast` messages become `app.status(...)`, which is what the web app already does by hand, and `toast` goes away. Less to build, less visible for an error.

Either way the field as it stands is a quiet hole: code that reports something to the user, and a user who never sees it.

Found while adding a failure report to #2147 (a dragged file promise the source never keeps): `error_toast` was the idiomatic call and produced nothing on screen, so that PR writes to the status bar as well.

title: Media pool never evicts anything: memory grows indefinitely while a project is open
author: scottyallen
body:
### Description
Nothing is ever evicted from the media pool, so FilmCraft's memory use grows without bound for as long as a project is open.

`MediaPool` (`crates/engine/src/media_pool.rs`) keeps one opened `MediaSource` per project item in a plain `HashMap`. There is no byte budget, no entry cap, no LRU and no idle timeout. An entry only leaves when something explicitly calls `remove(item)` (clip delete, relink, replace footage) or `clear()` (project open/close). Every other opened source stays resident indefinitely.

For video that is cheap: a source is a demuxer plus decoder state, not frames. For stills it is not. `StillSource::decode` (`crates/media/src/still.rs`) decodes the whole picture to RGBA8 up front and keeps it inside the source, so every still that has ever been rendered stays in memory at `width × height × 4` bytes until the project is closed, whether or not it is still on screen. A 24 MP photo is ~96 MB; a project with a few hundred stills holds tens of GB decoded, and scrolling through more of them only ever adds to that.

The two caches downstream of the pool are both bounded: the frame cache (`crates/ui-egui/src/frames.rs`, Settings ▸ Memory, 768 MB default) and the GPU plan cache (96 entries / 1 GB). The pool sits under both and holds the largest thing, uncapped.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Open a project (or an empty one).
2. Import a few hundred large JPEGs and put each on the timeline, or simply render each one once (the Media Browser's thumbnail view does this for you, see #2464).
3. Watch RSS climb by one decoded picture per still and never come back down. `perf.stats` ▸ open sources climbs with it.

Measured with 60 × 12 MP JPEGs through the Media Browser: RSS 483 MB → 3,339 MB, pool sources 5 → 61, unchanged after leaving the folder.

#2464 is the acute version of this (the thumbnail view fabricates a pool entry per file in the folder). That issue will get a narrow fix in the browser; this one is for the pool itself.

### Environment
- Fil…

title: Standalone audio files stay fully decoded in memory for as long as the project is open
author: scottyallen
body:
### Description
Like stills (#2469), the standalone audio sources decode the whole file when opened and keep every sample as a field. The media pool (`crates/engine/src/media_pool.rs`) holds every source until its item leaves the project and never evicts, so each audio file costs its full decoded size for the life of the project, whether or not it is on the timeline or has been played recently.

| Source | What it holds | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| `AudioFileSource` (`crates/codecs/src/audio.rs`): MP3, MP2, AAC, FLAC, AIFF | Every sample, planar `f32` | ~23 MB per minute of stereo 48 kHz; a 10-minute track is ~230 MB |
| `OggSource` (`crates/codecs/src/ogg.rs`), `Kind::Pcm` (Vorbis) | Same, plus the whole file's bytes | Same |

Already bounded, for comparison: WAV reads samples in place through its reader; every video container goes through the GOP caches, which share `FRAME_BUDGET`; stills get a shared budget in the fix for #2469.

`AudioFileSource`'s doc comment says "audio files are small next to video". That is true of the file on disk and not of the decoded PCM: a 5 MB MP3 becomes 230 MB.

Sibling issues: #2469 (stills), #2474 (animated GIF / APNG).

### Steps to Reproduce
1. New project. Import 50 MP3s of a few minutes each (a music library folder).
2. Drop each on the timeline once, or open each in the Source Monitor, so its source is created.
3. RSS grows by the decoded size of each track and never comes back down. `perf.stats` ▸ `decode` shows nothing for it: the audio is in no counter.

A podcast edit (two or three hours of MP3 or AAC across a handful of files) holds 3 to 4 GB of PCM the same way.

### Possible fix
Audio is read in ranges (`MediaSource::audio(start, frames, rate)`), so unlike a still the natural bound is not "re-decode the whole file on a miss":

- Decode on demand through a seek table (MP3 / AAC frame index, FLAC seektable or frame headers, Ogg page offsets), keeping a window of decoded samples around the last read, the way the GOP cache keep…

title: Animated GIF / APNG sources keep every decoded frame in memory for as long as the project is open
author: scottyallen
body:
### Description
`AnimatedSource` (`crates/media/src/animated.rs`) decodes every frame of an animated GIF or APNG when the file is opened and keeps them all as a field. The per-file limits (`MAX_FRAMES`, `MAX_DECODED_BYTES` = 1 GiB) bound one file; nothing bounds the total. The media pool (`crates/engine/src/media_pool.rs`) holds every source until its item leaves the project and never evicts, so each animated image costs its full decoded size for the life of the project, up to 1 GiB per file.

Sibling issues: #2469 (stills), #2473 (standalone audio). For comparison, video containers go through the GOP caches, which share `FRAME_BUDGET` and decode again on demand.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. New project. Import a folder of animated GIFs (reaction GIFs from a messaging app are typically 300 to 500 px, 50 to 200 frames: 20 to 100 MB decoded each; a 1080p screen-recording GIF of a few seconds is several hundred MB).
2. Show each one once (timeline, Source Monitor, or a Project panel thumbnail).
3. RSS grows by each file's decoded size and never comes back down; `perf.stats` ▸ `decode` has no counter for it.

### Possible fix
Same shape as the still fix for #2469: the source keeps its reader (or bytes when that is all the host gave it) and a frame index, and frames live in a shared byte-budgeted cache (`media::FrameCache`), decoded again from the file on a miss. GIF and APNG frames depend on the previous ones (disposal / blend), so a miss decodes from the start of the file or the nearest full-frame; the GOP cache has the same shape with sync samples.

### Environment
FilmCraft 0.9.0, all platforms.

title: Proposal: Scale PR review capacity with contributor guidelines and trusted reviewers
author: cshapiro
body:
## Summary

Could FilmCraft establish clear contribution and review guidelines, together with a path for reliable contributors to become trusted reviewers and, where appropriate, receive scoped merge permissions?

As contributions increase, review and merge capacity could become a bottleneck if too much work depends on a small number of maintainers. Clear expectations and a broader reviewer pool could help contributions move forward while preserving quality and maintainer oversight.

This is a process proposal rather than a claim about the exact number of active maintainers or current review times.

## Proposed approach

### 1. Document contribution and review expectations

Create or extend CONTRIBUTING.md and the PR template to explain:

- When contributors should discuss scope before starting work.
- How to keep PRs focused and independently reviewable.
- Required checks, relevant tests, reproduction steps, and validation evidence.
- Expectations for documenting user-visible changes, platform limitations, and AI-assisted work.
- What makes a PR ready for review and how to address review feedback.
- Which changes require specialist or maintainer review, such as architecture, security, dependencies, media correctness, and release infrastructure.

### 2. Establish a path to becoming a trusted reviewer

Define transparent criteria based on demonstrated project knowledge, reliable contributions, useful reviews, and sound judgment.

Contributors could begin with issue triage, reproduction, testing, and advisory code reviews before taking on responsibility for a defined area.

A lightweight reviewer roster could identify areas of expertise and availability, helping authors request appropriate reviews and maintainers distribute the workload. Participation should remain voluntary.

### 3. Delegate responsibility gradually

Trusted reviewers could verify behavior, inspect code, and recommend approval without immediately receiving merge permissions.

title: Feature (Beyond Premiere): Video De-Noise with motion compensation
author: danielbanariba
body:
Split out of #2401 at the triage request, so each effect can be tracked and fixed separately. The other two effects from that ticket are #2515 (Diffusion) and #2516 (VHS Look). This is the one I'm claiming.

## What it is

I'm moving a Premiere edit of live concert footage to Linux, and a video denoise that does not ghost on fast motion is the first thing it leans on that is missing here. This proposes it as a CPU video effect, **Video De-Noise**, and I'll implement it.

Today there is Noise, VR De-Noise (spatial only, VR layouts), the obsolete Median and the Lights & Glows set, but no general or temporal denoise.

Measured on that footage: a temporal filter without motion compensation (FFmpeg's hqdn3d, run only as an external reference) leaves a doubled hand and smeared guitar strings at the strength that removes the noise. A useful denoise needs motion compensation, or temporal weights that back off where frames differ.

## Proposal

| Id | Name | Default | Range | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `luma` | Luma Noise Level | 30 % | 0 to 100 % | Brightness noise (0 = off) |
| `chroma` | Chroma Noise Level | 50 % | 0 to 100 % | Colour noise |
| `temporal` | Temporal Radius | 1 | 0 to 2 frames | Neighbours used each side (0 = spatial only) |
| `compensate` | Compensate Motion | on | on / off | Align neighbours with optical flow first |
| `detail` | Preserve Detail | 50 % | 0 to 100 % | Fine texture kept |
| `show_noise` | Show Only Noise | off | on / off | As in VR De-Noise |

**Algorithm** (linear premultiplied `f32`, weights on display-encoded values):

1. **Motion:** dense Lucas-Kanade flow (Lucas and Kanade, "An Iterative Image Registration Technique with an Application to Stereo Vision", IJCAI 1981). `crates/render/src/flow.rs` already has it for Optical Flow (#780); I'd expose that solver inside the crate instead of writing a second one. #1243 would need the same.
2. **Temporal:** each neighbour is warped onto the current frame and weighted by how well it matc…

title: Feature (Beyond Premiere): Diffusion effect, a soft mist look around highlights
author: danielbanariba
body:
Split out of #2401 at the triage request, so each effect can be tracked and fixed separately. The other two effects from that ticket are #2514 (Video De-Noise, which I'm claiming) and #2516 (VHS Look). **This one is not claimed**: it is a proposal and stays open for anyone who wants to implement it.

## What it is

A mist look: light spreads, contrast drops and highlights bloom, without the overall brightening of a glow. It is the second of three effects that a Premiere edit of live concert footage, which I'm moving to Linux, leans on and that are missing here.

I am **not** proposing bloom: Wonder Glow already blurs thresholded highlights at three radii. Wonder Glow only adds light from thresholded highlights, so it cannot lower contrast around a source. Halation is #1175.

## Proposal

A new CPU video effect, **Diffusion**.

- **Parameters:** Strength 0 to 100 % (30 %), Size 1 to 400 px (40 px, times `px_scale`), Highlight Bias 0 to 100 % (60 %; 0 = even veil), Color (white).
- **Algorithm:** glare as a narrow core plus a broad halo (Spencer, Shirley, Zimmerman and Greenberg, "Physically-Based Glare Effects for Digital Images", SIGGRAPH 1995), built as Wonder Glow does with three Gaussians in linear light, then **mixed** instead of added: `out = lerp(img, veil, strength)`. The exact construction of the veil (how Highlight Bias weights it, how Color tints it) is left to the PR; the tests below pin the behaviour, not the formula.

## Acceptance tests

- Mean luminance is preserved at Strength 100 % with Highlight Bias 0 (this fails if the effect is written as an additive glow).
- Pixels next to a bright dot rise and the dot falls.
- `px_scale` 1 and 0.5 agree within a tolerance.
- Hostile parameters (NaN, infinite, negative, huge values; 1x1 and transparent images) neither panic nor return garbage.

## Related tickets

- storytold/effectcraft#966 (Halation and Diffusion effects for EffectCraft, open). Same look, different app: that request is for EffectCraft and doe…

title: Feature (Beyond Premiere): VHS Look, a clip-level analog tape effect
author: danielbanariba
body:
Split out of #2401 at the triage request, so each effect can be tracked and fixed separately. The other two effects from that ticket are #2514 (Video De-Noise, which I'm claiming) and #2515 (Diffusion). **This one is not claimed**: it is a proposal and stays open for anyone who wants to implement it.

## What it is

A persistent tape look: soft luma, smeared colour, line wobble, tape noise. It is the third of three effects that a Premiere edit of live concert footage, which I'm moving to Linux, leans on and that are missing here.

The VHS Damage transition exists (`vtransition.rs`), but it plays between two clips. There is no clip-level VHS effect.

## Proposal

A new CPU video effect, **VHS Look**.

- **Parameters:** Luma Bandwidth 0.5 to 5 MHz (3.0), Chroma Bandwidth 0.05 to 1.5 MHz (0.3), Chroma Shift -20 to 20 px (2), Line Jitter 0 to 10 px (1), Noise 0 to 100 % (20), Head Switching 0 to 30 lines (0), Dropouts 0 to 100 % (10), Seed.
- **Algorithm:** a per-scanline model: Y'CbCr (ITU-R BT.601), luma and chroma low-passed separately (VHS records chroma far narrower than luma, "color-under"), then jitter, noise, a head-switching band and dropouts.
- **Bandwidth units:** MHz become a cutoff across the frame through the NTSC active line (about 52.6 µs): 3 MHz is about 158 cycles per picture width, about 240 TVL on a 4:3 frame. That matches the public VHS figures (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VHS: 3 MHz luma, 240 TVL, 300 kHz chroma; the article cites Poynton, "Digital Video and HDTV Algorithms and Interfaces", 2003, for the bandwidths), and the look does not depend on resolution.
- **Noise:** seeded from the clip time as in #906 and #956, so preview and export agree.

## Acceptance tests

- On a red/black step, the chroma edge is wider than the luma edge.
- A grating below the luma cutoff passes and one above it is attenuated, at two resolutions.
- New frames get new noise; the same timestamp gives the same noise.

title: Feature Request: Add an Optional Magnetic Timeline Mode to Adobe Premiere Pro
author: vedantdahake
body:
**Category:** Feature Request / Idea  
**Product:** Adobe Premiere Pro  
**Feature Area:** Timeline Editing / Editing Workflow  
**Priority:** High — Workflow Efficiency and User Experience  
**Suggested Feature Name:** Magnetic Timeline Mode

## Summary

I would like to request the addition of an optional **Magnetic Timeline mode** in Adobe Premiere Pro, inspired by the magnetic editing workflow available in Final Cut Pro.

Premiere Pro is a powerful professional video editor with a flexible, track-based timeline. However, for editors who primarily create sequential content such as YouTube videos, documentaries, interviews, social media videos, and short films, managing gaps and manually maintaining the order of clips can introduce unnecessary steps.

A magnetic timeline mode would allow primary video clips to automatically connect to one another, close unwanted gaps, and move together intelligently when clips are inserted, removed, trimmed, or rearranged.

The goal is not to replace Premiere Pro's existing track-based timeline, but to provide an additional, optional editing workflow that users can enable whenever it suits their project.

## Problem Statement

In a conventional track-based editing workflow, removing a clip can leave an empty gap in the timeline unless the editor performs a ripple delete or another gap-closing operation. Inserting and rearranging clips may also require additional adjustments to maintain the intended sequence.

Premiere Pro already provides tools such as Ripple Delete and Ripple Edit, but editors must consciously use these operations and manage the interaction between multiple tracks. This can interrupt the editing process, particularly when making frequent cuts, removing pauses, rearranging dialogue, or assembling a fast-paced sequence.

For example, when editing a talking-head video, an editor may remove several pauses and unwanted sentences throughout the sequence. A magnetic workflow could automatically close the resulting gaps a…

title: Linux hybrid Intel+NVIDIA: default start panics with "Invalid surface" instead of falling back to the iGPU
author: CybeRxNinja
body:
## Summary

On a hybrid Intel + NVIDIA laptop (KDE Plasma 6 Wayland), FilmCraft 0.9.0's default graphics start selects the NVIDIA GPU and panics during `Surface::configure` with `Invalid surface`. The Intel iGPU renders the same window fine with no other changes. The app does not retry the other adapter, and once the failed start is recorded, the next launch forces software mode and exits because lavapipe (`vulkan-swrast`) is not installed.

## Environment

- Arch Linux, kernel 7.2.7-1-cachyos
- KDE Plasma 6.8.0, Wayland session
- Intel HD Graphics 5500 (Broadwell), Mesa 26.2.5 + vulkan-intel 26.2.5 (works)
- NVIDIA GeForce 920M (GK208M, Kepler), nvidia-470xx 470.256.02, Vulkan 1.2.175; Optimus/3D controller with no display outputs
- FilmCraft 0.9.0 AppImage, wgpu 30.0.1
- `vulkan-swrast` (lavapipe) not installed; `vulkaninfo` enumerates both GPUs correctly, `nvidia-smi` works

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start from a clean graphics state (`--graphics default` resets the recorded fallback):
   ```bash
   ./filmcraft-0.9.0-linux-x86_64.AppImage --graphics default
   ```
2. Observe the panic below.

## Actual

```
ERROR [main] wgpu::backend::wgpu_core: Handling wgpu errors as fatal by default

thread 'main' panicked at wgpu-30.0.1/src/backend/wgpu_core.rs:3981:18:
wgpu error: Validation Error

Caused by:
  In Surface::configure
    Invalid surface
```

Exit code 101, no window.

If the previous launch crashed, `~/.local/share/filmcraft/graphics-start.json` is left at `{"failures":0,"mode":"software"}`, so the next launch exits earlier with:

```
WGPU error: Adapter selection failed: no software graphics adapter (WARP, lavapipe, llvmpipe) among 3 adapters
```

## Verified matrix

| Setup | Result |
|---|---|
| default (all ICDs) | panic `Invalid surface` |
| NVIDIA Vulkan ICD only | panic `Invalid surface` |
| Intel Vulkan ICD only | **runs, window appears** |
| `WGPU_POWER_PREF=low` (all ICDs) | **runs, window appears** |
| `WGPU_ADAPTER_NAME=Intel` | ignored, still pan…

title: Web build: report the open document in the viewport title
author: robertcsakany
body:
The web build sends no `ViewportCommand::Title` naming the open document (eframe would log it as `Unhandled egui viewport command: Title(…)` on the web). WordCraft, GridCraft, PhotoCraft and VectorCraft do (`<document>[ •] — <App>`).

An embedding host (pi-agent-dashboard runs the web build in a sandboxed iframe and delivers the document as a synthetic drop) uses that title to confirm WHICH document the app opened and whether it has unsaved changes. Without it the host can only assume the drop worked after a delay; when a drop is refused, the app's default document is mistaken for the file (seen with CADCraft 0.8.0 and a `.dwg`: it showed `Drawing1`).

Ask: send `Title("<file name>[ •] — <App>")` on open, rename and dirty change, like WordCraft.

title: Failed graphics start persists software mode even when no software adapter exists (lavapipe), dead-ending later launches
author: CybeRxNinja
body:
## Summary

When a graphics start fails before the window paints, `graphics-start.json` is persisted with `mode: "software"` without checking that a software adapter (lavapipe / WARP / llvmpipe) is available. On systems without `vulkan-swrast`, every later launch exits before trying the working hardware adapter:

```
graphics mode software after earlier failed starts (...; `--graphics default` goes back)
WGPU error: Adapter selection failed: no software graphics adapter (WARP, lavapipe, llvmpipe) among 3 adapters
```

Only `--graphics default` recovers, and the error text doesn't mention it. On a hybrid Intel + NVIDIA machine this turns a one-off startup failure (#2553) into a persistent one.

## Environment

- Arch Linux, KDE Plasma 6.8 Wayland
- Intel HD Graphics 5500 + NVIDIA GeForce 920M (nvidia-470xx 470.256.02)
- FilmCraft 0.9.0 AppImage, wgpu 30.0.1
- `vulkan-swrast` (lavapipe) not installed; `vulkaninfo` enumerates the Intel and NVIDIA adapters normally

## Steps to reproduce (deterministic, no failing GPU required)

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.local/share/filmcraft
printf '{"failures":0,"mode":"software"}' > ~/.local/share/filmcraft/graphics-start.json
./filmcraft-0.9.0-linux-x86_64.AppImage
```

## Actual

```
ERROR [main] eframe::native::run: Exiting because of error: WGPU error: Adapter selection failed: no software graphics adapter (WARP, lavapipe, llvmpipe) among 3 adapters
ERROR [main] filmcraft: FilmCraft could not start its window: WGPU error: Adapter selection failed: no software graphics adapter (WARP, lavapipe, llvmpipe) among 3 adapters
```

Exit code 101, no window.

## Expected

- Only persist/enter software mode after verifying that a software adapter actually exists.
- If none is available, reset to the default mode (or surface an actionable message: "no software adapter; run with `--graphics default`").
- Do not let the fallback ladder dead-end when a working hardware adapter is present.

## Related

- #2553 — the failed start that creates this sta…

title: ### [Feature Request] Add support for third-party audio/video plugins (VST3 / OpenFX)
author: rogerhue
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently, FilmCraft does not support external third-party plugin formats (such as VST3 audio plugins, OpenFX video plugins, or host extensions). This limits advanced audio processing (like noise reduction or parametric EQ) and custom video effects/transitions directly within the timeline.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add native support or standard host architecture for:
1. **VST3 / AU Audio Plugins:** Allowing users to scan local VST3 directories and apply third-party audio processing to tracks and clips.
2. **OpenFX (OFX) Support:** Enabling industry-standard video effect plugins.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Using external tools like EffectCraft or pre-rendering audio/effects in third-party software before importing them back into FilmCraft.

**Additional context**
- **App Version:** FilmCraft v0.9.0

title: Feature request: publish to YouTube from Export (sign in once, like DaVinci Resolve)
author: Dorusto
body:
**Feature request:** connect a YouTube account and publish from the Export dialog, like DaVinci Resolve does (Preferences ▸ Internet Accounts ▸ sign in; Deliver ▸ "Upload directly to YouTube").

**What it needs, at minimum**
- Sign in with Google once (browser OAuth, installed-app flow), token kept in the user's settings.
- On export: title, description, privacy (private / unlisted / public), optionally thumbnail and subtitle files (.srt); upload with a progress bar and resume after a dropped connection.

**Why it has to live in the app**
Since July 2020, YouTube locks every video uploaded through the Data API from an *unaudited* Google Cloud project as private, and it cannot be made public until that project passes the YouTube API Services audit ([docs](https://developers.google.com/youtube/v3/docs/videos)). Every user creating their own project hits this wall. Resolve avoids it because Blackmagic's project is audited and users only sign in. The same applies to FilmCraft: one audited project for the app makes direct publishing work for everyone. (TikTok's Content Posting API has the same audit rule, if more platforms come later.)

**Searched before opening:** no existing issue or PR about YouTube upload/publishing (searched youtube, upload, publish, direct publish, social media export, vimeo). YouTube appears only as an export preset.

title: Media Sequence Timeline Playhead Is Extremely Laggy Even When Idle on Windows Version
author: XIILO
body:
Description:

The Media Sequence timeline playhead feels noticeably laggy and stuttery during normal interaction.

**Problem**
This is not just a playback issue.
Even when:
No playback is running
The sequence contains no footage
The timeline is empty
Simply clicking, dragging, scrubbing, or moving the playhead manually
the playhead still feels sluggish, stuttery, and lacks smooth responsiveness.

**Expected Behavior**
Playhead movement should be smooth and immediate.
Timeline interaction should feel responsive regardless of sequence complexity.
An empty timeline should have virtually no noticeable lag.

**Actual Behavior**
Dragging the playhead feels choppy.
The playhead appears to "jump" instead of moving fluidly.
There is visible UI lag even on empty sequences with no clips or effects.
The issue has persisted across multiple releases.

**Impact**
Timeline interaction is one of the most fundamental parts of video editing. The current playhead behavior makes editing feel less responsive and significantly affects the overall user experience, even before any media is added to the project.

**Additional Note**
This issue has been present for several versions already. Since it occurs even on completely empty timelines, it appears to be related to timeline rendering or UI responsiveness rather than media decoding or playback performance.

title: Nested audio source-channel picks select from a downmixed parent layout
author: nuclearspike
body:
Nested-sequence source-channel picks are applied after conversion to the parent track layout. For a nested sequence whose master output is 5.1 on a stereo parent track, selecting source index 4 (the fifth channel, a rear channel) should play that source; the current path downmixes first, so the selection no longer refers to the original 5.1 channel.

To reproduce, nest a 5.1 sequence whose six channels have distinct test tones in a stereo parent sequence. Select the nested audio clip on the parent timeline (for example, `timeline.select` with `{"clips":[<nested-audio-clip-id>]}`), then invoke `clip.audioChannels` with `{"channels":[4]}` and render the parent mix. The selected rear tone should play; current main instead selects from the mix after it has been downmixed to stereo. A synthetic regression uses constant values 0.1–0.6 and expects 0.5 on both output channels; unpatched main returns 0.6656853.

The linked repair in PR #1847 renders the nested sequence at its own rendered master width for valid consumed source-channel picks before applying selection and parent layout conversion. Empty lists and consumed invalid picks keep the parent-width path. Regression tests cover selected channels; all nine tested Mono/Stereo/5.1 child-master/parent layout pairs without picks match captured baseline samples within `1e-6`. This is the nested-render case split from #1845. PR #2483 addresses that report's channel-less command reset; the explicit-pick failure here is also distinct from ordinary six-channel media downmix in #1016.

title: FCPXML export: a text graphic is written as <asset-clip ref="">, so Final Cut rejects the whole file
author: Reyzick-code
body:
**Version:** FilmCraft 0.9.0 (same in 0.8.0), macOS on Apple Silicon, headless `filmcraft-cli`. Final Cut Pro 12.4.

**What happens:** a text graphic on the timeline is exported to FCPXML as `<asset-clip ref="" ...>`. An empty `ref` is not a valid IDREF, so the file fails the FCPXML 1.10 DTD and Final Cut Pro refuses to import it at all. Not just the title is lost: nothing comes in. The export report says the graphic "is written as a clip without media and is not read back on import", which sounds like only the title is affected.

**Expected:** the file stays valid and the rest of the timeline imports. Leaving the graphic out, with the report saying so, would already be enough.

**Repro:**
```sh
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc2=size=480x360:rate=30000/1001:duration=2 -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p src.mp4
filmcraft-cli --save-as r.fcproj exec file.newProject name=repro
filmcraft-cli --project r.fcproj --save import "$PWD/src.mp4"
filmcraft-cli --project r.fcproj --save exec file.newSequence '{"name":"seq","width":960,"height":720,"fps":29.97}'
filmcraft-cli --project r.fcproj --save exec timeline.place '{"item":1,"track":"V1","audioTrack":"A1","seconds":0,"insert":false}'
filmcraft-cli --project r.fcproj --save exec graphics.newText '{"text":"HELLO","seconds":1,"time":0}'
filmcraft-cli --project r.fcproj exec file.exportFcpxml path="$PWD/out.fcpxml"
# FCPXMLv1_10.dtd copied out of Final Cut Pro.app/Contents/Frameworks/Interchange.framework/Versions/A/Resources/
xmllint --noout --dtdvalid FCPXMLv1_10.dtd out.fcpxml
```
```
out.fcpxml:19: element asset-clip: validity error : Syntax of value for attribute ref of asset-clip is not valid
out.fcpxml:19: element asset-clip: validity error : IDREF attribute ref references an unknown ID ""
```

**Workaround:** delete that `<asset-clip ref="">` element from the exported file. Final Cut then imports the timeline.

title: FCPXML export: scale ignores the default fit conform and the anchor is measured from the sequence centre, so Final Cut shows clips 2x and off-centre
author: Reyzick-code
body:
**Version:** FilmCraft 0.9.0 (same in 0.8.0), macOS on Apple Silicon, headless `filmcraft-cli`. Final Cut Pro 12.4.

**What happens:** a 480×360 clip fitted to a 960×720 sequence (`clip.fitToFrame`, scale 200) is exported as

```xml
<adjust-transform position="0 0" scale="2 2" anchor="-33.33333333333333 25"/>
```

In Final Cut every clip comes in twice too big and pushed toward a corner. Two separate things:

- **Scale.** FCPXML's default spatial conform is fit (the import side of this is #2218), so Final Cut first fits the clip to the frame and then applies `2 2` on top of that. Adding `<adjust-conform type="none"/>` to the clip did not change it in Final Cut 12.4: the clip was still twice the size.
- **Anchor.** `-33.33 25` is the clip's centre (240, 180) measured from the sequence centre (480, 360) in FCPXML units (% of frame height, y up). FCPXML measures the anchor from the clip's own centre, so a centred anchor is `0 0`. A 1280×720 clip in the same sequence gets `22.22 0` for the same reason.

**Expected:** scale relative to the fitted size and a centred anchor written as `0 0`. Here that is `scale="1 1" anchor="0 0"`, with scale keyframes divided by the same fit factor (2 → 1, 2.9 → 1.45). I made those two changes by hand in a 27 s edit with about 30 clips, scale keyframes and a position push, and Final Cut then framed everything the way FilmCraft renders it.

**Repro:**
```sh
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc2=size=480x360:rate=30000/1001:duration=2 -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p src.mp4
filmcraft-cli --save-as r.fcproj exec file.newProject name=repro
filmcraft-cli --project r.fcproj --save import "$PWD/src.mp4"
filmcraft-cli --project r.fcproj --save exec file.newSequence '{"name":"seq","width":960,"height":720,"fps":29.97}'
filmcraft-cli --project r.fcproj --save exec timeline.place '{"item":1,"track":"V1","audioTrack":"A1","seconds":0,"insert":false}'
filmcraft-cli --project r.fcproj --save exec clip.fitToFrame '{"clips":[9]}'

title: Feature Request: Add distinct Numpad support for Timecode entry and Clip Nudging (Premiere Pro parity)
author: 2105kocha-blip
body:
Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
Currently, FilmCraft does not recognize the physical Numpad as a distinct input device. Numpad keys simply duplicate the top-row QWERTY numbers, and they do not appear as separate bindable keys in the Keyboard Shortcuts editor.

Because of this, it is impossible to recreate the professional editing workflow found in Premiere Pro, where the Numpad is used to type exact timecodes or frame offsets to move clips precisely on the timeline.

Describe the solution you'd like
Please implement native Numpad support as a distinct set of keys (e.g., distinguishing Numpad1 from the regular 1 key).

When a clip is selected on the Timeline, pressing a Numpad key should:

Trigger a numeric/timecode input overlay (or focus the timecode field).

Allow the user to type a value and press Enter to apply the movement.

Differentiate between Relative (using + or - sign first) and Absolute (typing just the digits) movements.

Examples of expected behavior:

Relative Move: If a clip is selected, pressing Numpad +, 1, 0, 0, Enter should move the clip forward by exactly 100 frames (or 1 second, depending on the sequence timecode). Pressing Numpad -, 5, 0, Enter should move it backward by 50 frames.

Absolute Move: Pressing Numpad 1, 1, 1, 1, Enter should place the clip's In-point at exactly 11 seconds and 11 frames on the timeline.

Timecode Format: The input overlay should support standard timecode formatting (HH:MM:SS:FF) or frame counts, depending on the user's current sequence settings.
